For the veiled people have been fearful in respect of their worldly accounts – this because the Lord loveth not that anyone should owe a debt to another: wherefore they take such extraordinary pains to avoid becoming so encumbered; heedless the while of their own soul, and of that for which they were created: of the eventuality that for one thousand two hundred and seventy years they should have been acting according to the precepts of the Qur’an, but that on the Day of Recompense and Judgment they should be marked out by the Pen of God with a circle as of no account. Thus it is that the people are devoid of spiritual understanding, for otherwise they would give all that is on earth in order that their sentence should be delivered in grace, not in justice: for in justice they will be tormented in the Fire until the Day of Resurrection; while in grace they will enjoy felicity in Paradise until the Day of Resurrection.

The Year Seven of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest is the Year of Judgment. Notwithstanding, should He so wish it, He would appoint the seventh month; or else the seventh week; or else but seven days. He doeth what He willeth, and ordaineth what he pleaseth. He is not to be asked concerning aught that He doeth, while all else are to be asked concerning all that their hands have wrought.

Gate Fifteen of the Second Unity: In explanation of the Book, and that it is true

The substance of this gate is that the intention of the “Book” is that which is revealed by the Point of Truth; for the Eternal Essence hath never been, nor ever shall be, subject to change or alteration. Nay, the book of the Point of the Bayan is the Book that guideth unto God, for none but God is capable of producing such a book.

The term applieth to everything of this description, ranging from a single letter at one extreme, to the end that hath no end at the other; for whatever is disseminated from the Point of Truth is referred to as a “Book;” while whatever “Book” He Whom God shall make manifest shall write in His own hand is a book that hath been written in the hand of God, inasmuch as it hath ever been, and ever shall be, related unto God.

For His Book is true: that is, the spirits attaching to the word “Truth” in the words He sendeth down, in whatever mode they may be – whether in that of Verses, which are the “limpid water” of Ridvan; or Prayers, which are its “unaltered milk;” or Commentaries on the Verses, which are its crimson “wine;” or Responses and Commentaries on the Prayers, which are its “refined honey” – are in the Book of God. The Persian Modes are precisely identical to those of the Verses, for all flow out from the Sea of Truth: and should someone look into the Persian Words with the eye of his heart, he would behold the selfsame eloquence of the Verses, and would be certain that none but God hath been, or is, capable of utterance of this description.

Yet how many are those who confessed the Book to be true, but remained shut out as by a veil from Him by Whom the truth of Truth itself is established! And how oft is it the case that the Point of Truth, Whose Book is the Book of God – nay, Whose Book is more precious than All Things; nay, one letter of Whose Book is more precious than All Things – becometh, on account of the contumacy of the people, afraid of them, so that He is loath to send unto them His Book, whereby they may be delivered from the Fire, and gain admittance into Paradise! And how oft, out of the sublimity of His grace and mercy, doth He still dispatch His Book; yet the one unto whom it is dispatched perceiveth not its nature: nay, the Pen is ashamed to mention his response! Yet night and day he had recited “O my God, give me my book in my right hand!” Now, however, that the Lord hath given him it, he taketh it not: nay, he would, if he were able, inflict upon the bearer, who is but a messenger on His behalf, that which the Pen is ashamed to recount.

Yet the book is the Book of his God, and the messenger His messenger; while out of the sublimity of grace and bounty He hath revealed it for him in such a manner that he may be certain that it is the Book of God, and none but He is able to produce its like. For the religion of all is today vindicated by the Verses of the Qur’an: and whatsoever the Tree of Truth hath sent unto all is in the mode of its Verses; yet none have adverted to the matter. Notwithstanding, all have confessed, and still do, that the Book is true.

With each successive manifestation of the Tree of Truth, the believers in Him and His Book aforetime are tested by Him and His Book in their latter manifestations in such wise that none remaineth save the true believer; while he is rarer than the philosopher’s stone. Thus, for example, had those who believed in Jesus, the Son of Mary, and His Book, recognized that the manifestation of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – was identically that of Jesus in a nobler guise in the after life, and that His Book was the selfsame Evangel in a nobler guise, not one of the Christians would have apostatized his faith, and all would have believed in the Apostle of God, and acknowledged the truth of His Book.

In like manner, were the believers in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and His Book to be certain that the manifestation of the Qa’im – peace be upon Him – is the selfsame manifestation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – in a nobler guise in the after life, while this Book, the Bayan, is that identical Furqan, which hath been sent down in a nobler guise in the after life, not one of the believers in the Qur’an would have abandoned his faith, and, swifter than the twinkling of an eye, would have believed, and acknowledged the truth of the Bayan.

The fact, however, that they are uncertain in this respect is rejected in the sight of God. Nay, that whereby certitude itself is constituted such hath been afforded them: for were they to reflect upon the proof whereby the religion of Islam hath been established, they would behold that identical proof in a nobler guise. The mere fact, then, that they acknowledge not the truth, and are uncertain thereof, is a sign that their very natures are of the Tree of Negation, and revert thereunto; and that their faiths, and the works they have wrought in the religion of Islam, are of a temporary, not permanent, nature, and shall not benefit them to the extent of a grain of mustard seed.

If the works of the Letters of the Book of Alif (Evangel) today benefit them, then their works too shall benefit them, even should they adhere to that which hath been sent down by God without the alteration of a single letter. Most of the mujtahids and muftis, indeed, have applied this same principle to themselves, regarding it as impermissible to adhere to the word of a deceased person. Notwithstanding, the truth of every question is evident in the sight of God, and reverteth unto the Tree of the Bayan. Whatever decree hath been revealed from that Source – the same informeth all the understandings of the mujtahids and muftis.

Whosoever seeth in this decree naught else but God hath been, and is, correct in his perception: and even should differences arise, since it reverteth unto God it is accepted. Notwithstanding, there hath not been, nor is there, any difference in aught that hath been sent down in the Bayan on the part of God: for each decree in its own context is true: while differences only arise when it is applied in particular cases. Yet even here, if differences arise, they do so only as the particular circumstances in each case – the multitudinous different places, hours, conjunctions and standards – themselves differ. Ever at all times hath God instituted a novel way, a new creation and a fresh decree: notwithstanding, all that hath been revealed from the Point of Truth until this day hath been, and is, from God. Yet to outward appearance in each religious law one may say that innumerable differences exist among its followers, even while it is indubitably established that there is no difference in aught that cometh from God.

As far as the eye can see the mystery of this subtle matter is apparent: for the likeness of the decrees of God is that of the creation of men’s inner natures: ever are they in a state of renewal and inception, and in respect of the object of His Command, swifter than the twinkling of an eye a new creation and a novel state are made apparent. Howbeit in the eyes of His creatures this process is from Revelation to Revelation: for at the time of Concealment the matter reverteth unto that which had been revealed at the time of Revelation. Notwithstanding, the Hidden Truth sustaineth All Things at the time of His Concealment, albeit He doth so by means of that whereby He had sustained them at the time of His Revelation; for otherwise, none could be certain of His intention, save Him whom God willed. He, verily, is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.

Gate Sixteen of the Second Unity: Explaining that Paradise is true

The substance of this gate is that until today no one, excepting only the Manifestations Whom the Lord hath assigned unto Himself, hath understood either “Paradise” or the “Fire,” and that which is connected to the term “Paradise,” in this world, which is at once the origin and the final destination of all the worlds – all of which are comprehended in the station of the Throne of Truth, through Whose effulgence the first Divine Effulgence is vouchsafed. Even as is mentioned in the Prayer of ’Arafih: “O Thou who hast established Thyself in Thy mercy upon the Throne, whereupon the Throne became a mystery within itself, even as the worlds became a mystery within Thy Throne.”

In the Dispensation of the Qur’an, the manifestation of Mercifulness is, in the eyes of the people of the Bayan, restricted in the primary sense to the Commander of the Faithful: for the origin of whatsoever there is in all the worlds was from him, even as their return is likewise unto him. For example, from the Day of Adam until today, in each successive revelation of the Manifestation of Truth the opening of the Gates in Truth and in other than truth hath been effected through the first to believe in Him, until the essence of all Truth hath culminated in this Revelation, while the essence of other than truth likewise hath been realized through this Revelation.

Thus it is that were someone to look with the very essence of discerning vision, he would observe that all the worlds originate in the station of the Purpose, which is begotten by the Will, while this Latter subsisteth by Itself, and encompasseth all the worlds in virtue of Its rank in the world of creation: for anyone who is possessed of any rank in this Dispensation of the Bayan confesseth the exaltation of Its rank in his own soul: inasmuch as the world of the souls conformeth unto the world of the horizons. For example, when, in the Revelation of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – it became apparent in the world of the horizons that He was the First of Creation, in the world of the souls too all the believers in Him became assured that He had ever been, and ever would be, the First of Creation.

Now that this matter hath been indubitably established, let no one have any doubt that in the knowledge of God there hath not been, nor is there, a greater Paradise than the manifestation of God in the Point of the Will; whence from Revelation to Revelation the Paradise of the Former Revelation is in the Latter, until all the Revelations culminated in the Point of the Qur’an. From the inception of His Prophetic Mission, there was in the knowledge of God no greater Paradise than that peerless Soul, in that Revelation, for such is the case in the world of the souls. In this day, no one, betwixt himself and God, knoweth one greater, after the Lord, than His Apostle; and the sign thereof in their souls was not realized save through the appearance of that Primal Soul.

Thereafter, there is in the knowledge of God no greater Paradise than the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – even as in the realm of the souls no one, after the Apostle of God, looketh but to Him. In like manner, stage by stage, the ranks of the Gates of Paradise multiply, until the process culminateth in the Letters of the Vahid. For example, upon the appearance of the Fifth Paradise, no Paradise, after those precedent to him, was, at the end of His Life, greater then he: at which time he was alone in the land of Taff (Karbila), while the denizens of Paradise at that time were ’Ali Ibn Al-Husayn, and the captives. In like manner do thou regard all the Paradises, until they culminate in the Letter “Mim,” thereafter returning unto the Point.

From the time of the appearance of this Cause, the first moment thereof, without the lapse of so much as the ninth of the ninth of a minute, or the smallest fraction of time that can be computed, marked the beginning of the appearance of the Paradise of the Point of the Furqan in His after life, which is that of the Point of the Bayan in His present life. At that time, there was in the knowledge of God no greater Paradise than this: and even until the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, there shall be no greater Paradise than this. Howbeit, at the time of His appearance, the Former Paradise of the Point of the Bayan shall be converted into His Latter Paradise.

After this Paradise, the Paradises of the Letters of the Living, who are the souls who believed before all others, are the greatest of Paradises: which Paradises culminate, at the end of the Revelation, with the Paradise of the Letter “Sin.” It is not that with the appearance of each new Paradise, the previous Paradise doth not remain in his own place. For example, at the time of the appearance of the Paradise of “Sin,” the Paradise of “Ba’” is established upon His Throne. Such too is the case with all the Letters.

The Lord hath appointed for each Paradise, in the sense of the appearance of the Will by Its own Self, Nineteen Gates: for the circumstance that in this Revelation such a decree hath been exalted is a sign that on each and every appearance of the Will the same is true. Even as in the Qur’an, all revert unto the Gates; and the Gates unto the Holy Family; and the Holy Family unto the Apostle of God; and the Apostle of God unto the Lord, exalted and glorified be He. Thus it is that the Fourth Name is sustained through God by the Third Name; and the Third Name by the Second Name; and the Second Name by the First Name, which is the Name itself.

The person who first entered within this Paradise was the Holy Spirit, who before all other spirits attained the meeting with God, and confessed His Unity: inasmuch as no quintessence of pleasure in existence can be conceived of more precious and delightful than to confess the Unity of God, and to glorify and sanctify Him. Just as, if a person attain in this world unto the utmost happiness that could befall him, if it be in the way of Truth, his utmost delight is to yield thanks to God for the bounty that He hath bestowed upon him. For example, if the Lord cause a servant to attain unto the rank of Gate, Imam, or Prophet, the most delightful fruit of which he can partake is to yield thanks to God, saying, “Thanks be to God, Who hath caused me to attain unto this bounty.” So too in respect of material matters: for whatever servant the Lord place upon the throne of sovereignty, he can experience no higher pleasure than when he looketh unto his God, and saith, “Thanks be to Him for having honoured me with this bestowal.”

Thus it is that all pleasures revert unto the Second Pillar, which is the station of Thanks. Just as the inner natures revert unto that most sacred station, so too words, in their own distinctive manner, revert thereto. It is for this reason that in the eyes of those endued with understanding, the fruit of the last is already apparent in the first: for the one who, after the appearance of God’s bounties, yieldeth such thanks, received permission to do so from the Source of Glory. Thus it is that the first spirit, at the time of entering into the first Paradise, hath arrived at the fullest measure possible in the contingent world of every gracious bestowal: for as was explained, the fruit of all reverteth unto the Word, or formula, expressing thanks to God, the bearer of whose spirit is that soul; while whatsoever beatific manifestations branch out therefrom branch out from him, ranging from the essence of understanding at one extreme to material matters at the other.

Even the wearing of silken garments is through him: and whatsoever delight is enjoyed in Paradise is enjoyed through him. He, however, taketh delight in naught but his own Revealer, Who occupieth the station of the Point; while this latter is the “Circular Kaf” which hath ever moved, and ever shall move, about Its own Self, and hath neither beginning nor end, neither final goal nor ultimate destination.

For indeed, as is apparent unto whoever entered into the Paradise of the Furqan, whatsoever bounty he witnesseth is from the heaven of the generosity of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: to the degree even that if, for example, someone were to inherit a ruby, this would be due to naught but the bestowal of that Primal Reality Who decreed in this wise: for had He decreed otherwise – ordaining that another than the present heir should inherit the ruby – who would be able to ask why or wherefore? Thus it is that whatsoever all beings possess, from the point of their coming into existence even unto the utmost limit of their ascent, is due to His bestowal, which is none other but the bestowal of God.

No thing possesseth any substance, in respect of which it may be termed a “thing,” save in virtue of His grace and bounty. For example, if in this Paradise someone weareth silk, this is due solely to His bestowal, naught else, inasmuch as previously, although able to wear silk, he could not do so. Thus it is that were anyone to open the eye of his heart, he would see the whole of existence as naught but a scattering from the hand of His bounty.

All who entered into the Paradise of the Furqan are sheltered beneath the shadow of the First Gate, Who is the Apostle of God; while the other Gates of Paradise are held within the grasp of this Gate. Nay, He hath unlocked these through His bounty. For example, should anyone ascend with respect to the Last Letter to the furthest possible extent, and material benefits accrue to him to a degree that naught more splendid could be conceived of in this world, this is due to naught but the permission of Him Who said, “This is one of the Gates of Paradise, and of my guidance.” Even as that which hath been made outwardly manifest in the Paradise of the tomb of the Eighth Imam is due to naught but the announcement of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him, “He is mine Eighth Viceregent.” Although at present, naught of this nature is to be witnessed at his tomb, yet all such manifestations have never been, nor ever shall be, but in the grasp of His bounty, and the hand of His power.

Beneath the shadow of each of the Gates of Paradise there have been, and are, innumerable subordinate Gates: even as each soul who entereth into the allegiance of one of the Gates of Paradise is in himself a Paradise, for his sake, in his own degree. To an illimitable extent the operation of this mystery is evident and effective.

Whatsoever delight can today be conceived of is in this Paradise; while from the Former Paradise all delight hath been cut off: even as at the time of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – all delight was cut off from the Paradise of the Evangel. For the whole of Paradise consisteth in confessing the Unity of God; in knowing Him, and winning His good pleasure; and in obeying the Manifestations of His Cause: wherefore, when a person is cut off therefrom, what Paradise can there be? Even were he to enjoy throughout his whole life the utmost possible delight, he would in the end return unto the fire of extinction.

If in the inner realities of the Letters of the Evangel there be a sign of the Truth, which is the culmination of delight, yet this sign – albeit it existed in the Revelation of Jesus – hath today been removed; and it is only under the misapprehension of its continuance that he hath tarried in his Paradise until now. For were all the Letters of the Evangel to know with certainty that the manifestation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – is the selfsame manifestation of Jesus in a nobler guise, not one of them would remain in his Evangel, or take delight in that Paradise.

Such too is the case following the completion of the Dispensation of the Furqan: if today any of its followers conceive himself to have experienced any sensation of delight, this hath no reality: for if betwixt himself and God he performeth an act “for God,” and conceiveth himself to have taken any delight therein, yet in the sight of God he hath performed it for other than Him. Under the same misapprehension that hath caused the Letters of the Evangel to tarry in their Paradise, these too have tarried in theirs. For the Mirror of God hath dawned in another Paradise, whence all delight is cut off, save from him who recognizeth God alone, and believeth in Him; and recognizeth His Proof, and believeth in Him; and recognizeth His Book, and believeth therein; and recognizeth that which hath been sent down in His Book, and believeth therein.

In like manner, the denizens of this Paradise shall take delight therein up to the beginning of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest. I swear by the Divine Essence that there shall be for them at the time of His appearance no greater Paradise than to believe in Him, and to obey Him; while all delight shall be cut off from the people of the Bayan. Blessed is he who entereth beneath His shadow, and taketh delight in His remembrance, for he shall abide as long as He Himself abideth, even unto the following Revelation. Then, if he believe in Him, and take delight in His remembrance, he shall have attained the Revelation after that following; neither shall there be any end or limit to this process. If, however, he remain in any Revelation, both his faith and delight shall be cut off from him at the time of the following Revelation.

I counsel all the people of the Bayan that if, at the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, ye all succeed in attaining that Most Mighty Paradise and Most Great Meeting, then blessed are ye; then blessed are ye; then blessed are ye! Otherwise, if, from the time of the Name of God “Aghyath,” ye hear that One hath been made manifest with the same Verses as before, do ye all enter therein. Yet if He have not appeared by then, and the time wear on till the Name of God “Mustaghath;” whereupon ye hear that a Point hath appeared, but ye are not all assured that it is He – have then mercy upon your own souls, and, if ye have not all entered beneath the shadow of that Manifest Point, do ye all, with your whole being, seek shelter therein.

Should ye hear that a Soul hath been made manifest having the ability to reveal Verses, and that the learned of that age have confessed His truth – not those who are merely famed for learning, but rather those who look with scrutinizing gaze (even as was the case in this age, when the former were shut out as by a veil, whereas those who looked with scrutinizing gaze and penetrating vision, although arrayed in the raiment of poverty and wretchedness, were the first to enter into Paradise, whence they attired themselves in silk; while the former have remained until now in their previous state) – should ye hear of such a Soul, then hesitate not, but enter ye all beneath the shelter of His shadows: for He is the First and the Last; and He is the Manifest and the Hidden. Should ye, however, not hear such tidings, do ye resort to ardent prayer and supplication, that haply the grace of God may not be cut off from you up to “Mustaghath.”

Should ye, ere “Mustaghath,” hear that He Who is my Beloved and your Beloved, my King and your King, hath been made manifest, then tarry not even for so long as it taketh to draw breath, but all of you, without exception, enter beneath the shadow of God, nor ask why or wherefore, for this is among my weightiest commandments unto you, in order that I may deliver you from the fire of your remoteness, through having granted you this permission. O people of the Bayan, do ye all give thanks: for should anyone, after two thousand and one years, tarry for the space even of a single breath, unquestionably he is not in the religion of the Bayan, and is within the Fire; unless the Manifestation of God appear not, in which case ye are all charged to resort to ardent prayer and supplication.

I wish not that ye should tarry like the Jews after the advent of Jesus – peace be upon Him; or that, like the Christians, Muhammad should arrive, and ye should tarry; or that, like the people of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – the Qa’im of the House of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – should appear, and ye should tarry. Were my heart to consent that any of those in the Bayan should thus tarry, I would declare,

“The Point of the Bayan hath come in His Latter Manifestation, and ye, verily, continue as ye were before!”

I swear by Him Whom God shall make manifest that in the knowledge of God there hath not been, nor is there, a more grievous matter: for should He appear, and anyone tarry in the Bayan, the whole vengeance of the Bayan shall light upon him in double measure, for today the vengeance of the Furqan upon those who entered not into the Bayan is doubled, even as was the vengeance of the Evangel upon those who had entered not into the Qur’an, while the vengeance of the Qur’an too was doubled in their case.

Should any such soul exist, he hath never been within the fold of the Bayan, nor ever entered beneath the shadow of the Tree of the Possessor of the Seven Letters; even as, if any of the Letters of the Qur’an should thus tarry, through not entering beneath the shadow of the Bayan, he had never entered within the fold of the Qur’an, nor ever sheltered beneath the shadow of the Tree of Muhammad: for otherwise he would not have held aloof from His manifestation in nobler guise in His after life. The same too may be said of the Evangel, for if a soul had truly believed in Jesus, he must needs have believed in Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: whence the mere fact that he hath not done so is an indication that he had never believed in the Evangel, or in Jesus.

In like manner, if anyone today looketh at the Traditions concerning the trial and temptation of the believers, he will observe what pains the supporters of the Truth have taken to insure the deliverance of this people on the Day of Revelation: even as those writers who look with scrutinizing gaze have mentioned in their works that the appearance of His Holiness – peace be upon Him – is none other but the appearance of that “Truth” concerning which, as recorded in the Tradition of Kumayl, the Commander of the Faithful was once questioned. Howbeit, God guideth whomsoever He willeth, and causeth to enter into Paradise whomsoever He desireth.

Such is the reality of Paradise in this present life; while after death, none but God is apprised thereof: therein is what eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, nor human heart conceived. Therein hath God created everything whereof everyone beseecheth, through His bounty, to receive a portion. Were the seas of the heavens to be converted into ink, and all things into pens, and all who are endowed with spirit into scribes, assuredly they would be unable to apprehend aught of what is contained in the Paradise after death. The axis around which this Paradise revolveth is that same Paradise which, as mentioned, existeth during the lifetime of the servant. If, during this present life, he have entered into the Paradise of the Revelation of God, he shall after his passing likewise enter into the Paradise of the life to come.

Otherwise, he shall enter into the Fire at the time when he is caused to yield up his soul. I seek refuge in God from such a fate! I have not seen in this Paradise aught else but God; nor within it aught else but Him; nor before it aught else but Him; nor after it aught else but Him; nor above it aught else but Him; nor below it aught else but Him. His are the creation and the Command aforetime and hereafter. No God is there but Him, the Living, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.

How oft it chanceth that a soul is in one Revelation among the most exalted ranks of the denizens of Paradise, while at the time of the following Revelation, he descendeth to the lowest ranks of the people of the Fire! Seek ye refuge in God, and lay fast hold upon the cord of the Point of the Bayan, both in His Former and in His Latter Manifestation: for He needeth not that anyone should believe in Him, or enter into His Paradise. Nay all, if they enter not, shall but go into the Fire; otherwise, if they enter into Paradise, they shall do so to their own behoof. Wherefore it is better to guide one soul than to possess all that is on earth, for as long as that guided soul is under the shadow of the Tree of Divine Unity, he and the one who hath guided him will both be recipients of God’s tender mercy, whereas possession of earthly things will cease at the time of death.

The path to guidance is one of love and compassion, not of force and coercion. This hath been God’s method in the past, and shall continue to be in the future! He causeth him whom He pleaseth to enter the shadow of His Mercy. Verily, He is the Supreme Protector, the All-Generous.

There is no paradise more wondrous for any soul than to be exposed to God’s Manifestation in His Day, to hear His verses and believe in them, to attain His presence, which is naught but the presence of God, to sail upon the sea of the heavenly kingdom of His good-pleasure, and to partake of the choice fruits of the paradise of His divine Oneness. Yet, praise be to God that all in this day are shut out as by a veil from this Paradise, and take delight in that which, at the time when they are caused to expire, shall be cut off from them, and cause them to enter into the Fire; and withal that they are shut out as by a veil from that for the sake whereof they were created!

Would, indeed, that they were but shut out as by a veil therefrom, and not opposed thereto! And would that they were but opposed thereto, and had not inflicted upon the Tree of Truth that which, in relation to Him, beseemeth not His station! All believe through Him, yet have confined Him to a mountain; and all are honoured through Him, yet have consigned Him to isolation. Neither hath there been, nor is there, a fiercer fire for the authors of this wrong than the wrong itself: even as for the believers there hath never been, nor is there, a greater Paradise than belief itself.

There is no God but God. He is the God of Paradise, and its Lord, its Possessor, its King, and its Sovereign. All that are therein abide through His Command; while He, verily, is independent of all that live and move therein. All that are therein, however, take delight in meeting Him at the time of His Manifestation; and thereafter in meeting Him at the time of His Concealment, in a manner unperceived by all. Verily, all the denizens thereof give glory to Him by thanking Him at every moment, and before each moment, and after each moment; and confess the Unity of God, their Lord, by remembering Him in every matter, and before each matter, and after each matter.

No soul shall enter therein but that it shall, in truth, proclaim on the part of its Lord: “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me, the Almighty, the Best-Beloved!” and “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting!” and “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me, assuredly a Regal Lord!” and “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me, assuredly an Exalted Truth!” and “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me, the Lord of All Things, the Lord of the Exalted Throne!”

All Things revert unto the human temple, whether male or female. If the soul in question dwell in Paradise, all that is in his or her possession likewise is a part of Paradise, even should it be a thing that is not peerless in its kind: for whatsoever emanateth from the Will is in the likeness of its own self, at its own level, so that when it is stripped of its limitations, naught remaineth in the highest form thereof – which is that pertaining to the heart – save the human temple. It is for this reason that All Things beseech of the Lord that they might rest in the shadow of that which is related unto the believer, not other than he: for the Paradise of each thing is to be related unto God: and that which is related unto the believer is related unto God. If, however, it reverteth unto other than a believing soul, then all is in the Fire, and a manifestation thereof, although the thing concerned be at its own level peerless in its kind.

For example, this room, which hath no doors, or any recognizable dimensions, is today the loftiest chamber of Ridvan, inasmuch as the Tree of Truth resideth therein. Yea, methinks the very atoms thereof all now raise the cry “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me, the Lord of All Things!” – a cry in virtue whereof they vaunt themselves over all other rooms, even should these be apartments adorned with mirrors and ornamented with gold. If, however, the Tree of Truth were to reside in such apartments, then the atoms of the mirrors thereof would raise the selfsame cry: even as the atoms of the mirrors of the most exalted chamber of the ’Imarat-i-Sadri, wherein, during the period of my sojourn in the Land of Sad, I resided, raised such a cry, and do so to this day.

Naught is possessed of any consequence except it revert unto that soul. Thus, wherever the denizens of Paradise be seated, the spots in question are potentially capable of the utmost possible exaltation, as indeed is witnessed by those who look with the eye of truth. For example, no spot was more abased on the day of the martyrdom of the Fifth Word than the site of this event: yet, since it was a part of Paradise, it displayed beneath its shadow the utmost possible exaltation, so that, even then, had one looked with a discerning eye, he would have seen that it was fitting for its walls to be constructed out of ruby, not gold; and if such hath not appeared, it is on account of the weakness of the people, not the incapacity of that spot, for it was endowed with such potential.

By the same token, although there was on that day no more exalted spot than that whereon the opposing tree was seated, the discerning people of that age beheld already its evanescence, whence even then they seemed to see it reduced to naught: and indeed there is today no trace or sign either of the one who reposed upon that spot, or of the place itself. In such wise God bringeth Negation to extinction, and raiseth Affirmation unto the very heights, through His Command. He, verily, is powerful over All Things.

Similarly, if the situations be reversed, so that the Tree of Truth be seated upon the most exalted spot on earth, there is no doubt that it would from everlasting unto everlasting ascend upwards in its state of exaltation; and so likewise in the shade: even if the place in question be the most abased spot on earth, it would continue to descend downwards in its state of abasement: inasmuch as All Things revert unto the human soul; while it reverteth unto God in Paradise, if it had believed in Him Whom God shall make manifest; and unto other than the truth in the Fire, if it had been shut out as by a veil.

Whoso followeth My Command at the time of “Mustaghath” shall enter into Paradise, as irrevocably ordained by of God. He, verily, is powerful over All Things.

Gate Seventeen of the Second Unity: Explaining that the Fire is true

The substance of this gate is that the Fire hath ever had, and ever shall have, innumerable and never-ending manifestations. The quintessential reality thereof is lack of recognition of God, which in each Dispensation is evidenced through lack of recognition of the One Who is the Bearer of the Divine Revelation in the Dispensation itself, Who calleth unto all in whatever tongue is spoken by the people among whom He is raised up: “There is no God but God, truly, truly;” “There is no God but God, truly, truly, truly;” “There is no God but God, truly, truly, truly, truly;” and “There is no God but God, truly, truly, truly, truly, truly.” For in All Things the essence of that which God loveth not reverteth unto Negation, while the essence of that which God loveth reverteth unto Affirmation; neither of which can be made apparent save through that which, in each Revelation, the Point of Truth loveth not, and that which He loveth.

This essence, alike in the Qur’an and the Bayan, is the heart of the first person whose heart, when he heard that the Tree of Truth had been made manifest, was consumed by the fire of hesitation or repudiation, although this heart had erstwhile been in Paradise; for he had been wont to say: “There is no God but God;” “Muhammad is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him;” “’Ali and the Imams are the Proofs of God;” and “The Gates of Guidance – these, truly, are the witnesses of God;” and had regarded all that God had sent down in the Furqan as true. Yet in consequence of blindness, heedlessness, halting, repudiation, or denial, all the true signs that had formerly been within him – of the recognition of God, and of the recognition of the Prophet, the Imams and the Gates, and the acknowledgment of all that is true in Islam on the part of God – were rendered vain: for all these had sprung from the Tree of Truth; and this identical Tree hath been made manifest, and these fruits were from Him aforetime.

From the mere fact, therefore, that He hath been made manifest and no one hath accepted Him, it would seem that no one had accepted Him even in His Former Manifestation: for this present manifestation is His manifestation in His after life, and is more powerful than His manifestation in His former existence.

Thus it is that the most exalted dwellers of the former Paradise become dwellers of the lowest depths of the Fire. For the first root of the Fire was fain, in his own particular station, to detach himself from the world and devote himself entirely unto the Lord: nay, one more detached than he hath not been heard of till this day; and under the delusion that a certain soul was possessed of the truth, he committed unto him all his affairs. Notwithstanding, that first “Second” likewise was formerly the “First;” yet since in reality he was sunk fast in the earth of his own remoteness, all his piety availeth him naught, for had he been sincere in his aspirations, he would not have hesitated on the appearance of Him by Whom the truth of Truth itself is established; nor, in virtue of his station, been shut out as by a veil from attaining the meeting with God.

At the beginning of the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, whatsoever there was of good in the knowledge of God was created by Him through the first to turn unto Him, and whatsoever there was of other than good was created by Him through the first to turn away from Him; for, from the day of the creation of All Things up to the beginning of the Revelation, the quintessential reality of all Paradise is embodied in the First Gate, while the quintessential reality of all Fire is embodied in the first to turn away. The Lord wished to cause him to turn towards Him; lavished upon him the utmost favour; and sent numerous Tablets and peerless emissaries into his presence; but he allowed himself to be shut out as by a veil by that which profiteth him not, and donned the robe of the first to enter into the Fire.

For there is not now in the knowledge of God a greater Paradise than the Point of the “Ba’” in the Bayan; nor is there beneath the sod a remoter fire than the shade of this Point: inasmuch as all things that revert unto the latter, of each kind, are things that have entered within the Fire; while all things that revert unto the former, of each kind, are things that have entered into Paradise. Even as aforetime, whatsoever reverteth unto the Apostle of God had entered into Paradise; while whatsoever reverteth unto the first not to believe in Him had reverted unto the Fire.

The manifestations of this Fire are limitless: but the totality of its Gates are stated to be nineteen; otherwise none knoweth their number but God. For whoever is taken from a Gate of the Fire is a gate of the Fire in his own right; while whatever gate is taken from the Gates of Paradise is a gate of Paradise in his own right; notwithstanding that all who are in the Fire revert unto the first origin thereof; while all who are in the Light revert unto the first origin thereof. Both of them worship God; bow down before Him; praise Him, extol Him, and confess His Unity; but with the difference that the latter confesseth the Unity of God in virtue of His manifestation in the after life, while the former doth so in virtue of His manifestation in the earthly life, which was none other but the beginning of this present Revelation, and the after life of that preceding it.

Thus it is that the former is invalidated, while the latter is confirmed; the former turneth into fire, while the latter turneth into light; the former fadeth into nothingness, while the latter is established; the former is ennobled, while the latter is abased; the former is enriched, while the latter is impoverished – until it reacheth the pass that no further mention of him remaineth, even within his own self. For otherwise both today confess, “There is no God but God:” but those who say this in the Bayan, say it in a manner that God loveth; while those who say it in the Furqan, say it in a manner that God loveth not. So too aforetime, whoever was in the Book of Alif (Evangel) necessarily confessed the Unity of God: but at the time of the revelation of the Qaf (Qur’an), the Lord of the world – exalted and glorified be He – wished to have His Unity confessed through the confession of Muhammad, the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and not through the confession of Jesus.

Whoso followeth the wish of God, the spirit of the angels shall dwell permanently within him: unless God had deposited that spirit within him in a merely temporary manner, in which case it shall assuredly depart from him; and whoso followeth it not, the soul of “Shin” shall dwell permanently within him: unless God had deposited that soul within him in a merely temporary manner, in which case it shall inevitably depart from him. Otherwise, both of them worship God. Thus it is that, after refusing to bow down, the first “Shin” spake in his accents, even as he is recorded in the Tradition to have spoken: which utterance at the time of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – taketh the form: “Excuse me, O Apostle of God, from acknowledging the Vicegerency of the Commander of the Faithful” – peace be upon him. To which the answer of the Lord, on that day, is the answer of the Apostle of God, which, phrased in the accents of God, is, “as I wish, not as thou wishest:” which is to say, “I wish to be obeyed in such wise as I wish, not in such wise as thou wishest.” This same Word is likewise evident in the Bayan.

The first to accept the Truth is the essence of Paradise; while the first to turn away therefrom is the essence of the Fire. All the manifestations of good culminate in the one, and all the manifestations of other than good in the other. Even as, in the Qur’an, the Lord hath counselled all in this wise: “Be not the first to disbelieve therein!” I counsel you all to be, assuredly, the first to believe in Him Whom God shall assuredly make manifest on the Day of Resurrection, in order that ye may be, assuredly, the source of all good in the Book of God: for this, truly, is a surpassing bounty; and I, verily, caution you not to be, assuredly, shut out as by a veil through Him before all other souls, lest ye be, assuredly, the source of other than good: for this, truly, is a grievous torment.

Were one to look with a discerning eye, he would see that whatever good is destined to be made manifest in the Bayan reverteth unto the first to utter the word “Yea,” who believed in the Point of Truth, and whose creation occurred first among the Exalted Letters; while all the manifestations of other than good revert unto the first to utter the word “Nay.” The one is a Fire beyond which there is none fiercer in the Bayan; while the other is a Paradise beyond which there is none greater in the Bayan: and so shall they remain until the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when the reasoners on that day shall reason in this same manner with respect to Him also.

The Fire hath not become such save through failure to bow down before the Lord, Who is adored by all – which association of this Word with him he meriteth on account of lack of belief in the Point of the Bayan. Nor hath he revealed his fiery nature unto himself, and unto all, save through doing whatsoever he doth “for the sake of God:” whence, for example, out of the extremity of his caution, he hath refrained, in view of the scruple he hath conceived, from performing ablutions, or resolving to fast, in his own home: nay, he hath made scruple of all the mosques in his land, performing prayers in one only – all of which precautions are rejected in the sight of God, and so many expressions of the Fire: for that sign in his soul in virtue whereof, as he imagined, he did whatsoever he did “for the sake of God,” was the same sign which had shone forth in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan in His former existence, which is none other but the Revelation of the Point of the Furqan; and had he recognized Him to be the same as He, the very idea of hesitating with respect to Him would not have crossed his mind.

And yet recognize Him he did, for He had been made manifest with the same proof wherewith the Primal Point had been made manifest aforetime – namely, the Verses of God: as he himself could plainly see, for of the Point of the Furqan today there is naught else apparent save the Verses of God. The moment, therefore, that he heard the Verses of God, yet bowed not down, neither confessed the Lordship of His Creator, his inner nature – which had until then existed only potentially within him – was brought into being, and he donned in consequence the robe of the First Gate of the Fire. I seek refuge in God from such a fate! If, however, one believe in God, this embodiment of the Fire hath no way of reaching him: and God, verily, protecteth His believing servants.

Each soul who stood opposed to one of the Gates of Paradise of the Qur’an is himself a universal gate of the Fire, in the shadow whereof other similar manifestations are raised up: all of which revert unto that first heart which is the essence of pure Negation; while all good, and the manifestations thereof, revert unto the Point of the Furqan, Whose heart is the quintessential reality of all Affirmation.

The most beloved of All Things unto him that dwelleth in the Fire is none other but the one from whom he hath been shut out as by a veil; while the most abhorrent of All Things in his sight is none other but his own self, which hath caused him to remain so deprived: even as in the Qur’an the most beloved of All Things in the eyes of the slayer of the Fifth Letter was precisely he who proclaimed “God is Most Great!” – yet still he bore the burden of that which came to pass: even though, had he known him to be the manifestation of Grandeur in that day, he would have bowed down before him, nor ever would the thought of other than love towards him have entered his heart.

The most abhorrent of all things in his own sight is none other but his own self: which is the same concerning which the Lord hath sent down in all the Holy Books, “I shall not forgive him.” The First Letter of the Fire in the Bayan, for example, merely in virtue of understanding the words of a divine who regardeth himself as related unto the Holy Family – these being the Viceregents of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; while the Apostle is appointed on the part of God – assuredly held himself in high esteem, and was honoured by all: how, then, would the thought of other than love towards the word of Him by Whom Prophethood is established, and Who is the Manifestation of pure Lordship and sheer Godhead, have entered his heart, when night and day he was bowing down before none other than He?

Thus it is that he hath remained shut out as by a veil; hath neglected the One Who is his Best-Beloved; and hath donned the robe of the most abhorrent of All Things, which is the first to turn away through Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. Nay, it was in virtue of the former that the latter donned this robe: even as each subsequent Revelation is the cause of that preceding, in the sight of God, in a nobler guise. For Jesus was created for the sake of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him, just as the Qur’an was created for the sake of the creation of the Bayan, and the Bayan was created for the sake of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest.

Although the pen consenteth not to set down the name of the one to whose soul the mere thought should occur of other than obedience to Him, on the Day of His appearance with perspicuous signs, on the part of God – exalted and glorified be He – yet, should such a one appear, it is the robe of this that that hath donned; and it is through the blindness of this that that hath been blinded; and it is through the Negation of this that that hath embraced Negation; and it is through the remoteness of this that that hath become remote; and it is through the Fire of this, that that hath turned into Fire.

Whoso, on that day, seeketh refuge in Him Whom God shall make manifest, the manifestations of this embodiment of the Fire shall not reach him. The meaning of “I seek refuge in God” on that day is to believe in Him, not simply to utter this Word: for the First Gate of the Fire was wont to repeat this same Word times without number, seeking thereby refuge from his own self, which was “Shin:” but it availed his condition naught, since, had he been sincere, he must needs have sought refuge in the Point of the Bayan, through believing in Him, from his own self, which believeth not in Him. Otherwise, what doth it profit him each night and day, according to the prescription of the Qur’an – setting aside the practice of the Prophet – to bow down thirty-four times before God, through Him, even while inflicting upon Him – what is the exigence of his inner nature – that which the pen is ashamed to mention; notwithstanding that he boweth down through Him, and professeth himself desirous of drawing nigh unto Him: whereas he is in His sight the remotest of all creatures, and the origin of all fire?

In the Revelation of the Bayan too, just as in Paradise all revolveth around the number Vahid, so too in the Fire it is in this same wise. However illimitably it may proliferate, it is in both cases but the proliferation of that same First Vahid. Whoso believeth in the Bayan, and whatsoever the Lord hath sent down therein, hath been, and is, in the shadows of Paradise; while whoso deviateth therefrom hath been, and is, in the shadow of the Fire. It is not that by the term “Gates” is intended aught such as a city gate: nay rather, for example, the Gate of Paradise in the Land of Ba’ is none other but the Lights who dwell therein, and are subsumed under the shadow of the Universal Gate. The shade is even as the shadow. I seek refuge in God from other than the Letters of Affirmation at every time, and before each time, and after each time; and I, verily, put my whole trust in God in every matter, and before each matter, and after each matter.

For example, conceive thou the First Gate of Paradise as the Point; and the First Gate of the Fire as the one who standeth opposed thereto, up to the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest. Regard thou the water of Negation in the veins of the rejected trees as evanescent; and the water of Affirmation in the veins of the well-rooted trees as permanent: until Negation is brought to naught, in such wise that there remaineth thereof in the Bayan not so much as a mention thereof, save in the Book; while Affirmation is affirmed, to the degree that all take pride in their relation thereto.

How many a fire shall the Lord convert into light through Him Whom God shall make manifest! And how many a light shall He convert into fire through Him! If at the time of “Ghiyath” He be made manifest, and all enter therein, none shall remain in the Fire. And if it come to the time of “Mustaghath,” and all enter therein, none shall remain in the Fire, but rather all shall be converted into light. Beseech ye this very bounty of Him Whom God shall make manifest, for this is the Transcendent Bounty and the Supreme Attainment: that ye remain not like the remaining peoples – like the Letters of the Evangel who, even though two further Books have been sent down on the part of God, are still awaiting “He that shall come, Whose name is Ahmad.”

Should He not appear up to the time of these two Names, it is inevitable nevertheless that He shall be made manifest; nor is there any escape therefrom: notwithstanding that I behold His appearance even as this sun in the midmost heaven, and the setting of all even as the stars of night by the light of day – in respect of belief and reality, that is, not of the physical temple, and of outward material means. Conceive ye that time to be even as today, and say:

“That, verily, is God, your Lord: His are the creation and the Command; no God is there but Him, the Exalted, the Great.”

Although the decrees of God differ in each particular respect, yet in the Bayan there is no mention but the mention of Him: haply, at the time of His appearance, He shall witness no sadness at the hands of His believers, who believed in Him whilst He was concealed from their eyes, and all of whom now abide His advent. I, verily, commit His affairs unto God, His Lord: He, verily, is the best of protectors and succourers, and He, verily, is the best of advocates and supporters. He it is Who sufficeth all above All Things; nor doth any thing suffice above Him. For no thing, without belief in Him, hath any fruit, even while no thing, with belief in Him, hath any sadness.

Otherwise, God, verily, sufficeth you above All Things – O All Things, even above All Things! – while no thing, verily, sufficeth you above God, your Lord; nor doth any thing suffice above any other thing, neither in the heavens, nor in the earth, nor in whatsoever is between them: save only he who seeketh sufficiency in God, His Lord; He, verily, is the All-Knowing, the All-Sufficing, the All-Powerful.

All that which hath so far been mentioned concerneth the lifetime of the servant; while after death, the reality thereof is such as no human heart can conceive. I seek refuge in God from all to which the term “Fire” may be applied, the which revolveth around the axis of the Fire in each Dispensation, which today in the Bayan is apparent.

Whensoever the servant entereth into a land the possessor whereof is Light, he entereth into Paradise; otherwise, if he entereth into a land related unto the Fire, should he do so for the love thereof, he shall enter into the Fire at once; unless by his visit he purposeth to undertake some matter for the sake of God, in which case let him beseech God to take vengeance thereon. Methinks I see already that the believers in God shall not enter into the places associated with the Fire: until it shall reach the pass that the very roots of the Fire enter not into their own places; or, if they do so, seek refuge therefrom: unless the Point of the Bayan, or He Whom God shall make manifest, should grant permission unto their believers, or unto the witnesses in truth, to do so, if in some such place they judge expedient to secure some benefit for a believing soul.

Otherwise, do thou enter Kufih, and look upon that place whereon the seat of the Fire was established, and say: “Truly did God promise! Even so doth God cause Negation to perish, until no trace thereof remaineth, even on the earth.” Then look upon the seat of the Light, and say: “Truly did God promise! Even so doth God affirm Affirmation through His Command.” He, verily, is the All-Knowing, the All-Powerful.

Gate Eighteen of the Second Unity: Explaining that the Hour is coming, no doubt is there about it

The substance of this gate is that in each Dispensation, “the Hour” is in the primary sense the Manifestation of the Will of God: whereafter the term is applied at lower levels, to the degree that if He apply it to any true statement which is related unto Him, on His part, in His Revelation, He doth so justly; otherwise is it not fitting that the term should be applied thereto. This principle is valid to the extent even that if during His Revelation some tidings on His part be relayed to another person, the statement “the Hour is coming, no doubt is there about it” would still be warranted in this case, inasmuch as it testifieth unto His exaltation.

In this day, “the Hour” is the Soul of the Bayan, Who cometh unto the people, and judgeth them even until the Day of Resurrection; nor is there any escape therefrom. Were the seas of the heavens to be converted, in explanation of “the Hour,” into ink, they would be unable to impart so much as a sprinkling of all that could be said on this head. In each Revelation of the Truth, of whatever object the True One saith that is “the Hour,” its identification therewith is indubitably established by that very word.

Do ye then await the Revelation of God, for the Hour, verily, shall come upon you suddenly, and, verily, unto God, your Lord, shall ye be presented for judgment.

Gate Nineteen of the Second Unity

On this, that all that is in the Bayan is a present from God unto Him Whom God shall make manifest. Exalted art Thou, O my Lord the Omnipotent! How puny and contemptible my word and all that pertaineth unto me appear unless they be related to Thy great glory. Grant that through the assistance of Thy grace whatsoever pertaineth unto me may be acceptable in Thy sight. Thou verily art the best of the gracious ones.

The substance of this gate is this, that in each Dispensation, the writings of the Manifestation of Truth is a present from God for Himself in His Next Revelation, which is the manifestation of His being in the Next Resurrection. Likewise, all that God hath sent unto the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, is today visible in those who believe in the Qur’an, while the mirrors of their hearts, were a mere present from God unto the Qa’im, a descendant of the Family of Muhammad, peace be upon Them. For example that which God hath revealed unto Jesus, was a gift from God unto Muhammad the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, inasmuch as the purpose of His Book was naught but the very souls who recognised Muhammad, as well as all that returneth unto them, though it be an infinitesimal part (a ninth of a ninth of a tenth of a tenth) of an atom of dust.”

In like manner, all that cometh into existence in the Bayan, of diverse beloved modes, is a present from the Point of the Bayan unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, Who is but the very Next Revelation of the Point of the Bayan. And this supreme glory and pride would suffice all, if He accept a person or a thing, by granting them the honour of association with Himself. But today, the present pertaining to the Dispensation of Gospel is not accepted by even the least significant of the very lowest of the Qur’anic manifestations, how much less it would be accepted by the Manifestation of Truth. In like manner, the least significant of the very lowest of the Bayan refuseth to accept the most sublime of the past, unless he entereth beneath the shadow of the Testimony that the believer of the Bayan hath entered.

Likewise, He Whom God shall make manifest will not accept anything pertaining unto the Bayan, except the things that become related unto His Book. The same principle applieth to endless Revelations of God. In each Dispensation, all the modes that return unto the First Revelation, are but a gift from God unto Him for the day of His Revelation in the Next Resurrected Life.

How utterly remote is the man who breaketh his relation unto Him, and ceaseth to be a true gift. Thus today, should the believers in the Qur’an desire to present the gift of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, they all should recognise the Bayan, otherwise, they would severe from themselves the attribute of glory and sublimity. Such severance is not because of any external admonishment by the Exalted Tree, saying, wherefore ye are veiled from attaining the presence of your Beloved. Rather at that very moment, it is He Who remaineth the supreme Object of desire of your hearts, inasmuch as ye even refuse to engage in your worldly pursuits unless ye consider the good pleasure of God therein. Yet today, when the Exalted Tree, Who is the Mine of divine good pleasure, hath been manifested, ye are veiled from the Fruit of your existence, unto Whom your souls return. What ye do harmeth only your own selves. For the All-Possessing God is independent from you and from all that pertaineth unto you. As for ye, should ye relate your souls unto God, ye would thereby become immortalised, and partake in glory; otherwise ye would perish naught but your souls. Behold then ye, and attain certitude.

The Third Unity

Gate One of the Third Unity: On this, that anything that existeth is His possession, and He, more than anything besides Him, holdeth the rightful authority over it

The substance of this gate is this, that the Lord of the universe hath created all things for the sake of the Exalted One Who refereth unto Him. He is the Mirror of Truth, Who hath always been, and will continue forever to be, the One Who revealeth God. All things have been fashioned in the past, and all things will be fashioned in the future, solely through Him, while He subsisteth by His own Self, by virtue of the grace of God. All things are dependent in their existence upon Him, and nothing attaineth thingness, except through Him. Therefore, His truth and legitimate right surpasseth those of all things, and all besides Him are His possessions by virtue of the fact that all beings are absolutely held in the hands of the Most Holy Essence. Thus, He holdeth in His hands more right to all aspects of all things than the things do to themselves.

The fruit of this knowledge is this, that were the Point of Truth to bestow all things upon a thing, His decree would be absolutely binding, be it actually fulfilled or remaineth just a mere command. For example, Had the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, conquered, all that is on earth, He would have held more rightful authority over them than that of their owners. Such is the meaning of the absolute possession of all things by God, when the people attest,

“His is the Kingdoms of the world and that of the Revelation.”

Likewise, should He Whom God shall make manifest take possession of the inmost realities of all things, He would hold more rightful authority over them than the things themselves do in relation to their inmost realities, even though He is far exalted and glorified to even glance at anything, inasmuch as all things look up to His bounty and grace. He is independent of all things by virtue of His Self, while He remaineth dependent upon God by virtue of His Essence.

The fruit of this gate is this, that in the Day of His Revelation, if He pronounce a law, all would be mindful of His supreme truth and right, that none may say unto Him why or wherefore. Should He enjoin a decree concerning anything, it would befit no one to speak of any right of ownership before Him, inasmuch as He holdeth in his hands more rightful authority over that thing than the thing doeth to itself. At first He will not command except according to the decrees of the Bayan, till the time cometh when He chooseth to renew His sovereign covenant with all, which layeth low the necks of all things. Should He command that a man, who is according to the law of the Bayan entitled to inheritance, may inherit not even a carat, that would assuredly be the law of God in the Bayan for that man.

And if he receive any share, he would transgress the Command of his Lord. In like manner, were today the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, to proclaim that a law which hath been revealed in the Qur’an in a certain way, must be now fulfilled in another way, there could be no doubt that this command is the law of the Qur’an, even if it is revealed in this Day. For that which hath been revealed before, hath also been from Him, and in the estimation of those who recognise God, the past and present laws are one and the same. This is what is worthy of His supreme right and authority.

As for the right that the people deserve, the Pen is ashamed to even mention it. Behold! All perform the Friday Prayer solely by virtue of His Command, yet should He command one of them not to pray in the position of leadership, or that another soul is more entitled to lead the prayer, he would refuse to obey Him. While he beareth allegiance of faith unto His earlier command, yet he even refraineth to accept Him as one who believeth in His earlier Cause (Islam), otherwise this would not have happened.

This was the right that is worthy of the creatures. But the authority that behoveth Him is this, that should He announce a new word, to replace the declarative word of the divine unity, previously deposited by Him in the hearts, He would hold more authority over His previous declarative word than that very word doeth over itself. Even as in the Revelation of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, He cancelled the word of the divine unity that was previously imprinted in the hearts, and thus the splendours of His new Qur’anic declarative word was revealed upon all the hearts. Had He not possessed the supreme right over that word, He could not have removed it.

When He manifesteth in this supreme way, His absolute lordship in regard to the most sublime station of the servants, how that which is derived therefrom is even worth mentioning! Should one fix his gaze upon the Sun of Truth, he would recognise his own limit, nay, rather, he would glory in being related to Him, even if it is the very relation of servitude and subjection, like that of all other things. For the loftiest glory of all tings is this, that it is He, and none but Him, Who is the Supreme Lord of all things.

Therefore, if one show no vain pride in the Next Revelation of the Day-Star of Truth, he would be numbered as steadfast and exalted in His previous Revelation. On the other hand, the same truth is evident and clear in those letters of Gospel who glory not in the letters of the Qur’an, and enter not beneath His shadow, though they pride themselves in bearing allegiance unto Gospel! The same principle is true with regard to the Revelation before His previous Revelation, till it reacheth that of the First Adam, which is without any beginning, as well as in the Revelation after His Next revelation till it endeth in the Last Revelation which is without any end. Say! God createth all things, and then He returneth them all. There will never be any mention after God, even as there hath never been any mention before Him. Will ye not then believe?

Gate Two of the Third Unity: On this, that things are created by His Word, should It be uttered by Him, for verily His Word is the Truth

The substance of this gate is this, that no word of any contingent being resembleth the word of the exalted Tree of Truth, inasmuch as the inmost reality of things is created by virtue of His word. For example, if that Exalted Tree had not spoken of the guardianship of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon Him, that very successorship would not have been created. Even though He hath been from time immemorial, the God’s Guardian, but the Source and the Beginning of the Revelation is His word in that Dispensation, and not a word earlier. In like manner, all that is non-truth, from the first fire till the last, are fashioned by His word, otherwise, if He had not proclaimed, “Verily this is not true,” they would not have been realised either in the universe, or in the souls. Therefore, both light and fire revolve around His word.

Likewise, in the Revelation of the Bayan, if the first fire had not been mentioned, how could it have been created? And likewise, if the word light had not been uttered, how its guardianship could have been proven? Behold, how many gates of fire appeared in the Dispensation of the Qur’an, after the disappearance of the Exalted Tree of Love. Then why there is no longer any mention of them? Witness how fire is proven for them, and the universal disowning of them is manifest unto all.

For those endued with understanding heart, there hath been no doubt, nor there ever will be one, that should He speak of the Letter of the Sublime Paradise, the universal soul of light would instantly be created, in its own station, through that utterance, to celebrate divine unity with utter sincerity and devotion. And should He, by virtue of His justice, utter the letter of non-sublime paradise, the universal soul would be generated in fire, in its own station, where the pen is ashamed to even mention that which it deserveth.

There is no greater bounty in any Revelation of Truth for the people in that Dispensation, than this, that the Supreme Manifestation of the Will would not gaze upon anything unbefitting of Him (dun-i-istihqaq). For if He would, then He definitely shall pronounce the due judgement on it, which would call that decree into being, and become the fire for the people of that Revelation. Were the people to know how profitable is it that no non-truth is gazed upon by Him, they verily would strive, with their utmost power, that the non-truth may not be mentioned before Him. Otherwise, the non-truth would be judged, turn to fire in that Dispensation, and the people would perish therein.

Likewise, had all the people exerted their utmost endeavour in the inception of this Revelation, that naught may be mentioned before the Exalted Tree but that which is worthy of Him, there would have been made no mention of fire, to become the everlasting abode of those who are veiled. For the fire is created by His utterance. Otherwise, why there is no mention of that letter of non-truth that hath preceded this second letter of non-truth, even though both have wronged people equally? Rather, the moment that this latter performed, in defiance of truth, an unbefitting act before the Truth, his existence hath been called into being by virtue of this relation, and therefore, until the Day of Resurrection all will disown him, and he will perish in the fire of his negation.

On the other hand, there is no bounty greater than this, that in each Revelation of Truth, the people of that Dispensation firmly grasp the words of God, inasmuch as their inmost realities are fashioned by them. For example, should He reveal a verse, without reference to any specific thing or command, like,

“God’s is the kingdoms of the heavens, the earth, and that which lieth between them. For God is potent over all things,”

then a manifestation would be created in the Bayan, who will reflect this verse, nay, rather, there would be generated endless manifestations beneath the shadow of that manifestation, even as there are a number of verses like this in the Qur’an. Yet, there hath been countless manifestations of authority from the time of Revelation till today. Thus infinite shadows are created beneath the reflection of each verse.

But if the verse concerneth a specific law, then all would act in conformity with it till the Day of Resurrection, like the law of khums, or other enjoined laws. Therefore, His word is what createth things, and is unlike the words of men. For in His word, naught is seen but God, and none besides God is the Creator of things, Provider of things, Slayer of things, Quickener of things, Fashioner of things, or Generator of things. Behold! His is the kingdoms of the creation and that of the Revelation, aforetimes, and hereafter. For He is the Lord of all worlds.

Should one attain the time of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, no bounty would be more exalted for him or anyone else, than this, that the attributes pertaining to fire would not be mentioned before Him, otherwise, the indomitable determination of God would call the fire into being. On the other hand, each soul must strive to receive, to the degree of his own inmost reality, his sustenance from the mine of His grace, till His Next revelation, and thus to be honoured in the interval between the two Revelations by His bestowal, though it be a single verse, for the spirits pertaining to that word, will assuredly be manifested in his station. “And Whose word is more true than that of God?” Could ye but recognise it.

Gate Three of the Third Unity

On this, that The Bayan and whosoever is therein revolve round the saying of Him Whom God shall make manifest, even as the Alif (the Gospel) and whosoever was therein revolved round the saying of Muhammad, the Apostle of God. In like manner, that which God hath revealed unto Muhammad in His First Revelation, and whosoever is therein, circle around His saying in His Next Revelation.

The substance of this gate is this, that the Bayan hath no end in view but Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as none save Him hath ever repealed, or will ever repeal, this Book, even as none but Him hath ever revealed, or will ever reveal, it. The Bayan and such as are believers therein yearn more ardently after Him than the yearning of any lover after his beloved. Even as the Qur’an and the spirits that pertain thereto, yearned after the Revelation of its Revealer, and have never had in view, nor will ever have in view, any end but Him. Today the Furqan sendeth salutations unto those letters who have uplifted it, and caused it to enter in the Bayan, whereas it beseecheth its Revealer to torment those spirits who have not entered the Bayan, and have failed to give the Furqan its due portion.

Likewise, the Bayan sendeth salutations unto those amongst its faithful souls, who are its letters of the sublime paradise, who will recognise Him Whom God shall make manifest, and elevate the Bayan towards His Book. On the other hand, it beseecheth God, glorified and exalted be Him, to torment the letters of the non-sublime paradise, those who at the time of His Revelation, will refuse to bow down, for the sake of God, before Him, and are veiled from attaining God’s presence by some excuse.

Should one behold with the eyes of the heart, he would hear today this crying out from the Qur’anic letters: ‘Help us! Help us! O our Lord and the Lord of all things! Overtake us, and deliver us from the fire of our relation to what we have been related to. Then relate us to Thyself, and cause us to enter in the Bayan, for verily we seek Thy grace.’ Even as this was the very word of the letters of the Alif in the past, and the same shall be cried out by the Bayan in the future.

May bounty and grace rest upon he who will not waste the due right of the Bayan, will not bring its torment and wrath upon himself, and will kneel down before its Supreme Revealer. For in the Day of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the Bayan will gaze upon its believers, and ask them: ‘Is there any spirit related unto me, who would step forward in this Day, and acknowledge Him Whom God shall make manifest, and thus be faithful to the covenant of his Lord that is established in me?’ It would be rejoiced if its faithfuls recognise its Revealer, and would be grieved if its faithfuls grieve its Revealer. Thus, nothing is more afflicted with anguish today than the Furqan. All recite it, yet they fail to receive its blessing, and attain naught but its torment, even as those who were reciting the Book of Alif in the day of the Revelation of the Furqan.

O the people of the Bayan! Refuse to do the like of that which is done by the people of the Furqan, and be not veiled by anything from your Beloved, inasmuch as the supreme exaltation of the Bayan, and that of its spirits, is its ascent unto Him. Cry not in clamorous protest, “Help O Bayan! Help O Bayan!” Ponder upon the Cause of God, and bow down before the same One unto Whom ye kneel down at all times. For the Bayan will never be content with you, unless ye recognise Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as He is the One Who hath revealed the Bayan and all the other Scriptures. Then it will intercede before Him on behalf of its believers, and its intercession is surely accepted by its Revealer.

Ere the inception of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, none will call unto God by the Bayan, except that his prayer will be answered. But after that, should he call unto God by the Bayan, infinite times, his prayer would never be answered. As to the Bayan and whosoever is therein, of those who are loved by Thee, and not those who are not, I beseech Thee O God, by Thy bounty and grace, to bestow, in the Day of Thy Revelation, Thy mercy upon the Bayan and upon whomsoever believeth therein. O God! Exalt the Bayan and whomsoever believeth therein, in that Day, by that which will be revealed from Thee. For verily Thou art the best of the mercifuls.

Gate Four of the Third Unity

explaining that whatever Verses and Words God may send down upon Him are greater and more exalted than that which God hath sent down at this time.

The substance of this gate is that on every appearance of the Manifestation of the Will of God, just as the Manifestation Himself is more exalted than His own previous Manifestation, so too His Words are more exalted than His own previous Words: nay, the first are the Former Creation thereof, and the second the Latter Creation thereof, as is indubitably established in the sight of God and of those endued with understanding. Yea more, the first are revealed not but for the second; nor the second but for the third; nor the third but for the fourth; and so on everlastingly throughout an eternity for which, by which, from which, to which, there is no end.

To the same degree that the excellence of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – surpasseth that of Jesus – peace be upon Him – the excellence of the Qur’an surpasseth that of the preceding Book.
