This is the essence of every essence, wherefrom all are shut out as by a veil. They take pride in these baseless scientific matters, which if they be not conjoined to belief in Him become as naught; while remaining shut out as by a veil from belief in Him, the believer in Whom – even if he know naught – shall be credited with the whole essence of knowledge. Thus it is that all are seemingly dead, nor have regard for the fruit of knowledge and philosophy.

The worst of people on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest are those who esteem themselves upon their knowledge, failing to grasp even this much, that their knowledge is for the sake of understanding His words aforetime: whence at the time of His appearance what need can there be there for learning these sciences, considering that His utterance is manifest and His purpose is evident; even as, in this present Revelation, anyone – whoever it may be – hath observed this circumstance.

God establisheth the Truth as such, and He is the best of judges.

Gate Eleven of the Fourth Unity

Whoso transgresseth the precepts laid down in the Bayan, he will not be reckoned as a believer, no matter his position, a learned, a king, a slave, or a servant.

The substance of this gate is this, that at the moment of the revelation of the Bayan, God hath gazed upon all His creatures, and therefore, hath ordained precepts for all people in every level of standing, so that no soul in the paradise of the Bayan would be grieved or constrained to the least degree. Rather, He hath commanded a universal precept for all things, that whoever possesseth power over anything, must elevate that thing to its uttermost perfection, that it would not be deprived of its own paradise. For example, the paradise of a paper in which a few excellent lines are inscribed, is this, that it would be refined with utmost kinds of gold-illumination, adornment, and excellence that is customary for the most exalted patched scrolls. Then the possessor of that paper hath elevated it to its utmost possible degree of glory. Should he know of a higher degree of refinement and fail to manifest it in that patched paper, he would deprive it of its paradise, and he would be held accountable, that wherefore despite possession of power, thou hast withhold the effusion of grace and favour.

Whoso transgresseth the precepts of the Bayan, no matter whether the most exalted or the most abased amongst the creatures, he would not be judged as faithful. However, watch yourselves lest ye pronounce such judgement against Him Whom God shall make manifest, inasmuch as until the time that He would make Himself known to anyone, which is the supreme paradise of that soul, he would command in conformity with the laws of the Bayan, but upon the time of Revelation no one is permitted to say why or wherefore in regard to His command, for the precepts laid down in the Bayan are all from Him.

But be watchful for the Revelation, for His Revelation resembleth the Revelation of the Bayan, letter by letter, and verse by verse. Thus He shall assuredly shine upon the inmates of His dominion in stages. Thus in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, the first effulgence embraced only two souls, till it gradually reached unto all. Be attentive and watch for the hour of Revelation, that should it be manifested unto one, he would not be cleft asunder out of the majesty of the Revelation, seeing all the people of the Bayan rise from their seats for His name, and then hearth all of a sudden that the one who hath been day and night with him is none but Him. Rather, behold the truth of this same principle in regard to the Point of the Qur’an, and in all the Revelation preceding Him till that of Adam, as well as in the infinite Revelations to come.

But seek refuge in God lest ye be the first who conceive of non-truth with regard to His Truth, and attain the supreme excellence of the precedence in faith, even if ye witness that He is not yet recognised by anyone. For even in that very moment of unity, the moment that He is not yet recognised by anyone, the Testimony of God is complete and perfect, could ye but comprehend. Ye observe that the most mighty testimony of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, which is naught but the Qur’an, is today recognised by countless number of the faithful, yet this very same testimony was present in the early Islam, and till seven years no soul acknowledged that Most Great Day-Star.

Take heed and be watchful at all times not to transgress the precepts of the Bayan. This same principle was also confirmed in the Qur’an, as it hath been revealed,

“Those who judge not in conformity with that which is revealed by God, they are assuredly numbered amongst the disbelievers.”

Likewise in two other verses the same people are described by two other abased attributes. Notwithstanding that, ye witness the extent of their transgression from the laws of God.

But watch yourselves that ye never heedlessly extend the judgement of this verse unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, for at that time, “that which is revealed by God” is naught but His command, even as at the time of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, “that which is revealed by God” was the Qur’an, and not that which was revealed in the Gospel. In like manner, today that which was revealed by God in the Qur’an is but that which is revealed by God in the Bayan, and not that which is revealed by God in the Qur’an.

It is for this reason that all imagine that what they do is “for God”, whereas in truth all their doings is “for one other than God”. For the Essence of Eternity is immeasurably sanctified above the reach of any judgement for or against Him. Rather, in its primary truth, this pertaineth to the Manifestation of the Primal Will, as it is explicitly testified by the Qur’an: “In truth, they who plighted fealty unto thee, really plighted that fealty unto God.” The same principle is true in all other modes of action, and therefore, a judgement against Him is a judgement against God.

Nay, even the Members of the Sacred Family, have descended this same principle, and have applied it, in its secondary truth, unto themselves as well, even as the Long Friday visitation tablet is filled with assertions like this:

“He who recogniseth You, hath recognised God, and he who faileth to recognise You, hath failed to recognise God. He who loveth You, hath loved God, and he who hateth You hath hated God.”

Today only God reckoneth the number of times that the adherents of the Shi’ih sect recite this visitation tablet, yet the Imams have Themselves returned unto this world, and none recogniseth Them, while day and night they continue to recite this tablet without the slightest trace of understanding!

This is certainly not due to any incompleteness of the testimony of God, even as in the day of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, the promise of Jesus to the Christians was fulfilled, that “Who shall come after me, bearing the Name Ahmad,” and yet until this very day they have halted within Christianity and eagerly await the fulfilment of that promise, as thou canst witness myriads and myriads of the people who are in the West, who have remained in that same belief. This is due to the fact that they have not pondered upon the testimony of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, which was the Qur’an, otherwise, at the time of the Revelation, all would have witnessed that the promise of Jesus was fulfilled. Inasmuch as they were shut out as by a veil from Him, they turned into permanent inmates of fire, but they imagine that they are still faithful to their religion and are awaiting.

O people of the Bayan! Take pity upon yourselves, that the same disgrace would not come about at the time of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest.

Describing the manifestations of divine decree, the Members of the Sacred Family have even applied that principle, in its tertiary truth, to Their Shi’ih followers. For all this visible grandeur that the Doctors display in Islam, is solely due to the word of the Imam, peace be upon Him, in His long tradition, whose fruit is this:

“He who repudiateth him, hath repudiated Us, and he who repudiateth Us, hath repudiated the Apostle of God, and he who repudiateth the Apostle of God, hath repudiated God.”

Nay, rather, They have further extended the same principle and have applied it to the faithful in general, even as it is mentioned in the tradition regarding the interpretation of the Surih of the Cow, whose essence is this: “Whoso bringeth joy to a believer, he hath brought joy unto God.” Behold then how the people have been content with descent in four degrees, and yet in regard to the supreme Station of Truth, in Whom naught is seen but God, in Whose praise is revealed the verse, “Be not forward in the presence of God,” they commit so grievously. Though some have understood this verse to be a reference to forwardness in the presence of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, but this is contrary to God’s intention, for in that same verse, the Apostle is also mentioned. Rather, it refereth unto the Sun of Truth, Who is the most exalted side of the Apostle, in Whom naught is seen except God.

All these diverse points are solely mentioned in this gate for the sake of gathering fruit, that none may be veiled from the purpose, the Desired One, for God is the best of Judges.

Gate Twelve of the Fourth Unity: Concerning the assumption of all shrines on earth

The substance of this gate is that in each Revelation vouchsafed by God, the shrines that were in the preceding Revelation are taken up: for example, do any who now follow the religion of the Apostle of God behold today the shrines of the Viceregents of Jesus? Nay, their very names are not known, how much less the places where they are buried. In like manner, after the appearance of the Manifestation, all the exalted graves on earth are taken up, ranging from that of the Manifestation of Prophethood on the one hand, to those of the manifestations of the Shi’ih on the other. Nay, the graves that are attributed to the former Prophets, in Kufih or elsewhere, must likewise be taken up; and so too the site of the House: for, as thou observest, the people of Moses – peace be upon Him – travel to Jerusalem; the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – to the spot that Jesus hath destined for them; and the people of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him and His Family – to the Ka’bih. There is no honour in the clay itself; nay, the essence of this honour resideth in the Cause of God: wherever the former is made manifest, the latter attendeth upon it.

Consider today the level of the people: how diligently they travel to the grave of any one of the children of the Imams, who are but their kindred; while from that Manifestation, in virtue of the Verses descending upon Whom both Prophethood and Vicegerency – and the religion of all – is established, they have remained shut out as by a veil: else would He not now be residing in the Mountain of Mah-Ku. Nor marvel at this: but picture to thyself how it was on the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – aforetime: how the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – performed the works prescribed in their religion, and how the Christian monks worshipped God in their retreats; while for a period of seven years that Sun of Truth was veiled from sight in one of the mountains of Mecca, at the hand of those who recognized not His truth: whereas from the very inception of His Prophetic Mission, whatever claim to truth had been possessed by any among the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – was cut off from him, unless it came beneath His shadow.

After the appearance of the Point of the Bayan, thou seest how many people travel each year to Mecca, and perform the circumambulation: whereas that Person by Whose word the Ka’bih is the Ka’bih is consigned to solitude in this mountain. Notwithstanding, He is identically that same Apostle of God: for the likeness of the Cause of God is that of the sun, which if it rise eternally, is no more but one sun – the same through which all subsist. Thus it is that in each subsequent Revelation, the Revelation of God appeareth in a nobler guise, in respect of the Manifestation, in the manner that is apparent: for all the Revelations of the past were created for the sake of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; all these Revelations, and that Revelation, were created for the sake of the Qa’im of the House of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; and all those Revelations, and the Revelation of the Qa’im of the House of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – were created for the sake of Him Whom God shall make manifest.

In like manner all those Revelations, and this Revelation, and the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest were created for the sake of the Revelation after Him Whom God shall make manifest; while all these Revelations were created for the sake of the Revelation after that following Him Whom God shall make manifest; and in such wise the Sun of Truth shall continue throughout eternity to rise and set; nor hath there ever been, or ever shall be, any beginning or end to this process.

Blessed is the soul who, in each Revelation, understandeth the purpose of God in that Revelation; rather than, through having regard for the various manifestations of the preceding Revelation, being shut out therefrom in the succeeding Revelation as by a veil. For in this day, whatsoever was instituted in Islam was in virtue of the Prophetic Mission of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; while whatsoever was exalted in the religion of Jesus – peace be upon Him – was in virtue of this same Prophetic Mission. In like manner, should one consider the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, he would see that whatsoever hath come to pass in the Bayan is in virtue of the appearance of the Possessor of the Seven Letters; while on that Day, should he have regard for the Source of Command, he shall not remain shut out as by a veil therefrom by the exalted manifestations of the Bayan, beside each law of which innumerable souls have slumbered, priding themselves upon its observance, and conscientiously putting it into effect, even as is witnessed in this day: for each one of these manifestations of the Bayan is subsumed, in His eyes, under the shadow of a single pronouncement on His part of the Word, “We have lifted it up:” howbeit He shall not lift it up until he hath sent down a greater in its place.

In this wise also do thou behold the present Revelation: until the Lord make manifest a greater than the preceding Revelation He shall not command the latter to be lifted up. God is powerful over All Things.

Gate Thirteen of the Fourth Unity

concerning the exaltation of the shrines of the Vahid, and the stipulation that whoso owneth aught of the shrines on earth is not permitted to expend it save on those shrines themselves. Be it not concealed that no day or night passeth on which the true and other-than-true manifestations in all the worlds are not manifest and hidden upon this earth; while all the human spirits, from Adam until this day, enjoy the felicity of human temples, and likewise the other-than-believing temples are tormented in temples of the Fire. Howbeit, in each Revelation a particular law is revealed, which all are enjoined to obey; while after the setting of the Sun, this law is exalted up to the following Revelation, during Its concealment.

In this Revelation of the Bayan, the Lord hath not wished to see any exalted resting-place except those of Muhammad and His Family – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and the Gates of Guidance: who in this Revelation are referred to as the Letters of the Vahid. For He wisheth but to look upon nineteen exalted resting-places; while those of the rest of the prophets, saints, witnesses and believers – whose hearts have ever been, and ever shall be, the daysprings of the Names and Likenesses of God – are hidden under the shadow thereof, so that the matter may not become hard for the people: for should anyone wish to reckon their full number he would be unable to do so; and all are within this same First Vahid, whereof – in the sight of God, and of those endowed with understanding – they are accounted the proliferation.

Blessed is each soul who is graciously aided to contribute to the exaltation of these peerless tombs, which shall become the alighting-places of the angels of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them. It hath been destined in the knowledge of God that they should be exalted: and exalted they shall be; nor hath there ever been, or ever shall be, any averting the Will of God: inasmuch as He is supreme over all things, and transcendent over all beings. Blessed is the soul who becometh a channel for the appearance of His Will: for he is the best preserver of the bounds which the Lord hath fixed in the Bayan. The Lord hath promised to increase two thousand-fold each mithqal of gold thus expended; to record it to the donor’s credit; and to bestow upon him that wherewith he shall be well pleased. God is powerful over All Things.

Whatever shrines there be on earth today, no one hath permission to dispose of any part of them, except he expend it on these same exalted shrines, inasmuch as it is the property of these shrines: unless, while the Sun of Truth still shineth, leave be granted in some other wise; the which is the command of God with respect to all things. Although, to this day, no other ordinance hath been promulgated, the Lord hath been, and is, best apprised of what shall transpire hereafter. Nor, ere such an ordinance hath been promulgated, hath any obligation attached, or ever shall it, upon the one charged with observance of the religious law. God hath knowledge of All Things.

Gate Fourteen of the Fourth Unity

concerning this, that whoso seeketh refuge in these shrines, shall be in safety, and shall be pardoned insomuch as God hath pardoned him.

The substance of this gate is that if anyone seek refuge in the shrines of the Letters of the Vahid, it behoveth the people to grant him refuge: inasmuch as these of all lands on earth are the manifestations of “He granteth refuge, and is not granted refuge against:” haply, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest – which is the Day of Resurrection of this Revelation – refuge shall be taken in the actual Letters of the Vahid, that deliverance may be obtained from the perdition of that Day – which perdition is one of faith, not of the body: for all perform their works in order to draw nigh unto the Lord, and if on that day they seek not refuge in the “Countenance,” they shall be lost beneath the shadow of “All Things are doomed to perish.” If there be anyone on earth endued with insight, he would give all that is on earth that he might not be lost in Negation, but enter the fold of Exception: for this is the fruit of man’s creation, that he be not of a sudden brought utterly to naught.

It is not that by seeking refuge in them is meant no more than travelling to their resting-places, or making mention of them: for in the Dispensation of the Qur’an all travelled to the graves of these Letters, and made mention of them night and day; yet, after they were made manifest with that same proof whereby their own religion was established, and communicated unto them the Message of the Point of the Bayan, all were shut out as by a veil therefrom by worldly matters, until there befell that which befell. Today in Islam, all act in accordance with their words aforetime, even while pronouncing judgment against them in their proper persons. If this had been the extent of their transgression, still no dire consequence would have befallen them: yet, they expend millions upon millions of their wealth for the sake of commemorating the sufferings of the Prince of Martyrs – may the peace of God be upon him – while against the One Who hath precedence over him they have wrought what they have wrought.

Such is the level of this spurious people, with respect to whom it is indeed a pity to make use of such a term. They do whatever they do in the name of Islam: yet against the Revealer of Islam, Who is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – they have wrought what they have wrought. Take heed, therefore, O ye endued with insight: then look discerningly into the Cause of God. They describe what they do as being “for God,” yet inflict it upon those manifestations, to pronounce judgment against whom is to pronounce judgment against God, nor know what they do; and depart from their religion, even while, in their own conceit, they conduct themselves according to the highest degree of precaution and endeavour.

Should ye make it a rule, O people of the Bayan, not to inflict upon anyone that which ye would not wish for yourselves, haply on the Day of Revelation ye shall not turn against the Letters of the Unity, even should ye not be for them. Consider ye all the recompense which, as ye relate of your Imams, attacheth to the Surihs of the Qur’an, and the recompense of the prayers ye recite – the fruit of all which on the Day of Resurrection is that ye should be gathered beneath the shadow of Muhammad and His Family, this being the greatest bounty that the Proofs of God have bestowed upon their supporters, to whom they have promised these kinds of recompenses.

Yet, praise be to God that He hath set on foot the Resurrection, and the Proofs have come to the world, and suffered in the way of upholding the confession of His Divine Unity what they have suffered: yet still the supporters of these Proofs recite the Qur’an and those prayers in expectation of the said recompenses. Nor marvel thou thereat, but consider the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – who still await the fulfilment of the promise of Him that “shall come after me, Whose name is Ahmad,” and who pray ardently night and day for His return: whereas He hath come; one thousand two hundred and seventy years have passed; His Resurrection hath been set on foot; and still they wait.

Have mercy upon yourselves, and render not your works as scattered dust, but make yourselves such a one that if ye be not for another, ye be not at least against another, inasmuch as this is the way of salvation, both in this world and the next, should ye act accordingly.

No Revelation befalleth but that the One made manifest therein admonisheth His people in the strongest terms that haply, on the day whereon the fruit is garnered – which is the subsequent Revelation – they may not be brought to naught. Until now, this fruit hath not been forthcoming from them: perchance in the Dispensation of the Bayan ye may distinguish yourselves amidst the peoples of the Day of Resurrection. For on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, whatever people have existed from the Day of Adam until that day are present on earth: nay, it is possible that people from the worlds before Adam also – and from the worlds after Him too – may be present on that Day. Do ye distinguish yourselves amidst all peoples by believing in Him: for if any of you should be shut out from Him as by a veil, ye would, in his eyes, be in a more grievous condition than all peoples; yet, should ye appear among men having garnered the fruit of your existence, ye would, in His eyes, be more honoured than every soul.

Disgrace not yourselves until the succeeding Resurrection by that which is revealed from Him: for the circumstance ye have heard of that on the Day of Resurrection all become apprised of whatever judgment is given – the intention thereof is this, that all the choicest of people on that Day are believers in that Revelation; and up to the following Revelation whatever judgment is passed, all read and see it, and act accordingly. For example, everyone who hath read the reference in the Qur’an to Abu Lahab – from the time of the revelation of the Verse up to this day – hath witnessed his creation. What a disgrace is this! Consider, could anyone gauge the full extent of it? – for but a few brief mornings of his life he was shut out as by a veil from the True One; yet afterwards he was disgraced in the eyes of all who read the Qur’an, and even in his own eyes – for he too is one of the living, in his own fiery abode. This is what is meant by the statement that all come to hear of the judgment of the Day of Resurrection. Be watchful, therefore, O ye endued with insight: then walk ye in the fear of God.

Gate Fifteen of the Fourth Unity: Concerning this, that should anyone wish to take refuge in these shrines, no one is permitted to prevent him from doing so

The substance of this gate is that if anyone wisheth to take refuge in the exalted resting-places, no one is permitted to prevent him from doing so; while the one who taketh refuge is relieved of the dominion that anyone may have exercised over him: which latter, if he be possessed of any sense of shame, would indeed grant him refuge in his own home, should he seek refuge therein. For example, if there be someone in the East of the earth who taketh refuge in another, refuge should be granted him for the sake of the refuge taken in these manifestations, to the glory of God – exalted and glorified be He – in this religion. Verily, of them that grant refuge and succour, He is the best.

Gate Sixteen of the Fourth Unity: On the Sacred House

The substance of this gate is this, that there hath never been, and will never be, any physical place for God, and that in each Revelation of the Will, it is the earth that He hath attributed to Himself, that hath become His House, and the seat around which the angels of heaven and the people of the earth revolve. Nay, rather, all circle around His Command which is manifested in that piece of dust. If this sanctity was intrinsic to the dust itself, there must have been no change of the House of God in the past, and it must never change in the future. Though it is evident to those endued with understanding heart, that even the dust-House of God resembleth the Command, and that the Command is like the sun: should there be infinite change in the seats of the House, it would remain one and the same House.

Therefore, the change therein is like the relation of each Revelation of the Will to the Next Revelation. Otherwise, the dust that in the Day of Adam was attributed to God, is the very dust that is related unto Him in this Day. Even as the same Command that pertained unto that House, is the very Command that pertaineth to The Sacred House in This Dispensation. This House is in truth, naught but the glorious Seat of the establishment of Him Whom God shall make manifest, which is exactly the very House of He Who hath been Manifested, which is in turn the same as the seat of Ka’bih. Its measures equal the numerical value of the Name God (Allah=66) in Dhar’, width by length, without reckoning the walls.

Had it been in the power of the faithful, it would have been ordained that the House would be raised from diamond upon the water, and its dust would be made out of Elixir, and its water out of the crimson-coloured perfume! However, inasmuch as no such power is witnessed, any form befitting the utter exaltation is acceptable. But should the outward and the inward be made out of mirror, it would be closer to purity than the other forms that are manifest today amongst the men of industry.

In the land of Fars, there is a Mosque in the center of which rises a structure similar to the Ka’bih, (Masjid-i-Jum’ih). It was built solely as a sign indicating the Manifestation of the Will of God through the erection of the house in that land. [Allusion to the new Mecca, i.e., the house of the Bab in Shiraz.] Blessed be he who worships God in that land; truly we, too, worshipped God there, and prayed for him who had erected that building. Thus God rewardeth the doer of good. God mentioneth those who mention Him, though it be like that, for verily He remembereth the best.

But the command to exalt the House intendeth naught but this, that those who discern signs, vindicate through this House, the House of the celebration of oneness, glorification, exaltation of divine unity, sanctification of praise, and magnification. Thus, they must erect this latter House and fix their gaze upon the Manifestations thereof, so that at the time of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, they shall not be veiled from the One Who is the Source of the sanctity of the House.

Even as it was this same Exalted Tree Who, 1270 years ago, ordained all to pilgrimage, and thus each year 70 thousands souls revolve around it. But behold how many years have passed from the Revelation of the supreme Source of the sanctity of the House, yet not even a single soul hath recognised His purpose of revealing that command, and none hath gathered fruit.

Whereas the true House of God is the hearts of His faithful, who are naught but the faithful unto Him Whom God shall make manifest. Today, it is the believers in the Bayan who act in conformity with that which is revealed in the Qur’an, and not the believers in the latter. Had the people circled around the House of Truth, the command concerning the pilgrimage of the House would not have been enjoined. Inasmuch as they have failed to do so, the necks of the creatures have been shackled with the sovereign decree that they must revolve around the dust which is attributed unto Him, that they may comprehend their limits, and in the Day of His Revelation they would not be veiled from Him.

This is the fruit of pilgrimage that they may arise to fulfil His Command, that haply in the Day of His Revelation, by the aid of such ascent, they would ascend towards Him. Alas! For the Dispensation of the Qur’an no such fruit is harvested, inasmuch as while 70 thousands souls circle around that House, at this very time the supreme Source of the sanctity of the House resideth in the mount of Maku, yet except one soul, none is present before Him! It is evident that the fruit is not gathered. In truth, it was befitting that at the time of Revelation, all the faithful in the Qur’an, who by virtue of His Command revolve so frequently around a mere dust, would revolve infinite times and until the end that hath no end, around the Command of His own Self.

How very strange that the same letter of Shin (Satan), who hath traversed the long distance to His House on foot, now pronounceth this kind of judgement against Him, and those who have spent so much of their possessions for pilgrimage to His House, now they bar Him from even a tiny piece of land to reside therein! This is the contemptible estate of the people, who have always wandered, and continue to wander, aimlessly and without the slightest trace of consciousness, and then in the day of the harvest, they seem like a dead corpse, failing to be aware of the purpose of God in His ordinances.

Awake O people of the Bayan, and be prepared for the Revelation of the supreme Source of the sanctity of the House. For He is proud of those who revolve around His House during the time of Concealment. He beholdeth them, and sendeth unto them His pardon, on the condition that on the way to pilgrimage they all treat each other with courtesy and excellent conduct.

It is thus that I myself saw, on the voyage to Mecca, a notable who was spending considerable sums of money but who hesitated to spend the price of a glass of water for his fellow-traveller. This happened on the boat where the water was scarce, so scarce in fact, during the voyage from Bushihr to Mascate, which lasted twelve days with no opportunity to get water, that I had to content myself with sweet lemons.

Take heed and watch yourselves not to grieve any one under any condition, inasmuch as the hearts of the faithful are nearer unto God than the House made out of clay. Seek ye to draw nigh unto God in His House, inasmuch as prayers therein are answered. Whoso spendeth the price of one Carat for pilgrimage, while recognising the Lord of the House, he would be recompensed two thousands in this world. And whoso can go, without being afflicted with sorrow on the way, and refuseth to go, at the hour of death his spirit would be seized from him, and will be reckoned as a believer of the previous Book.

However, nothing is more important in the path of pilgrimage, than adornment with virtuous conduct, so that should he be accompanied by another, neither he himself would be grieved, nor he would grieve the other. I have seen (on the way to Mecca) acts of the vilest kind, in the eyes of God, which were sufficient to undo the good resulting from the pilgrimage. These were the quarrels among the pilgrims! For quarrels are forbidden at all times and under any condition, and the ways of the faithful have never been, nor will ever be, aught but forbearance, patience, shame, and tranquillity. Verily, the House of God has no need of such people!

Be warned and watch yourselves that the Religion of God is wider than anything. He whose habitation is separated from the House by sea, is exempted from pilgrimage. Were he to gain sufficient means for pilgrimage, he should pay the cost thereof to a faithful soul amongst his relatives, an act which would render him exempt, while his pilgrimage would be accepted before God.

This gracious law is enjoined that the one who stepeth in the court of God would not be grieved on the way, for one cannot imagine on the sea anything but discomfort. One cannot have all the necessities as in land travel. Nay, rather, should the merchants restrain the sea voyage, it would be more conducive, in this religion, to their tranquillity, but only if that is feasible, otherwise, the order of the world will be disrupted. The mariners are obliged to live thus but by their services they come nearer to God, and God rewards actions performed on the land and on the sea but He grants a two-fold recompense for those services accomplished by one of the servants on the sea, because their work is more arduous. And this on the condition that they are faithful to the religion of God, and treat each other in accordance with the bond of love. Verily God rewardeth the doer of good.

It behoveth the sovereign of the kingdom in which the Sacred House of God lieth, nay, rather, it behoveth all the kings, to establish offices in all parts of their territory, from the beginning to the end, to carry the news and correspondences of that land from one extreme to the other. Even as in the West, such system is organised in utmost excellence, and they know of the news, which otherwise can take several months to reach, in just a few days and nights. However, it is befitting that the king would make this accessible to all, that all can be informed of the news swiftly. For He Whom God shall make manifest will assuredly be manifested, and should the means of receiving news and books be prevalent amongst all, the servants of God would attain the blessing of guidance more swiftly. Were one to hear the news of the Revelation earlier, to the extent of an infinitesimal part (a ninth of a ninth of a tenth of a tenth) of a moment, and recognise Him, it would be better for him than becoming the possessor of all that is on earth and then offering them in the path of God.

It is for this reason that such ordinance is decreed, that haply in the Day of the Revelation of that Most Mighty Day-Star, the means to facilitate the attainment of the glory of guidance for His servants would be prepared. However, until such system is universalised, its benefit would not reach those who serve the kingdom, unless there be a time that it will be accessible to all the people. Otherwise, even today the kings have their own special careers. But it is fruitless, for the poor are barred from such service.

It behoveth every sovereign to be informed of the condition of all different parts of his territory, and provide the means of information accessible to all the inhabitants, so that should there be one of the followers of that Most Mighty Day-Star in the remotest corner of that land, he would be empowered, through the system that is effective in the kingdom, to turn unto the Sun of guidance. For God verily loveth those who create order.

Gate Seventeen of the Fourth Unity

concerning this, that it is not permitted to sell the periphery of the House; which should anyone wish to exalt, he may lawfully appropriate it, even against its owner’s wishes, for God is better entitled to His property than a servant who possesseth it for a span of years.

The substance of this gate is that should any potentate wish to exalt the House, or the Sacred Mosque surrounding it – howsoever much he wisheth – it is not for anyone to allege to Him ownership thereof, for the Lord is the owner of All Things as of right: and He is best entitled to His property, for the sake of the House of His own Self. This is the command of God, which should any be displeased with, his displeasure is the pleasure of God: inasmuch as it is for him to be well pleased with that which God hath bidden him withal. Who indeed can allege to His Creator ownership of aught? God loveth the pious.

Gate Eighteen of the Fourth Unity

concerning this, that it is not permitted to ascend unto this House unless with sufficient means to avoid experiencing sorrow on the way; and that the traveller to the House should, upon his arrival, bestow four mithqals of gold upon those who serve the First, Second, Third, and Fourth Pillars of the House, that they may distribute them amongst themselves; nor are they permitted to inquire after this donation, but rather must it be offered voluntarily by those who come into their presence; and exemption is granted unto the bond slave, he that serveth on the way, minors, those who have been despoiled on the way, and those who are unable to pay it.

The substance of this gate is that the performance of pilgrimage hath not been ordained but to the end that those who ascend unto God should, in His path, delight in His good pleasure. This obligation hath been removed from those with insufficient means, so that they may not be sorrowed in His path. It hath been made incumbent upon each soul to make pilgrimage but once in a lifetime, in order that it may not be hard for him to undertake this journey. To purchase a pilgrimage for the sake of the deceased hath been forbidden, so that all, at the time of the appearance of the True One, may in their own persons attain the meeting with their Lord; and, at the time of His concealment, attain the place where He came to rest in His Former Manifestation.

In case this duty be incumbent upon a soul, if, ere travelling to the House, death overtake him – so only he had the intention of making this journey, but was unable to fulfil it, it is for God to recompense him with the finest of recompenses, and to cause him to enter Paradise with the mightiest of bestowals. He hath removed this obligation from women, in order that no hardship should befall them on the way; and He hath granted permission unto the dwellers in the land of His House, as also to those who live in the vicinity of that Place of Glory, to make pilgrimage thither once a year, for it is not hard for them as it is for others: and what soul is there, whose home is situated in the land of the Sanctuary of God, who would not wish to circle about that House?

He hath granted leave unto the travellers to His House that four mithqals of gold, by the standard of the Bayan – according to which each mithqal is nineteen nakhuds – be bestowed upon the nineteen souls who are seated upon their couches around the House: all of whom subsist in virtue of the command of Him One Who standeth as Qa’im over the Pillar of Glory, so that this observance may guide unto the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan. He hath commanded them to treat the travellers to the House of God with the utmost honour; nor should they inquire after the donation unto their Best-Beloved, in order that those charged with this obligation may discharge it of their own volition, which proceeding shall tend more nearly unto honour and exaltation.

The nineteen souls should each year dispose of the gift of God equally amongst themselves; render grateful thanks unto their Best-Beloved; and expend it upon the requisites of the “single water:” on the prescribed silks, which have been mentioned in the Arabic version; on the exquisite coloured couches (which are in the First Pillar white, in the Second yellow, in the Third green, and in the Fourth crimson); and on such beloved and peerless matters as shall conduce to the honour both of the travellers to the House and of themselves – in all of which prescriptions there have been, and are, infinite allusions in the eyes of the followers of the Truth: all of which measures are for the purpose of preparing for the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, at which time there shall be for the pilgrims no pilgrimage save unto Him; nor for the custodians of the House any custody save over Him; nor for the servants of the resting-places of the Vahid any service save unto Him; nor in any aspect of religion any command save His command. This is the intention, should anyone apprehend it.

Exemption from this offering of four mithqals gold hath been granted unto those who have not the ability to pay it; and unto bond slaves, servants, minors, and those who are afflicted on the way; through the grace and mercy of God; so that this may serve as a pattern for those charged with the performance of religious duties, in respect of the various matters which have been enjoined upon them: inasmuch as all these laws, in the eyes of their Revealer, are betwixt the “Kaf” and the “Nun:” perchance, on the Day of the appearance of their Revealer, someone may garner the fruit thereof.

In each age, for the custodians of the House of Reality there have been, and are, sanctified souls, who look into the knowledge of the hidden of the hidden, which in the Fourth Pillar is the manifest of the manifest in the First Pillar. It is for his sake that the House hath been founded; and indeed night and day to the number of eight Vahids have passed over him, during which it is to his honour that the duty to exalt the House hath been laid upon the necks of all aforetime, even as it shall be hereafter. There is no soul who hath not the law of God upon his neck, being thereby submissive unto the Primal Reality, and His manifestations of the Living, from the Day of Adam until this day. Even that soul who remaineth shut out as by a veil from the Countenance of Truth – whether he be of the highest or the lowest ranks of the people – it is by His command that night and day he boweth down; and, from the beginning to the end of his life, he is captive in the cord of obedience unto Him, nor himself knoweth this to be the case.

For example, if the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – bowed not down for the sake of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – yet the laws which had been laid upon their necks by Jesus – peace be upon Him – represent nothing other than a bowing down on their part for the sake of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – inasmuch as the Reality that was manifest in Jesus – peace be upon Him – was, in His own age, the same that was manifest in Him. Regard thou likewise the Revelation before that preceding; and view thou in the same light also the Revelation after that succeeding.

Under no circumstance hath aught ever been, or ever shall be, possessed of any substance, in respect of which it may be termed a “thing,” but that in virtue thereof it hath ever bowed down, humble, lowly, adoring, mindful – and ever shall do – for the sake of the Point of Truth; and it everlastingly worshippeth God through Him, nor itself noticeth this to be the case: for were it to recognize Him, it would, with its whole being, turn unto Him detachedly from its whole self. How unreservedly, for example, did those who recognized the Apostle of God attest their belief in Him! And how persistently did those who recognized Him not, tarry in the fire of their unperceiving state! Conceive thou likewise the Revelation before that preceding His; and view thou in the same light also the Revelation after that succeeding His. Herein is the glory of God: that all should pride themselves on their servitude unto Him, should He deign to accept it: whereas He shall accept it not, save only from those who are sincerely devoted unto Him.

One thousand two hundred and seventy years have passed since the inception of Muhammad’s Prophetic Mission, and each year endless multitudes have circled about the House. In the final year, the Founder of the House Himself went on pilgrimage, and beheld that – God be praised! – people of all denominations had come on pilgrimage; yet no one recognized Him, while He recognized them all, knowing that it was in the grasp of His previous word that they had acted, and were acting, as they did. The one who did recognize Him, and who performed pilgrimage with Him, is the same over whom eight Vahids have passed, during which the Lord hath gloried in him amidst the Concourse on high, in virtue of his detachment, and of his sincerity in His good pleasure.

It is not that he hath been made the object of any special favour. Nay, that same favour hath been vouchsafed unto all; yet they have all shut themselves out therefrom as by a veil: inasmuch as in that year of the Revelation, the Book commentating on the Surih of Joseph came into the hands of all: yet, when they looked, and saw that they had no companion in confessing their belief, they all demurred to do so; not conceiving that this same Qur’an, whose truth is now attested by so many people, had been present in the very heartland of the Arabs for seven years, while apparently no one, apart from the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – had confessed its truth. Howbeit that soul, since he had regard for that whereby the proof is constituted such, became assured of the truth of the Revelation, nor had regard for any other person.

Thus it is that on the Day of Resurrection, the Lord questioneth each soul upon his own understanding, not upon his subservience to the opinions of another. How like it is that a soul, upon hearing the Verses, may submit to them, and recognize the True One; nor follow this and that person. It is for this reason that all have been charged with responsibility for themselves, not for others. Upon the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the most learned of the learned are in the same case with the lowliest of the people. How like it is that this epitome of lowliness may confess the Truth, while that embodiment of learning may remain shut out therefrom as by a veil. Hence it is that in each Revelation, some through following others enter into the Fire.

Were each person to act according to the extent of his own understanding, those who are possessed of an unspoilt nature would at least remain unchanged; nor would they have regard for the glory of the Cause, but rather for that whereby glory is constituted such: just as the aforesaid soul, at the time of Revelation, had regard for that by which the proof is constituted such; and, even though he had no companion, yet in the sight of God he was on the true path; whereas others, who looked first to see whether they had a companion, remained shut out as by a veil, and were in that year deprived of performing the real pilgrimage, which is to recognize Him Who established the identity of the House as such.

He who recognized God and His Verses performed the pilgrimage, together with those others who in that year believed in Him; while those who circled around the House, through not confessing His truth, were judged to be other than followers of the Truth. It is not that they had not heard of the Revelation, for had this been so, they would not have been subject to any obligation; nay, they had heard of it; yet, because they heeded it not, they remained shut out as by a veil therefrom. Although in their own conceit they performed the pilgrimage in the good pleasure of God, yet in the sight of God they were shut out as by a veil from the very condition of belief, whereof the performance of pilgrimage is but one among various subsidiary aspects.

O people of the Bayan! Have mercy upon yourselves, and cause not your works to be of a sudden rendered vain. At the time of Revelation, act ye with the most scrupulous care. Thou knowest not Who is the Manifestation, for wert thou to be apprised of His identity, thou wouldst undoubtedly observe the utmost care. Howbeit, He shall be made manifest in such wise that thou shalt be able to ascertain His truth, so that the proof may stand complete before thee and before all. God is the best of judges.

Gate Nineteen of the Fourth Unity

concerning this, that the women shall at night enter the Mosque, and come before the couches, in the presence of the nineteen ladies: which provision is as touching the womenfolk in that land.

The substance of this gate is that it hath been permitted the women of that land, and its vicinity, at night to circumambulate the House; to sit beside the four couches over which are nineteen; to delight in rendering glory, sanctity, thanks, unity and grandeur unto God; and thereafter to return unto their homes. The donation of four mithqals of gold is in their case due but once in a lifetime, in respect of each of them, not on each separate occasion that they are blessed with being able to travel to the House.

That, however, which is conducive to their drawing nigh unto God is the good pleasure of their consorts, and the love of their children: to the degree that were anyone, ere discharging her obligation, to lavish upon her children whatsoever kindness and mercy she was capable of, this would weigh more greatly in her favour than any act of obedience whereby she might seek to draw nigh unto her Lord. The Lord hath commanded parents to evince towards their children the utmost love that it is possible to show them, naming such love the love of His own Self, to the honour of Him Whom God shall make manifest; while He hath commanded all children to behave towards their parents, siblings and relatives according to the standards of courtesy customary in that age, so that no dust of despondency may sit upon their hearts, to the glory of the parents of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and of His relatives.

It is for the sake of but One Soul that all are created and sustained, are caused to expire and quickened to life; and He it is Who hath ever been, and ever shall be, the Desire of all nations. In each Revelation He is made manifest with a particular name; and after His disappearance He is veiled from mortal eyes in a height of glory: for were the matter otherwise, how would it be possible to say “There is no God but God”? – inasmuch as He is a Sign that guideth unto this Word: just as this Word, which is composed of letters, guideth unto the Unity of the Lord – exalted and glorified be He – so likewise His Divine nature guideth singly and solely unto the Most Sacred Essence.

There is no God but God, and We all, verily, circle about Him.

The Fifth Unity

Gate One of the Fifth Unity: Concerning the Mosque

The substance of this gate is that the first land wherein the place of the appearance of the body of Him Whom God shall make manifest shall become apparent hath been, and is, the Sacred Mosque. The Secret of Reality hath been, and is, likewise observable in respect of the Point of the Bayan. However much the Cause of God can be exalted, it hath been, and is, befitting that this be done. A day, for example, shall arrive when the place of the clay of God Ahmad shall be established in a quarter of that Great Land, and become a spot wherein the faithful may perform their prayers: even as is today evident in the case of Mecca: for the bounds of its sanctuary were not at first to the extent witnessed today: nay, its dimensions have increased four-fold from what they originally were.

The purport of this provision is this, that if the land related unto the appearance of His body be exalted in this fashion – so that that place become a spot wherein the faithful don the garb of pilgrimage in order to circumambulate His House – what must be the case with the lands of the essential bodies that guide unto His Grandeur; the lands of the souls that guide unto His Unity; the lands of the spirits that guide unto His Thanks; and the lands of the hearts that guide unto His Glory? – whereof in the first the Fire of Love shineth forth; in the second the Air of Vicegerency is exalted; in the third the Water of Unity is ennobled; and in the fourth the Earth of Existence is elevated.

God beginneth All Things, then returneth them. Will ye not then perceive?

Gate Two of the Fifth Unity: Concerning the description of the mosques eight before ten

The substance of this gate is that it befitteth those in the Bayan who are possessed of means to construct eighteen mosques, newly and apart, in the name of the Letters of the Living of Him Whom God shall make manifest, which may serve as a guide unto the former Letters of the Living; and wherein glory, sanctity, unity and majesty may be rendered unto God. However much the lanterns in these mosques can be exalted, there hath not been, nor is there, any extravagance in this measure. Methinks I see that exalted lanterns to the number of the Name of “Mustaghath” have been suspended therein, which shine forth like unto the stars of heaven; while in that place the believers in God and His Verses have gathered, and performed their prayers.

Yet fear ye that day whereon these same Letters shall return unto the life of this world; and take heed that ye deprive them not at least of their own seats: even as occurred during the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, when all, on the authority of the Traditions related of their former selves, assumed the rôle of imam in the mosques, while denying the Imams themselves, by reason of the baseless assertions they had attributed unto them, entry into those dwellings wherein the Name of God was exalted. Whoever indeed is in the present Revelation hath noted instances of this form of proceeding: how, not content with denying them entry into the finest of mosques, they would not consent to allow them entry into the lowly among them either. Nay, they sank to yet lower depths than this, until finally there befell that which befell.

It is not that they have no proof before them: even now, these mosques are being reared in virtue of this same proof, just as they were reared aforetime in virtue of this same proof: for had not the words “He who frequenteth the mosques of God …” been revealed, how would all these mosques have been reared? Yet, these people have looked not to the essence of the argument, whence they are shut out as by a veil from recognizing the Truth. When they look, they see that a vast multitude go on pilgrimage: yet they look not to see under the shadow of what Tree they all act in this fashion, and in virtue of what proof they are content to undergo all this hardship on the way. Howbeit, since the matter hath become a source of pride, they undertake it without reflection.

In truth, however, the actions of all these people are in virtue of “… to God, as a duty upon the people, is owed a pilgrimage unto the House;” and this same Word existeth in the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, as it doth today, and as it did at the time of the revelation of the Furqan; yet when they observe that they have no companion in obeying this command, they become shut out as by a veil from the Source of the command; and only afterwards, when they find for themselves a companion, and the matter becometh a source of pride, do they all of them obey it.

Were that same soul who today goeth on pilgrimage to have lived in that day, he would not have hearkened unto the command of God, how much less obeyed it: just as today thou beholdest that this same proof existeth; yet in this wise, those who are shut out as by a veil have persisted in their unperceiving state. They travel in the streams which have branched out from the sea of the proof constituted by the Book of God; yet are shut out as by a veil from the sea itself. Thus it is that the people are adjudged to be as shadows, and those who believe on the basis of discerning insight to be as rays; while the sun is the sign of Reality itself, and is exalted above being conjoined with any mention, inasmuch as naught is seen therein but God; He, verily, is the Lord of all worlds.

Gate Three of the Fifth Unity: On true exposition of the knowledge concerning the years and the months

The substance of this gate is this, that the Lord of the universe hath fashioned all types of years by His behest, and hath ordained that from the inception of the Bayan, each year to equal the numerical value of the word all things (kullu shay’=361=19x19), to consist of nineteen months, where each month equaleth nineteen days, that from the moment of the shining forth of the sun in vernal equinox, corresponding to the first sign of Zodiac, the sign of Aries, till the end of its voyage at the end of winter, corresponding to the last sign of Zodiac, the sign of Pisces, all beings would traverse through all the nineteen stages of the Letters of Unity.

It is thus that He hath called the first month that of Baha’ (Splendour), and the last month that of ‘Ala’ (Loftiness), and hath established His religion in accordance with this same number. Thus, He hath destined each month to be the spring of one of His laws, that the inmates of this paradise may partake of divine delights in the utmost joy that is possible in the realm of creation. Therefore, in the first three months, the months of glorification, the fire of the hearts of existing beings is created, and in the next four months, the months of the celebration of praise, the spirits of the contingent beings are created, a time during which they are provided for. In the subsequent six months, which are the months of exaltation of unity, God causeth the beings to die, not a physical death, but the death from negation, and the life in affirmation. Finally, in the last six months, which are the months of magnification, the Lord of the universe, glorified and exalted be Him, quickenth those people who have died from the love for one other than Him, and have remained steadfast in His love.

The first three months are the fire of God, the next four months, the air of eternity, and the subsequent six months are the water of divine unity which streameth forth upon the souls of all things, descending from the air of eternity, an air which is in turn derived from the fire of God. The last six months pertaineth to the dust, that all that is manifested out of the three previous elements, may be preserved in the dust element, and then, the fruit would be harvested.

In like manner, all the creatures are multiplications of this unity in unity (19x19). The first month is the month of the Point, and the 18 months belonging to the Letters of the Living circle around it. Amidst all the months, the month of the Point resembleth the sun, while all other months resemble mirrors which reflect the radiant lights of that supreme month, in such wise that naught is seen in them but that month. God hath called that month the month of Baha (Splendour), meaning that therein lieth the splendour and glory of all months, and he hath singled it out for Him Whom God shall make manifest. Each of its days is related by God to one of the Letters of the Unity.

The first day, which is the day of Nawruz, is the day of “There is none other God but God.” That day is like the Point in the Bayan, out of Whom all are called into being, and unto Whom all shall return. Its Manifestation in the Dispensation of the Point of the Bayan is the Lord of the seven letters, Who is ordained by God to be the Throne of Him Whom God shall make manifest in this Revelation. For He is the One Who is shining forth in this Throne, and He is the Revealer of these glorious verses, He is the One in Whom naught is seen but God, glorified and exalted be Him, He is the First, yet not defined by it, and He is the Last, but not described by it. He is the Seen, and not praised by it, and He is Hidden, and not recognised by it, and He is the One Who is the Source of the thingness of all, while His thingness is by the grace of God.

He who is blessed in His day to witness unto divine unity 361 times, he would be guarded in that year from the afflictions which will be sent from the heaven of destiny. God verily protecteth all things.

The fruit of this knowledge is this, that just as these months, which are a mere token attribute of the creatures, have turned to naught but that which pointeth unto the Letters of the Unity, all other creatures of God should be the same, that no one would see any thingness in himself, except through the Manifestation of the Cause of God. But this should not be limited to a mere knowledge. Rather, one must harvest the result, and in the Day of the revelation of these same Manifestations, though he possesseth all earth, he would see naught in himself except these Manifestations, and submit unto Them, even if They appear, like in this Revelation, in cheap cotton-garments. This is that which profiteth the virtuous.

Gate Four of the Fifth Unity

On the ordinance concerning calling people by the Names of God, the name of Muhammad, blessings of God rest upon Him, the name of ’Ali, Their twin names, the name of Fatimih, the name of Hasan, or the name of Husayn, peace be upon Them.

The substance of this gate is this, that God hath graciously permitted His servants to call themselves by names that refer unto Him, like ’Aziz (The Almighty), and Jabbar (The All-Compelling), and the like of them. But the best names are the names that would indicate relation unto God, like Baha’u’llah (Glory of God), Jalalu’llah (Splendour of God), Jamalu’llah (Beauty of God), Nuru’llah (Light of God), Fadlu’llah (Grace of God), Judu’llah (Bounty of God), and similar Exalted names, as well as ’Abdu’llah (Servant of God) and Dhikru’llah (Remembrance of God). This type of naming is a gate that one can ascend therein endlessly.

Should one desire to choose a name in the sea of prophethood, guardianship, or love, he should limit his choice to one of the five names. However, the combination of the names Muhammad and ’Ali is the most mighty name, and the most wondrous sign.

But the divine Cycle shall advance in stages, until such Revelation when all things will be called by the Names of God, that no name would be assigned to anything unless it resembleth one of the Names of God, glorified and exalted be Him, like halim (forbearing), which is a food, but resembleth a name of God, lauded and magnified be Him. It is thus that in this Cycle of the Bayan there shall be made many constructions like this, even such permission is granted unto all. For in the Day of the Revelation of the Sun of Truth, should people attain the utmost limit of perfection, they shall not call anything except by a name that is like one of the Names of God, glorified and exalted be Him. And if such level of perfection would not be attained, it assuredly will happen in the Revelation subsequent thereof.

This will happen in stages and gradually, until all heaven, earth, and that which lieth between them, would be filled with the Names of God. What difference it maketh, whether a dust refereth unto God or a man doeth so, for both are His creatures, except that the former is created for the latter. For God hath invested the human spirit with the spirit of the celebration of God’s unity by all things. For example, should a faithful sit on a land, the spirit of that land would attain utmost tranquillity and delight. On the other hand, should a non-believer sit thereon, it would be sore-vexed to such a degree that none can reckon it but God, and it ceaselessly beseecheth God to remove him therefrom. Thus the example of dust was given that thou wouldst be able to ponder the same principle in regard to all things.

Well is it with the people of that age, who call nothing but by a Name of God. That Age is worthy to be praised as the beginning of the worlds of paradise!

No created thing shall ever attain its paradise unless it appeareth in its highest prescribed degree of perfection. For instance, this crystal representeth the paradise of the stone whereof its substance is composed. Likewise there are various stages in the paradise for the crystal itself… So long as it was stone it was worthless, but if it attaineth the excellence of ruby—a potentiality which is latent in it—how much a carat will it be worth? Consider likewise every created thing. Man’s highest station, however, is attained through faith in God in every Dispensation and by acceptance of what hath been revealed by Him, and not through learning; inasmuch as in every nation there are learned men who are versed in divers sciences. Nor is it attainable through wealth; for it is similarly evident that among the various classes in every nation there are those possessed of riches. Likewise are other transitory things.

True knowledge, therefore, is the knowledge of God, and this is none other than the recognition of His Manifestation in each Dispensation. Nor is there any wealth save in poverty in all save God and sanctity from aught else but Him—a state that can be realised only when demonstrated towards Him Who is the Dayspring of His Revelation. This doth not mean, however, that one ought not to yield praise unto former Revelations. On no account is this acceptable, inasmuch as it behooveth man, upon reaching the age of nineteen, to render thanksgiving for the day of his conception as an embryo. For had the embryo not existed, how could he have reached his present state? Likewise had the religion taught by Adam not existed, this Faith would not have attained its present stage. Thus consider thou the development of God’s Faith until the end that hath no end.

Render then thanks unto God through each one of His Revelations in each Dispensation, inasmuch as that is a thanksgiving unto God which is beloved in His sight. God guideth unto the absolute path of truth, whomsoever He willeth.

The fruit of this ordinance is this, that by virtue of continuos remembrance of these names, ye would not leave the shadow of Those Who bear these names, that haply in this Revelation one may become, through his attraction unto He Who beareth his name, worthy of being a name sign who would solely point unto Him Whom God shall make manifest.

But be warned lest thou be shut out as by a veil, by virtue of a mere name, inasmuch as in this Cycle, the one who martyred the Prince of the Martyrs, peace be upon Him, appeared by the very same name of that Essence of Holiness, and there is no doubt that in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, all would be called by these beloved names. However, only he who shall remain firm in pointing unto Him, will be His name, for his inmost reality is fashioned out of the ocean of His bounty, who is worthy to be called by a most excellent name. Otherwise, he is a shadow of blatant error, beneath the nether ground, who shall perish in negation.

Thou hast witnessed in this Day of Resurrection, that myriad of souls were called by the name of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, which no name can surpass it in the world of creation, and yet they were veiled from their Beloved. God is a witness unto all things.

Know thou that He Whom God shall make manifest resembleth the touchstone which separateth pure gold from all besides it. For example, if one be called by the supreme name Baha’u’llah, and He recognise His Baha, Who is the First to recognise Him, then of all names, this name would be registered for him. Otherwise he would perish in negation, as if there hath never been any mention of him.

Gate Five of the Fifth Unity

in explanation of the ordinance concerning the expropriation of the possessions of those who believe not in the Bayan; and the ordinance concerning the restitution thereof, should they enter the fold of the religion; save in countries where such expropriation would not be possible.

The substance of this gate is that in each Revelation all that is on earth must fall beneath the shadow of the succeeding Revelation. For example, in the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – it was fitting that all who were on earth should have become believers beneath His shadow: and if, as proved to be the case, some came not beneath His shadow, this was on account of the frailty of the Muslims, for otherwise, the fitness for this to occur existed in that religion.

On the Day of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – the very soul of each person living was not lawful to him, how much less that which is subordinate to life; unless he entered the fold of belief in Him, at which time whatsoever the Lord had, out of His bounty, bestowed upon him would have become lawful to him. In like manner, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, no soul shall be lawful to its possessor unless he believe in Him. All shall be taken away from all, unless they enter beneath the shadow of His religion: and this is a token of the bounty of the Lord in respect of His creation.

For example, whatever countries, at the beginning of Islam, were conquered by force and coercion, thereby entered the fold of Islam, and attained the fruit of belief; and if, as proved to be the case, some remained without its fold, this was not a mercy to them, inasmuch as they have tarried until now in the Fire. Similarly in this Revelation, that which is related to other than the believers in the True One is not lawful to them; unless they enter within the fold of belief, at which time whatsoever the Lord hath, out of His bounty, bestowed upon them shall become lawful to them.

This ordinance, however, devolveth upon those sovereigns who are invested with power in the religion, not upon all the believers; nor hath the Lord permitted it to be implemented in any country where this might occasion sorrow or injury to any soul: as, for example, in the case of merchants with commercial dealings in the lands of the Franks, who should keep their accounts with the utmost scrupulousness, lest any abasement should befall them: unless the Lord should assist His Cause with a power sufficient to prevail over all who are on earth, according as He hath promised: at which time, all shall dwell within the pale of God’s mercy. Although they themselves abhor it, yet the power of God shall cause them to enter therein, and, delivering them from the Fire, convert them into light; and God is powerful over All Things.

It is not that those invested with power should wait for a prodigy to descend from heaven such as would cause all who are on earth to enter into the fold of the religion. Nay, just as in the religion of Islam, all entered therein in virtue of that which had been promulgated through the command of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – so likewise in every Revelation, things must be realized in this same manner. That which is requisite on the part of God is to grant permission; but that which is incumbent on the part of His creatures is to render Him obedience. Had, indeed, those potentates who existed in the religion of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – acted according to the precepts of the Qur’an, today all who are on earth would be believers in the Qur’an; and if this be not now the case, the shortcoming is on the part of His servants: inasmuch as that which it was incumbent should be promulgated from the Source, was revealed in the Qur’an. God assisteth whomsoever He willeth, and God is the All-Powerful, the Almighty.

The fruit of this ordinance is that on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, all should have been so schooled in the Bayan that none of the believers therein would depart from the fold of belief in Him; which if he did, he would be adjudged as one who had disbelieved in God. I swear by the Sacred Essence of God that if, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, all should combine to assist Him, there shall remain on earth no soul – nay, naught whatsoever – that shall not enter into Paradise. Be ye watchful of yourselves, inasmuch as the whole of religion is to render Him assistance, not to perform the works prescribed in the Bayan, at the time of His appearance; notwithstanding that ere His advent, whosoever departeth therefrom by so much as a barley seed shall have infringed against His command.

Seek ye refuge in God from that which keepeth you remote from the Source of Command; and cleave unto His cord, for whosoever cleaveth unto obedience to Him hath attained, and shall attain, deliverance in all the worlds. This is a token of the grace of God: He bestoweth it upon whomsoever He willeth; and the grace of God is infinite.

Gate Six of the Fifth Unity

concerning the disposal of the possessions that are expropriated in this religion: if there be aught among them that is peerless in its kind, none shall possess it save the Point of the Bayan; and if the Sun have set, let it be carefully preserved up to the Sunrise, by one engaged in commerce, not other than he; while as touching the remainder, after the number “Ha’” have first been levied from the value (Baha’) of the whole thereof, let the conquerors take therefrom, by the leave of their commander, each so much as shall satisfy his need; after which, if there remain a surplus, let this be distributed among the poor, and expended upon the shrines; and should it be bestowed upon each soul – though it be an infant in its mother’s womb – this is better than that it should be expended upon the shrines, as a bounty from God: He, verily, is the All-Bountiful, the Most High.

The substance of this gate is that whensoever the Lord of the world favoureth the believers with the conquest of a country which had not chosen to submit to His Cause, whatsoever is peerless in its kind hath been, and is, the right of the Point. For as long as the Sun of Truth shineth, it reverteth unto Him; and if the Sun setteth, it should be deposited with trustees from among the believers in the Bayan until the Day of the appearance of the True One, when they should return unto Him Whom God shall make manifest that which is in their possession.

Unto none is it permitted to dispose thereof: in the manner, for example, that the divines have appropriated, and disposed of, the property of the Proof of God without His leave: notwithstanding that if they have disposed of so much as a single qirat thereof, their recompense for doing so is the Fire. All Things are “for God:” and who is nearer unto the Lord than the Point of the Will? Howsoever much of the right of the Proof of the Lord aforetime anyone was indebted withal, not a single qirat thereof is lawful unto him; and should he have given it unto another, it is to no avail, although it was unto the most learned of the people of that age; and he hath squandered the right of the Proof, inasmuch as he hath given it unto another without His leave; and both the giver and the taker are in the Fire, for the Possessor thereof is living, and is better entitled to that thing which the Lord hath bestowed upon Him as a bounty in the Qur’an than any other person.

He is rich enough to dispense with wealth itself – how much more with one who is unable to enrich himself, unless through wealth. Notwithstanding, whosoever wisheth to deliver himself from the Fire will of his own accord render this due; for otherwise the Proof of the Lord hath ever been, and ever shall be, all-possessing. It is from the ocean of His bounty that all have been brought into existence – how, then, must stand the case with that which is subordinate to existence? Today, which is the Day of Resurrection, inquiry is made of a divine: “Thou didst expend a thousand, thousand of the property of the Proof upon the construction of a mosque – by whose leave didst thou so?”

This very question is more grievous unto him than any torment, in the eyes of those endowed with understanding, should the spirit of faith be in him; for otherwise, thousands upon thousands are they who might hear the Verse “All Things are doomed to perish, except His Countenance,” without, methinks, having hearkened unto a single word thereof. In the eyes of him who recognizeth God, however, it would be better, though all that is on earth were his, to give it up, than that on the Day of Resurrection he should be questioned concerning a matter wherein lay the displeasure of his Best-Beloved.

Apart from that which is peerless in its kind, an amount to the value (Baha’) of “Ha’” is to be levied on the whole, and applied, on the part of the Letters of the Vahid, to the propagation of the people of the Bayan, from the highest ranks thereof down to the lowest. Thereafter, the victorious commander shall bestow upon himself, and the companions of his triumph – each according to his station, and as is fitting in his particular case – a portion of the bounty of his Best-Beloved. If there remain a surplus, this should be expended upon the designated shrines; or else a share should be bestowed upon all the people of the Bayan – though it be a six-month-old infant in its mother’s womb – whether in the East of the earth or the West thereof: which latter course is nearer unto the good pleasure of God than that it should be expended upon the shrines, should these have been already exalted; for otherwise the exaltation thereof should be accorded precedence. Such is the command of the Lord in this respect.

The fruit thereof is that on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest – setting aside that whatever substance all who are on earth possess – in respect whereof they are entitled to the designation “thing” – is from Him, the people of the Bayan should nevertheless recognize the Right of God: insomuch as whatever, from the beginning of the revelation of the Bayan, hath come into their possession, is in virtue of His bounty ere yet He had appeared, whether as touching their spiritual condition or their worldly estate. Be ye abashed a little, that no sorrow may come upon Him from His servants. Deprive Him not of the rights which the Point of Truth hath destined for Him, of all that is peerless in its kind, inasmuch as such a thing can belong of right to none but Him, for He is the Sign of “There is naught like unto Him” of the Lord.
