Whatsoever thing arriveth at the stage of meriting this description, at its own level, is fitting but for Him, not for another; from the pinnacle of exaltation at one extreme, down to the lowest depth of abasement at the other: haply, at the time of His appearance, His blessed nature shall be occasioned no sorrow by the creatures who were brought into existence through His bounty: for His sorrow cannot be compared with the sorrow of All Things, inasmuch as All Things have derived from Him their substance, in respect whereof they are entitled to the designation “thing;” and similarly His good pleasure cannot be compared with the good pleasure of All Things, inasmuch as the good pleasure of All Things hath been brought into existence through Him.

I swear by Him – than Whom in the knowledge of the Lord there hath not been, nor is there, one greater – that a single look of His eye is greater in the sight of God than the works of All Things, even should they have arrived at the highest limit of their potential: inasmuch as the very existence of all is realized through Him – how, then, must stand the case with their works? This same principle of superiority on the grounds of merit is true likewise of all the degrees of creation, the nearest taking precedence over the nearer: of the Letters of the Living; then the Names and Likenesses; then the prophets, saints, witnesses and favoured ones: all, to the degree that hath been destined for them – all have their assigned degrees on the part of their Lord; and all worship Him.

Should it not be possible for the trustees of the Bayan to preserve intact the sign of “There is naught like unto Him,” and it becometh changed, it is incumbent upon them to preserve the value (Baha’) thereof; to trade with it on behalf of its Owner; and to appropriate as their own rights a hundred out of every thousand, in order that this may become customary among all, so that by this practice all may profit from all. Nor is it to be imagined, if the Proof of the Lord proceedeth thus, that anyone else would venture to exceed this limit, inasmuch as all grace hath resided, and resideth, in His laws.

There is no strength or power but in God, the Most Exalted, the Most Great.

Gate Seven of the Fifth Unity

concerning this, that God hath permitted those who believe in the Bayan to effect purchases, of all manner of things, from those who have not believed in this religion: inasmuch as the object of such a transaction, upon leaving the possession of the one, and entering into the possession of the other, becometh pure, in honour of its relation to this religion.

The substance of this gate is that the Lord hath bestowed upon the people of the Bayan a bounty such that, were they to give all that is on earth, they would have no way to obtain it: which is this, that He hath rendered pure whatsoever one may buy and sell – and beyond this, gifts of various kinds – in virtue merely of their being severed from their relation with other than the believers in the Bayan, and introduced into a relation with the believers.

For example, if one of the Christians have in his hand a rose, merely by his bestowing this upon a believer, it is at once rendered pure; and if he transfer it to him in a business dealing, so long as it is in his hand, it remaineth in its former state; whereas at the very instant of its transference, it becometh pure. Even should a cause of separation intervene – as in the case that a non-believing soul send a gift to a believer – from the moment of his stating “This is for such-and-such a believer,” it becometh pure, albeit several years elapse ere it arrive in the possession of that believing soul.

The Lord hath granted leave that whatever goodly thing there be in any land, the believers in the Bayan may acquire it: haply, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, some object may come into the presence of Him Who is the Lord of the existence of all creatures that is beloved in His sight: for however much refinement appeareth in the world, it is but a sprinkling from the ocean of the refinement of His bounty.

God – glorified and exalted be He – cannot in truth be characterized by refinement: He, verily, is too great and glorious to be described by that which can be conjoined with another than Himself: for His refinement is not conjoinable with the refinement of His creatures. So reason ye in respect of all Names and Likenesses.

Gate Eight of the Fifth Unity

ordaining that each soul should recite the Verses of the Bayan, and the impermissibility that these should be less than the number Vahid; and that whoso is unable to do so should repeat nineteen times “God, God is my Lord, and I associate no partner with God, my Lord.”

The substance of this gate is this: Imagine thou the creation of the Bayan to be like unto the believers therein, each one of whom standeth in a particular station, and appeareth in a particular guise; and so too regard thou the Verses of the Bayan. Immerse thyself in this ocean howsoever much thou wishest, and bring forth therefrom the pearls that the Lord hath created in its depths. Yet, do thou read it in a spirit of joy and radiance. Pursue thy recitation only for so long as thine heart delighteth therein; howbeit, permission hath not been granted for the recitation of a lesser number of Verses than nineteen. The secret thereof is this, that one should not stray beyond the manifestations of the Vahid: haply, through the blessing of the guidance obtained through the recitation of these Verses, on the day of Resurrection ye may be guided through their guidance.

Conceive thou the whole of the Bayan to be like unto a lump of capital, which one person bestoweth upon another to employ in trade. The owner thereof is He Whom God shall make manifest, Who hath deposited it with the believers in the Point of the Bayan, that they may trade withal, for the sake of the Day of His own appearance; when, should He wish to recover His capital, let none ask Him why or wherefore. In respect of each fine detail thereof innumerable souls are engaged in commerce: even as today thou beholdest, if someone studieth the question of the purity of the Qur’an, how he maketh it the stock in trade both of his worldly and of his spiritual estate! Yet on the Day of the appearance of its Possessor, when He wisheth to settle His account with men, all afflict themselves with blindness. Picture thou the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest – Who hath set on foot this Paradise – as that whereon He garnereth its fruits. Conceive thou one of its fruits to be a sovereign; another a divine; and another a merchant; and apply this same conceit to all categories of men.

On the Day of Revelation – whereon thou shalt thyself be present – deprive not Him Who is the Possessor of thy very existence – and of all that is subordinate thereto – of His own property: inasmuch as thou shalt behold that Day also to be like unto the present day in the Bayan: one shall say “I am a judge of the Bayan;” another “I am a Shaykhu’l-Islam;” another “I am a mujtahid;” and yet another “I am an Imam-Jum’ih:” and all shall take pride in these titles, yet be shut out as by a veil from their Possessor, from Whom these names have been diffused abroad: for on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the Bayan shall be recited to an illimitable extent: yet those who recite it shall be shut out as by a veil from its Revealer.

They imagine not, however, that as it was with the revelation of the Bayan, so too shall it be at the time of His Revelation; even as, although they have heard how it was at the time of the revelation of the Qur’an, still they garner not the fruit. Because today they behold it to be honoured, all make this honour the title of their own pride: yet it was this same Qur’an whereof – having come down over a period of twenty-three years – it is evident that until that day not a single fitting copy had been produced, for otherwise the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – would not have taken it in his blessed robe to the mosque in the manner that is recorded. I swear by the Most Sacred Essence of God – glorified and exalted be He – that should anyone, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest – hearken unto, and recite, a single Verse of His, it would be better than to recite the Bayan one thousand times.

Ponder the matter a while in the light of reason, and ye shall see that today whatsoever there is in Islam reverteth stage by stage until it endeth in the Source, which is the Book of God. Regard thou in like manner the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, when the beginning of the proof shall be held in His hand, and allow not baseless matters to shut thee out as by a veil from Him, for He is exalted above them: inasmuch as all aspects of the proof branch out from the Book of God; while the proof itself consisteth in the Book, inasmuch as all are powerless to produce its like. Otherwise there are thousands upon thousands of professors of logic, syntax, grammar, jurisprudence, juridical principles, and the like who, should they believe not in the Book of God, a sentence of other than belief would be passed upon them one and all. The fruit, then, resideth in the proof itself, not in the matters branching out therefrom.

Know thou that in the Bayan no letter hath been sent down, but that the intention thereof is to inculcate obedience unto Him Whom God shall make manifest: for it is He Who revealed the Bayan ere yet He had been made manifest.

Should ye be unable to recite the Verses, repeat ye nineteen times between the dawn of one day and the next “God, God is my Lord, and I associate no partner with God, my Lord:” should ye pronounce the which with discerning insight, without doubt ye shall on the Day of Resurrection be guided through the guidance of the True One, and the recompense of the whole of the Bayan shall be the meed thereof.

God bestoweth His grace upon whomsoever He willeth among His servants; He, verily, is possessed of grace abounding.

Gate Nine of the Fifth Unity

On this, that whenever one desireth to use anything, he should mention thereupon one of the names of God, inwardly, manifestly, or by awareness.

The substance of this gate is this, that inasmuch as nothing possesseth thingness except through the grace of God, glorified and exalted be Him, and that a day is destined for each thing to attain unto its utmost perfection, when all its potentialities would be manifestly actualised, and it is only then that it is worthy to be called by a name of God, within its own limit, and not the limit of that which is above it, and inasmuch as God hath commanded the people of the Bayan to elevate all things unto their uttermost limit of perfection, therefore, He hath granted them permission to call everything, through the letters of their names, by the Names of God, lauded and magnified be Him, that none would see in anything aught but the Countenance of the Revelation of the Will, in Whom naught is seen but God.

For example the lowest rank in the mineral kingdom is that of the stone (sang, consisting of three Arabic letters s, n, and g). Then in its letter Sin (s) naught would be seen but the All-Glorious (subbuh), in its letter Nun (n), the Light (nur), and in the letter Kaf (k, g) the All-Bountiful (karim), whether it would be mentioned by words, or conceived in the heart, or by awareness thereof, without either uttering in word or conceiving in heart. And should he be unable to do so, he should mention “In the Name of God, the Most Exalted, the Most Holy,” and God, glorified and exalted be Him, will accept from him that which He hath intended of this ordinance, that naught would be seen in anything except Him Whom God shall make manifest, Who is the Source of the Names and Attributes of God, that haply in the day of the Revelation of that Sun of Truth, no possessor of identity claim any identity of himself, and would not behold in himself aught but Him, inasmuch as he hath always been, and will forever continue to be, dependent in his existence upon Him.

Take heed that this implieth not that one can see His reality in himself. Nay, rather, everyone resembleth a mirror which is facing the sun. He witnesseth the sun within himself, but only the shadow of the true sun. When faced with Him Whom God shall make manifest, regard all that is called a thing, from the uttermost world of detachment, till the nethermost realm of limitation, in the same manner, inasmuch as any excellence that is possessed by any one is due to the shadow of the Sun of His Revelation in His previous Revelation. For there hath never been, nor will ever be, any One manifest except Him.

It is thus that in the day of His manifestation, he loveth to behold in His knowledge, that all have ascended to their utmost limit of perfection in the Bayan, and that there is no atom of dust in the nethermost depth of the sea, except that it hath come under His possession through the faithful, amongst His beloved creation, and thus all have become pure mirrors, capable of reflecting the revelation of the Sun, so that upon the shining forth of His radiant lights, which are His verses, all would refer unto Him. This is the fruit of this law, should anyone but ponder. God verily illumineth the hearts of His righteous servants.

Gate Ten of the Fifth Unity

Verily God hath ordained the Temples for men and the Circles for women, to inscribe therein that which they desire from the Bayan.

The substance of this gate is this, that God hath ordained two mighty bounties for the people of the Bayan, and graciously hath favoured them therewith. Unto men is conferred the temple, whose manifest aspect is the letter Ha’ (5), and whose inner side is the letter Vav (6). It is permitted to inscribe therein that which hath shone forth from the Sun of the Point, that every one is empowered to obtain that which he can, out of the sea of His bounty. For the effect of that which is written down in that temple, would be manifested in the soul of that person, letter by letter, and point by point.

And unto women (manifestations of the letter Ba ), the circle of the Countenance of the Sun of Truth is conferred, ordaining it to be five unities (5x19=95), and each unity (19) a unity (1), that it would refer to the letters of the word “for God” (lillah=95), confirming that “Verily all that is in the heavens, on earth, and in that which lieth between them, is for God. God embraceth all things,” so that the Countenance of the Sun of Truth may shine upon their very hearts, that haply in the Day of the Revelation of that Most Mighty Day-Star, they would not point unto aught but Him.

Thus He hath granted them permission to inscribe therein of the words that have dawned from the Sun of Existence, that which they desire, inasmuch as the effect of whatever they write therein, would be manifested in that soul, letter by letter and point by point. The original form of this circle hath proceeded in the manner that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon Him, hath mentioned the Names that is derived from the letter Ha’. Thus from the point, the name Ever-Living (Hayy), from the first derivative of the point, the name Self-Subsistent (Qayyum), from the letter Alif, the name Sovereign (Sultan), and from the letter Jim, the name Holy (Quddus) is derived. But for that reason in this Revelation He hath revealed the principle of “In the Name of God, the Most Exalted, the Most Holy,” that from the station of the point till that of the letter Jim, all the four stages of creation, provision, death, and life would be encompassed. Therefore, should anyone act in conformity with that which hath proceeded from that Ocean of Bounty, he would witness the realisation of his goals, on the condition that the Will of God hath destined their fulfilment.

The fruit of these two commands is that all comprehend that all the Bayan equaleth the creation of the Greater world, by virtue of its manifestation through temple or circle, without exceeding the limit of the letter Ha’ (5), so that in the first five years of the manifestation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, they would be blessed with the utmost bounty of recognising that Sun of Truth. For all that is written in the temples and the circles is naught but His praise and His sanctification from all that is uttered by those against Him.

But should anyone who is blessed with the possession of temple or circle, which is the bestowal of His grace, fail to manifest the fruit of that which is inscribed in the five lines, the six concentric circles, or the nineteen chambers, no mention of such fruit would be made for him or her. For such a person hath brought to naught the fruit of his own existence. All these is simply for this purpose, that none of the people of the Bayan would transgress the limits of five , inasmuch as in the temple five embraceth the letter Vav (6), and in the circle, the letter Vav preserveth the letter Ha’ (5).

This is the goal of their revelation, that haply at the time of the manifestation of that Sun of Eternity and the Ancient Countenance, all people attain such height that the possessors of temples would be wholly detached unto Him within five (letter Ha’), and the possessors of circle would do likewise within six (the letter Vav). Though should the Cycle advance, five years would be reduced to five months, nay rather, to five weeks, or five days, or five hours, or five minutes, or even five times of a tenth of a ninth, or whatever that can be mentioned in swiftness of nearness unto Him. For between the Will and that which is fashioned by Him, there is no distinction of separation. Rather, God hath always created between them the distinction of description, like the distinction between fire and its burning. Can it be that fire is flamed but it faileth to burn, or that the lamp is lighted, and yet its lights fail to illumine the place in which it is lighted? Ponder, in like manner, all the appropriate examples from the uttermost essence of existence to the nethermost rank of limitation.

Gaze not, at any time, upon all these temples and circles, except as one single Temple, even as at this very moment thou beholdest naught in the entire Qur’an but the Temple of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him. For had it not been for Him, naught thereof would have been generated, be it the faith in Him, in His Manifestations, and in all that is revealed from God unto Him. In like manner, in each Revelation, behold with the eyes of certitude, this Indivisible One Essence that streameth forth within the inner reality of all things. Therefore, in the Day of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, should anyone witness in a temple aught but His Temple, he hath been veiled from Him, though He is more manifest unto him than the manifestation of his self unto himself. And whatever he doeth, even at the time of being veiled from Him, he desireth naught but Him! This is the meaning of the phrase, “unto God shall return every Cause,” could ye but comprehend.

Gate Eleven of the Fifth Unity

concerning the Prayer for the Newborn and the Dead: five salutations are to be uttered in the Prayer for the Newborn, whereupon is to be recited, after the first, nineteen times “We all, verily, believe in God;” and for the second, “We all, verily, are well assured in God;” and after the third salutation, “We all, verily, bear life in God;” and after the fourth, “We all, verily, bear death in God;” and after the fifth, “We all, verily, are well pleased in God;” while in the Prayer for the Dead six salutations are to be uttered, whereupon is to be recited nineteen times after the first “We all, verily, worship God;” and for the second, “We all, verily, bow down before God;” and for the third, “We all, verily, are devoted unto God;” and for the fourth, “We all, verily, give praise unto God;” and for the fifth, “We all, verily, yield thanks unto God;” and for the sixth, “We all, verily, are patient in God.”

The substance of this gate is this, that whatever law the Lord of the world hath sent down on His own behalf is a bestowal on His part for Him Whom God shall make manifest; while all in consequence come beneath the shelter of the shadows of the laws of God.

Amongst the laws to which this observation is applicable, He hath granted leave that upon the birth of each infant – whether male or female – prayers should be offered up in its presence, through the utterance of five salutations, so that the Name of God may be pronounced upon it: perchance, should it survive, and attain the Day of Resurrection, it may become one of the believers in Him Whom God shall make manifest.

He hath ordained too the utterance, at the time of a person’s ascension unto his abode, of six salutations in a single prayer, so that this may betoken that, as his beginning was from “Ha’,” so his return is unto “Vav:” perchance, on the Day of Resurrection, he may believe in the First to believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest, nor allow worldly affairs to shut him out as by a veil from Him: inasmuch as this matter is in the utmost degree perplexing for those who do not truly recognize the Unity of God.

Who knoweth but that the soul in question may be unknown, while all regard themselves as “known:” even as was the case in the Revelation of the Furqan when, after the ascension of the Tree of Truth, none remained steadfast in belief in that Soul of Divinity save only the select number which is apparent. Notwithstanding, all continued to perform the works prescribed in the Qur’an; whereas a verdict of other than belief was passed upon them at the beginning of Islam by that selfsame soul.

Picture thou the case to be in this wise also with the Point of the Bayan, in the sense that whoever entereth the Gate (Bab), through the Gate (Bab) – on the basis of discerning insight – attaineth salvation, by this act, not by other acts: inasmuch as this is a Soul from Whom is realized the beginning of All Things through God; and unto Whom is realized likewise the return of all things through God. How few are those souls who, from the time of the appearance of the Tree of the Bayan, looked at their own understanding, and were shielded therefrom as by a veil: whereas in the sight of God all had been charged with that which they were charged withal. In the eyes of the Lord “higher” and “lower” have ever been, and ever shall be, on an equal footing.

If today, as thou observest, all believe in the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – it is because they have beheld naught different; nor have they been reared in other than his love: otherwise, were these same souls to have lived at the beginning of Islam, thou wouldst have beheld but those same solitary three who, according to the Traditions, were alone exempted from unbelief. In this Dispensation, for example, when the Lord hath shown His favour unto the believers, manifestations of love to the number of the Name “Rahman” have been raised up in His Cause: yet this was in virtue of the Point Himself; for had the testing of the people ended in Him, it would have become evident that the true believer is rarer than the philosopher’s stone.

The command to perform these Prayers is to the end that should one be living in the Day of Resurrection, one would not be shut out as by a veil: for afterwards, all shall accept the Truth; but on the Day whereon the fruit is garnered, it is made apparent how hard it is for all that dwell on earth to enter, through the agency of a soul who hath not even a cord to tie about his robe, within the fold of belief in the Lord. Whatsoever thou hast heard concerning the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – it was not thyself that was tested; and for as long as thou hast had eyes to see, thou hast beheld his golden dome, and the respect in which he is held by all: yet hadst thou lived in his day, and made one of those aforesaid three, then wouldst thou be true in thy belief. In reality, however, the people of that day were not used even to speak of Salman, Abu Dharr and Miqdad in respectful terms. This is the source of difference in every Revelation.

Blessed the soul who looketh to that whereby the proof is constituted such: for then, swifter than the twinkling of an eye, all that dwell on earth would – if they so wished it – enter into Paradise, through the Gates thereof; and would behold the breadth of the Sirat to be broader than that which is between the heaven of receptivities and the earth of things accepted. At all events, be ye watchful of your selves lest, in the tests that are sent of the Lord, your foot should stumble; and cleave ye tenaciously unto the cord of the Book, which is a guide unto the whole company of the righteous.

God beginneth All Things, then returneth them; and unto God, verily, shall all return.

Gate Twelve of the Fifth Unity: Concerning the burial of the dead in marble sarcophagi, and the placing of agate rings upon their hands

The substance of this gate is this, that since this outer body is the throne of that inner body – so that whatsoever may be destined for the former, the latter too will be implicated in its fate (for otherwise, that which experienceth delight or pain is it, in this body, not this body itself) – it is for this reason – namely, that this body was once the throne of that – that the Lord hath decreed in respect thereof that it be preserved to the utmost extent possible, so that it may be spared whatsoever might cause it abhorrence. For the essential body, upon its throne, looketh upon this body: and should it behold that this hath been honoured, it shall seem as though it too hath been honoured; whereas, should it behold the reverse, there shall befall it that which shall befall it. It is for this reason that the command hath been given for it to be honoured and respected to the highest degree.

Leave hath been granted for it to be concealed in crystal or polished stone, lest it behold aught in its throne such as might cause abhorrence unto its essential body. This is the fruit of this command. In this wise, God showeth His favour unto whomsoever He willeth among His servants; He, verily, is the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting.

Leave hath been granted for the wearing of an agate ring, so that, through the blessing of the Verse inscribed thereupon, no sorrow may befall that essential body, and it may be shielded from the Fire, and repose in the shadow of the Light. Whosoever hath upon his hand a ring whereon the Name of God hath been inscribed – should he be of those who believe in the Bayan, and act according to its precepts – it behoveth the Lord to cause him to enter into His gardens, and to favour him with His grace and bounty in such measure that he shall be contented: “and who is there that telleth more truthful tidings than God,” if ye be confirmed believers in God and His Verses?

The fruit of this law is this, that since the return of all is unto the manifestations of Grandeur – in respect of which reference is made to the element Earth; and since the ultimate limit of the ascent of Earth is, in the first degree, stone: after which it continueth to develop until it arriveth at the utmost limit of purity, which is the crystalline state – at which time the Name “Samad” (“Ever-Abiding”) is made apparent in its case: haply, at the time of their return, all shall repose in such ethereal essential bodies, and guide unto the True One through betokening His Grandeur. God guideth whomsoever He willeth through His command; He, verily, is the Almighty, the Most High.

Gate Thirteen of the Fifth Unity: Concerning the will of the deceased, according to the law of the Bayan

The substance of this gate is that there hath never been a greater bounty on the part of God unto His servants than this, that He hath granted them leave to worship Him, and hath taught them the expressions of His Glory, Thanks, Unity and Grandeur. He hath granted leave, at the time of death, for a will to be written, comprising an acknowledgement of His Unity, and Justice; a recognition that His are the creation and the Command; a confession of belief in the Divine Point, and His Letters of the Living; an attestation of love for the manifestations of His Names and Likenesses; a disavowal of all that his, the testator’s, Best-Beloved hath not, and doth not, love; and a statement of what he wisheth from the Object of his desire.

He should instruct that the document be delivered to Him Whom God shall make manifest, Whose reply thereto – should He please to vouchsafe one – is the same which hath been sent down for him by God. The preservation thereof is with his heirs, so that, having been passed from hand to hand, it may arrive at Him Whom God shall make manifest, in the finest script and most exquisite beauty: for the length of the period from one Revelation until the next is apparent – being the interval between the two – and the preservation of that which is between them is, for all, the easiest of all things.

Yet should the utmost care be taken lest – God forbid – the True One be made manifest, and he that is charged with this duty be shut out as by a veil from Him; or else fail to deliver the document in his possession. For this circumstance is evident, that upon the appearance of the True One each soul is beguiled by some matter; yet he knoweth not that the source of his beguilement is from that True One Himself, in His Former Manifestation, which, in His Latter Manifestation, He attributeth not unto Himself, in virtue of the exaltation of His own Revelation: as in the case of the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – Who spake of the Revelation of Jesus – peace be upon Him – as a preliminary to His own; neither did He make Himself known unto all in the name of that Revelation.

Otherwise, there is no doubt that the people of the Bayan have acted, as they shall continue to act, with unexceptionable propriety according to the precepts whereon their faith is founded: yet how they react when the day cometh for reaping a result is the point in question. For example, all, in the article of death, confess “There is no God but God,” and go their way; and in this Revelation, the embodiment of kingship, who repeateth this Word obedient to His previous command, shall repeat it also at the time of death; even while the Manifestation of this Word, Who guideth unto God, is concealed unjustly in a mountain. Thus it is that all works become as scattered dust.

In this manner, ye shall all compose a will; shall confess the Unity of the Lord; and shall assert “I associate naught as partner with God;” yet on the Day of Revelation, it is ye yourselves who shall exemplify that association of partners with God which ye have repudiated, remaining the while oblivious of the circumstance. Thus it is that ye shall of a sudden render your religion vain, without yourselves adverting to the matter. Have a little mercy upon yourselves, that the works ye perform may be on the basis of discerning insight: haply, on the Day of Resurrection ye shall be able to attain salvation.

Know ye that the beginning of this document is from God, but in virtue of that which the Point hath spoken; while the return thereof is unto God, but in virtue of its returning unto Him Whom God shall make manifest. How like it is that ye should compose this document, yet recognize not the One Whom ye are addressing; and that He should make Himself known unto you by virtue of that same proof whereon the religion of all is founded, but the veils of your own selves should shut you out from Him.

Today, for example, all the people of the Qur’an are acting in accordance with His previous commandment; yet have they remained shut out as by a veil from the One by Whom this commandment is constituted such. Notwithstanding that they behold the proof of His commandments aforetime in a nobler guise, yet are they oblivious thereof. It is not that even those who see these words would advert to the matter: nay, although in their own estimation they conceive that were the True One to appear, they would be the nearest of all people unto Him, yet it is these same souls in every Revelation who, at the end thereof, have arrived at the highest degree of eminence in their religion; yet still there befalleth that which befalleth; and God beholdeth all that ye do.

Gate Fourteen of the Fifth Unity

concerning this, that purifying agents are of various kinds; namely: Fire and Air, Water and Earth; the Book of God; the Point and His traces; that over which the Name of God hath been repeated six and sixty times; that which the sun drieth; that whose nature changeth; all who enter into this religion – whereupon they are rendered pure – and all that is related unto them; and that which passeth from the hands of other than the followers of this religion into the hands of the followers of this religion – whereupon the severance of its relation with those, and its introduction into a relation with these, rendereth it pure.

The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world hath, out of His grace and bounty, commanded that a purifying capacity should reside in certain agents, not one of which, even were one to sacrifice all that is on earth, would he have any way to obtain. All of these have acquired their purifying capacity through the command of God, as promulgated from the Tree: for the truth of the matter is that it is the command of God that hath the capacity to purify, not the thing itself: nay, the thing in question is but a throne for that command, inasmuch as it is that command which is made manifest by the thing question.

Yet, with regard to the essential elements of Him by Whose word the purifying agents are created – elements that guide but unto God – see only what they say! Were such an one indeed to judge according to his own creed, no exception might be taken to him: yet, out of the very excess of his precaution, he persisteth in using water until it turneth black as ink: whereas in the case of Him by Whose word the water is rendered pure, he consenteth not to pass judgment that He is pure! The likeness of such an one is he who bore the iniquity of slaying the Prince of Martyrs – peace be upon him – yet made inquiry concerning the blood of a mosquito. Such is the level of this animal creation: albeit even the term “animal” doth not befit them, inasmuch as an animal doth not inflict harm upon another; whereas it is evident what injuries these people inflict.

The Lord hath enjoined these purifying agents, in order that they may betoken the purity of Him Whom God shall make manifest, and of the guides unto His glory. Yet, who is there that will look to the fruit and the purpose of the Lord? If in the Dispensation of the Qur’an they had done so, matters would not have reached the present pass. In the Dispensation of the Bayan too, may the Lord grant them a happy ending, and preserve them from remaining shut out as by a veil from the Object of their desire, so that they may not cause aught untoward to befall Him. For otherwise, in each Revelation the subordinate aspects of religion are, in their own prescribed domain, entirely valid.

Thus, for example, when the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – was made manifest, anyone who entered into the religion of Islam became possessed of its subordinate aspects. Yet, look thou to the thing under whose shadow these subordinate aspects fall, which is belief in Him. Thus it is that each person hath seized upon some particular aspect, and been shut out as by a veil from recognizing its Source. Should anyone acquire the knowledge of the Source, and be graciously aided to act in accordance therewith, then shall both the spiritual and the worldly aspects of that Revelation be his; otherwise shall he be reduced to naught, as though indeed he had never been aforetime a thing recorded in the Book of God.

The agents possessed of a purifying capacity are: first, belief in the Bayan, which converteth the body of the believer into a state of purity; second, the Book of God itself, whereof if aught be placed before a single Verse – provided it be not intrinsically corrupt – it becometh pure; third, the Name of God, which if it be recited over a thing sixty-six times in the form “Allah-u-Athar” (“God is Most Pure”), it becometh pure; fourth, the severance of a relation with other than the people of the Bayan, and the institution of a relation with the people of the Bayan; fifth, the Tree of Truth, on the Day of His appearance, and all His traces; sixth, the four elements; seventh, the sun; and eighth, that whose nature changeth – all of which are only operative provided that the thing concerned be not intrinsically corrupt.

Blood produced from the mouth by means of a toothpick or a toothbrush hath been condoned, and pardoned; but at all events, the Lord loveth them that are pure. No aspect of the Bayan is more beloved in the eyes of the Lord than purity, refinement and cleanliness; and the embarrassment occasioned by the paws of an animal that walketh in the wet, and then cometh into a room, hath been removed. The Lord in the Bayan loveth not to behold in any soul aught but joy and radiance; and He loveth that all should under every circumstance evince the utmost degree of both moral and formal purity, so that they may not be caused abhorrence by aught even in their own selves, let alone in others. There is no objection if, when performing prayer, one have contact with animal hair; as also if he have about him objects imported from the Franks, ivory and bone handles, and the like items. All these dispensations are to the end that the people should enjoy the abundance of God’s mercy: perchance, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, they may be grateful to Him for His previous laws.

It is not that they should exercise precaution with regard to a single hair, and repeat their prayers; yet when it cometh to pronouncing judgment upon the One by Whom the truth of religion itself is vindicated, have not a care: even as anyone who was in the Dispensation of the Qur’an aforetime witnessed this circumstance: for all those who dealt wrongfully with the members of the Holy Family were used to observe the niceties of religion; and in the Dispensation of the Bayan likewise anyone – whoever it may be – hath beheld this matter exemplified to the height of perfection: witnessing how a certain one composed on a detailed question concerning the branches of the law a treatise of a thousand verses; yet in the matter of acknowledging the truth of the True One – through Whom the very root of religion is established – had he written naught, he would but have had the likeness of an “animal,” but without the addition that he was “noxious:” whereas he hath expressed himself in contradiction to the Truth.

Suffer not such things to shut you out as by a veil from the True One; nor be beguiled by these attempts on your part at sanctification – attempts which in the sight of God become as scattered dust: save at such time as they are conjoined with belief in the True One. Time was aforetime when someone would indite five hundred thousand verses in the contrived science of juridical principles, observing therein every last aspect of precaution in his faith: yet, in the matter of acknowledging the truth of God and His Verses he hesitated; and had he done no more than hesitate, he would but have rendered his existence vain: yet he would not content himself with this, but committed against the One from the ocean of Whose bounty the Confession of the Unity of God – which is the very root of religion – shineth forth, that which the pen is ashamed to recount.

O people of the Bayan! Act ye not as the people of the Qur’an have acted! At least, to whatever level ye ascend, exhibit ye the likeness of an animal, so that ye inflict no harm upon another soul, even should ye be unable to confer benefit upon him: perchance, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, ye shall not commit that which shall cast your religion to the winds, while ye yourselves are oblivious of the matter. This is the counsel of the True One unto all; which should anyone abide by, he shall under no circumstance experience any harm: inasmuch as the pardon and forgiveness of that Sun of Truth encompass all creation: and so only He witness not from anyone aught other than love towards Himself, perchance, out of the ocean of His bounty and grace, He shall cause him to enter the fold of belief in Him, and shall show unto him His favour by making mention of him, albeit he himself be uninformed thereof; just as, at the time of recompense in this Resurrection, the Point of Truth recompensed with His Verses those souls from whom naught untoward had been forthcoming: whereas one was at sea, and another was on land: and God alone knoweth when he shall become informed of the recompense of the True One in his regard. God recompenseth them that do good.

Gate Fifteen of the Fifth Unity: Concerning this, that the water from which ye are created hath been purified by God in the Book

The substance of this gate is this, that since there is but One Whose original seed deserveth the designation “pure,” while those that guide unto Him – of the resplendent suns engendered in the mirrors by the sun of His bounty – are so characterized in virtue of His designation, the Lord hath caused all to shelter beneath His shadow, and granted that their seed too be considered pure. Howbeit, He hath loved, and loveth, that refinement therefrom should be manifested to the very height of perfection, in case of ease, not of hardship.

The fruit thereof is this, that with regard to that Most Great Luminary and His guides, no one should so much as entertain the thought that they are impure, inasmuch as all purifying agents are rendered pure through the ocean of the bounty of this same Primordial Germ. At all events, be ye watchful lest a judgment of impurity be passed upon any of the people of the Bayan; if which be done by anyone, he would thereby depart from the fold of belief: perchance, in the period betwixt the Twin Revelations, no sorrow may on this account befall them who are the manifestations of the True One.

How grievously, in the Qur’an, the believers transgressed the ordinance of the Lord, branding as impure those souls who but guided unto God! – whereas the purity of the souls of the believers derived from the blessedness of their sanctified beings. For example, during the days of my residence at the Holy Thresholds, the late Siyyid – peace be upon him – came one day to my abode; and after he had left, the owner of the house gave order for the door with which the hand of that tree of purity had come into contact to be washed: whereas, according to the requirements of their own code of law, how is a state of impurity engendered when two dry bodies come into contact? Thus it is that they transgress the ordinance of their own religion, on the pretext of “observing caution:” whereas, when the root is lost, how can the branch remain?

Wherefore, O ye servants of God, guard against incurring My displeasure!

Gate Sixteen of the Fifth Unity

concerning this, that unto God belongeth whatsoever is peerless in its kind, which, for as long as the Sun shineth, should be brought into His presence; while after Its setting God hath granted each soul leave to possess until the Sun dawn from Its Dayspring; whereupon it shall not be lawful unto that soul, but must needs be returned unto Him, to the number Vahid, not above this, should he be possessed of such; otherwise is he not charged withal: and should there be one from whose hands emergeth, through his craftsmanship, an object that is peerless in its kind, he hath been excused thereof, as a bounty from God in his respect, if it be the source of his wealth; otherwise is he required to return it, inasmuch as God hath enriched him with the wealth of His dominion from another source: he should not be occasioned distress thereby; and should he be distressed, he hath been excused thereof, as a token of God’s grace unto him: He, verily, is the Most Gracious, the All-Bountiful.

The substance of this gate is that the greatest of all things which the Lord loveth should be made manifest amongst the people of the Bayan is their love, one for another. However much they may ascend or descend in the stations of understanding – or in the knowledge of juridical principles or juridical branches, of Manifest or Hidden, of First or Last – they should not rebuff each other: for whosoever hath entered within the fold of the Bayan is a believer, and in whatsoever station he be situated, it is good.

Should anyone in the Bayan rebuff another of the people of the Bayan, a payment of ninety-five mithqals of gold shall become incumbent upon him, to be rendered unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, not other than He; nor hath anyone the right to demand it of him, but rather is it to be rendered by himself alone: nay, this obligation attacheth solely betwixt himself and God: should that Sun of Truth so will it, He shall waive the payment; and should He so will it, He shall receive it of him.

The purpose of the Lord in prescribing this penalty is this, that no one in the Bayan should have the audacity to rebuff another, through ascribing unto him other than belief; otherwise, the degrees of each person within the bounds of his proper station are evident; and each person, in whatsoever position he be situated, is – if he be “for God” – to be praised in his doings – alike one who is lying at the level of the lowest question of juridical branches, and one who is standing at the level of the highest question of juridical principles: perchance, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, no one shall consent to aught but loving references in respect of that Most Great Luminary: haply, by this means, the people of the Bayan may not perish on the Day of Resurrection, but obtain deliverance through the love of Him, which is the essence of all belief.

Since He is the Sign of “There is naught like unto Him” of the Lord, He hath accordingly commanded that aught in His dominion which arriveth at this level should be for Him. For as long as the Sun of Truth shineth, unto none shall be lawful that which befitteth only Him in His dominion, unless with His permission after the rendering therefrom of the manifestations of Vahid; while from the time of Its setting, permission hath been granted unto the believers to acquire such objects on His behalf, and to render thanks unto their Best-Beloved: until the time of His appearance, whereupon it shall not be lawful unto anyone to tarry for so much as the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of a second ere he return unto its Owner whatsoever, in His dominion, hath arrived at the station of perfection – even of all that hath attained unto the furthest limit of development at its own level, to the number Vahid, since aught above this number He hath granted unto him, as a token of His bounty, ere yet He hath appeared.

As for him who fulfilleth not the command of God on the Day of the appearance of the True One, should he withhold a single item that is peerless in its kind, a payment of ninety-five mithqals of gold shall become incumbent upon him: lest anyone be able to be shut out as by a veil from observing the command of God that he make expense in His religion. Permission hath been granted, in the case of a craftsman who, in the course of one year, produceth a single artefact, that he shall not thereby incur an obligation: so that all may repose in the abundance of His mercy. Whensoever anyone becometh possessed of such an object, he should at the time of Revelation return it unto its Owner.

Whosoever wisheth to obey his Lord’s command shall do so: for what greater glory can there be for a bond slave than to be honoured through obedience to his Owner? It is but a token of His grace unto His creation that He hath granted them this permission; for otherwise He is, in Himself, absolutely capable of dispensing with all else besides Himself: and all have been created from the ocean of His bounty, and are in the twin scales of His grace and justice. For God is all that is in the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them; and He is the All-Possessing, the Most High.

It is not that the one who withholdeth any item, withholdeth it for other than Him: nay, no one, under any circumstance, wisheth to act but for the Lord; unless he becometh shut out by a veil, in each Revelation, from recognizing His good pleasure: whence that which, in his own conceit, he performeth “for God” is rendered vain; for otherwise, at the time when it is rendered vain, it hath not departed from the dominion of the Lord; and All Things are still for Him. It is on account of this mystery that whatsoever affliction befalleth the True One is from Him, even as it is intended for Him: yet since the author thereof was shut out as by a veil from Him, it falleth out against Him.

It is not that, at the time when one is thus shut out as by a veil, the proof of God in his respect is incomplete: for had the proof in his respect been incomplete, he would not have been liable to any judgment. At the time of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – the proof of God before the people of the Evangel was complete, and He Who had been promised unto them was made manifest with the selfsame proof of their own religion; howbeit, since they remained shut out from Him as by a veil, they were rendered vain. Notwithstanding, they permit not the thought to enter their hearts that the One Promised by Jesus should have come, and they not have believed in Him: whereas the truth of the matter is evident.

Thus it is that on each appearance of the True One, the chain of believers in the previous Revelation – in the conceit of their precaution and endeavour – remain shut out as by a veil within the fold of their own faith; while the Lord favoureth with His guidance whomsoever He willeth, for this guidance is more precious in His eyes than any thing (for whatsoever there be, and He be not – methinks there hath never been, nor ever shall be, aught; while whensoever He be, and there be naught, He hath never been, nor ever shall be, diminished in aught); and in Paradise he shall attain whatsoever had been promised unto him: for conceive thou the creation of Paradise to be like unto the creation of All Things: whatsoever is possible to it within the limits of its own potential the Lord hath created therein: for ever hath He been powerful over each thing, and transcendent over all things. There is no God but God. We all, verily, are devoted unto Him.

Gate Seventeen of the Fifth Unity

setting forth the monthly duty to make mention of God each day five and ninety times, through repeating “Allah-u-Abha” (“God is Most Glorious”) on the first day; “Allah-u-A’zam” (“God is Most Mighty”) on the second; and so on, until the succession endeth with “Allah-u-Aqdam” (“God is Most Ancient”) on the nineteenth day, the final day of the month.

The substance of this gate is that from the dawning of the sun until its setting, the Lord hath permitted each soul to repeat ninety-five times “Allah-u-Abha;” or “Allah-u-A’zam;” or “Allah-u-Azhar” (“God is Most Manifest”); or “Allah-u-Anwar” (“God is Most Luminous”); or “Allah-u-Akbar” (“God is Most Great”); or the like of this kind of peerless Words: perchance on the Day of Resurrection he may, through the blessing of reciting these Holy Names, attain the honour of being guided by that Most Great Luminary and Ancient Countenance, and may be able on that Day to be guided by the guidance of the Letters of the Living.

It is not that, while reciting these Names, one should be shut out as by a veil from those who guide unto them: for the likeness of these Names is that of the realities of those that guide unto God: just as these letters guide unto the truth that the Lord is too great to admit of any description, so too those realities guide unto the truth that the Lord is too great to accept of any qualification. It is not that the Letters of the Vahid exceed the limits of their character as likenesses: inasmuch as none hath ever had, or ever shall have, a way unto the Eternal Essence. Whatsoever is possible in the realm of being is but His creation; while the Letters of the Vahid are but the guides unto His Names, before His creatures – guides wherein naught is to be seen but God, single and alone. In the station wherein they themselves are seen, they are God’s creation; while in the station wherein naught is to be seen in them but God – then are they the Letters of the True One.

Beware, O servants of God, of extravagance when describing the nature of their station! Notwithstanding, whatever extravagant terms might be employed, still it would be impossible to comprehend them; while in whatever lowly terms they might be limned – such hath been, and shall remain, but an affirmation of their servitude. Nay rather, their exaltation resideth in the capacity of their hearts to act as mirrors, which guide not but unto God alone. It is for this reason that the Lord of the world hath appointed them the Letters of Glory, Thanks, Unity and Grandeur. It is not that at the time when – by exclaiming “Allah-u-Akbar!” – thou makest confession of God’s Grandeur, thou shouldst have regard for them: for whilst doing so thou wouldst be shut out as by a veil from Him; nay, in the same way as thou beholdest in the letters of “Allah-u-Akbar” naught but God, in these realities likewise naught is to be seen but God.

Say: All are God’s creatures, and all worship Him.

Gate Eighteen of the Fifth Unity

ordaining, with respect to purchases, that once the consent of both parties hath been established, however this be arrived at – though it be through the act itself – buying and selling are valid, on the part of both young or old; whilst the use of discount is permitted amongst merchants, however this be agreed upon betwixt buyer and seller – the which is to be within a stipulated term according to a stated value (Baha’), although this value (Baha’) be reduced.

The substance of this gate is that the Lord hath permitted buying and selling on condition that the consent of both parties be established. He hath permitted young and old, freeman and bond slave, to buy and sell: so only the consent of both parties be ascertained – though it be by a sign, or through the act itself – buying and selling are valid in the Bayan. The Lord hath permitted merchants to make use of that discount which is today customary amongst them, and to appoint in their transactions a gradual increase or decrease of value within a stipulated term: so that all, in the abundance of the grace and mercy of the True One, may be thankful. Perchance, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, the buying of the Sign of the Sun of Truth, and the selling of aught else but Him for Him, may be transacted with His consent, and that of their own selves: haply, by this means, all who adhere to these procedures may on that Day obtain salvation.

Gate Nineteen of the Fifth Unity

explaining that the mithqal is nineteen nakhuds; and that the value (Baha’) of nineteen nakhuds of gold is ten thousand dinars, while the value (Baha’) of nineteen nakhuds of silver is one thousand dinars; and that he who reduceth them is under no obligation; while he who hath not had such in his possession for one full year, nor have they amounted in either case – according to the number of the letters of “Ta’,” at the time of the levying of “Ha’” – to five hundred and forty mithqals, is in a similar case: after which, of each mithqal of gold five hundred, and of silver fifty, dinars are to be rendered unto the king of the Bayan, should he not transgress the bounds fixed therein: neither is he to ask after it, but those with the ability are themselves to render it: perchance by this means he may champion Him Whom God shall make manifest, and be in consequence of the truly thankful.

The substance of this gate is that the Lord is the Creator both of His creatures and of His dominions; and, so that the property of His dominions may not be in the hands of other than those who truly recognize His Unity, He hath granted all permission to render unto him who is their captain in championing their faith – whensoever a year hath passed, and the amount thereof hath surpassed the threshold of five hundred and forty mithqals (whereof no mithqal hath been reduced at the hand of a believer in whose possession it had arrived at nineteen parts) – to render, of every mithqal of gold (which is made up of nineteen nakhuds), five hundred dinars; and of every mithqal of silver (which is made up of nineteen nakhuds), fifty dinars, unto the king of the Bayan: perchance, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, he shall have been enriched from the ocean of His bounty, and cause no sadness to befall Him, even should it be in consequence of the denial of the very nearest of all people unto himself.

This levy is of the Rights of God (Huququ’llah) for Him Whom God shall make manifest, in which, in the eyes of them endued with understanding, the Mystery of “Qaf” is witnessed. Notwithstanding, He hath granted it unto those who await His arrival: haply, at that time no sorrow may befall Him, lest He be compelled to transgress the limits fixed by God, and anyone be occasioned sorrow on His account. For in the Bayan, there is no act of piety more beloved in the eyes of God than that one soul should benefit another, even though it be by means of bringing joy into his heart; while there is no action more remote from godliness than that one soul should inflict harm upon another, even though it be by means of bringing sorrow into his heart.

It is not that they should perform the works they do in His Name; yet on the Day of His appearance, term it “precaution,” and hesitate to accept His truth: even as today, all who are on earth perform the works they do in the Name of that same Primal Will which in each Revelation hath been made manifest in the name of the Prophet of that Revelation; whereas in this Revelation – in comparison with which all other Revelations are a ghostly shadow – it is evident what hath come to pass. Nay, the harm that was inflicted by those related unto His Former Manifestation was not inflicted by those related unto His Manifestation before that preceding: for if these accepted not His truth, neither did they inflict harm upon His partisans: whereas that which was inflicted by those who claim to be related unto His Former Manifestation is evident.

Should all behold his justice, there is no doubt that, in obedience unto their Adored One, the believers in the One True God shall discharge their obligation. Notwithstanding, if in this Revelation he acteth conformably with the good pleasure of God, he shall – in virtue of the conquest of all that is on earth – become rich enough to be able to show his favour unto those sheltering beneath the shadow of his sovereignty, and to excuse them from the payment of some part of the Rights of God: inasmuch as all that is on earth hath been, and is, for the Lord to the degree that were all to take but a step in the path of rendering him their assistance, all would become enriched thereby.

Permission hath been granted for each mithqal of gold to amount to nineteen nakhuds, and likewise in the case of silver; and for the value (Baha’) of both to be set at that which is today apparent. Should it be wished to expend them, they should both be dispensed in nineteen parts: whence in the hands of the believers in the Bayan naught but silver and gold may be current: so that all, in the abundance of the grace of the True One, may be thankful. In the eyes of those endued with understanding, the secrets of wisdom are treasured in this law: to the degree that were one to look with discerning insight, he would behold with the eye of certitude all the mysteries of the Unity of God.

At the time when naught hath been levied, the impost of “Ha’” should be entered in its proper place – as elucidated by the foregoing reference to “Qaf” – in the shadow of what is owing. Although in this law, for merchants, a decrease in the value (Baha’) of gold and silver today is apparent, yet after its enactment this will be reversed. Should anyone owe a qiran, he is to render twenty-eight nakhuds, not the value (Baha’) thereof; likewise, in the case of gold, he is to render twenty nakhuds, not the value (Baha’) thereof; unless by this means buying and selling may be promoted.

All of these enactments are to the end that no one should be occasioned sorrow in the path of the True One, on the Day of His appearance: perchance, at the time of His appearance, no untoward occurrence shall befall, such as would engender fire in those souls upon whom in the Bayan had been passed a sentence of belief. God guideth whomsoever He willeth unto a path of certain truth. There is no more exalted Paradise than the mere observance of the laws of God, in the eyes of them that truly recognize His Unity; nor is there a fiercer fire than the transgression of the bounds fixed by God, and the infringement of one soul against another, though it be to the extent of a grain of mustard seed, in the eyes of those who are acquainted with God and His Verses.

God distinguisheth on the Day of Resurrection between all in truth; and we all, verily, beseech a portion of His grace.

The Sixth Unity

Gate One of the Sixth Unity

enjoining, with respect to the ordering of the Bayan, that it should not exceed nineteen volumes, whereof in the first three should be inscribed the Verses; in the succeeding four the Prayers; in the succeeding six the Commentaries; and in the final six the Scientific Treatises: in all of which the Chapters should be from Vahid to “Mustaghath;” and, furthermore, that each person should have in his possession a writing (if the which contain no less than a thousand verses it would be better for him) of the Verses, which he may recite howsoever he wisheth (the verse being estimated at thirty letters, and the vowel markings at ten).

The substance of this gate is that there is naught more beloved in the eyes of the Lord than symmetry: to the degree even that should someone possess a plot of land, and wish to make symmetry apparent with respect thereto, it should be in such wise that a person with an astrolabe, surveying it with the most scrutinizing gaze, would be unable to perceive the beginning thereof to be in excess of the end thereof to the extent of aught that could be mentioned. If such be beloved of the Lord even with respect to land, how must stand the case in circumstances wherein it is possible to make symmetry apparent?

The Lord hath given leave for the Bayan to be ordered, providing that it exceed not nineteen volumes, and that in all it be laid out with the utmost symmetry, order and regularity, so that were someone to examine it, he would not perceive in the end thereof a single letter to be in excess of the beginning thereof. It is not that such hath actually been enjoined: rather, the purpose of these remarks is to exemplify the utmost limit of what might be achieved in the way of symmetry: nay, a yet higher degree of symmetry hath been destined in the knowledge of the Lord, according to which regard could be had for the numerical values of the letters – an undertaking which would be impossible for the people, in view of the sheer volume of all that hath been sent down: whence neither the former nor the latter system of arrangement hath been enjoined.

The name “Bayan” applieth in the primary sense unto the Verses alone: for these are the Most Mighty Proof and the Most Great Sign, which guide not but unto God alone; while in the secondary sense it applieth unto the Prayers; in the tertiary unto the Commentaries; in the quaternary unto the Scientific Words; and in the quinary unto the Persian Words: but all are subsumed beneath the shadow of the Verses. Although that mystery of eloquence which is apparent in the first is hidden also in the last, yet because all are unable to apprehend this, it hath not been so designated.

The purpose of this ordering is this, that on the appearance of the Possessor of the Bayan, all the human realities shall have acquired a similarity to the letters of the Vahid, and be travelling upon the sea of Oneness: perchance, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, they may be able to derive illumination from the splendour of the Sun of Truth, and, in the privacy of their hearts, come into the presence of that Most Great Luminary, without the aid of the spiritual and worldly matters that are apparent.

If in each volume material from all five categories be included, with the utmost symmetry, it would be beloved in the eyes of the True One. Although in the first three the “limpid water” is flowing; while in the succeeding four the “unaltered milk;” in the succeeding six the “wine” of Unity; and in the succeeding six that which is mentioned in respect of the Fourth Pillar, are flowing; yet in each pillar all have been, and are, both manifest and hidden: nay the observer will behold them in each letter – nay in each point. Since this is in form possessed of four pillars, it is an indication of the likeness of the reality of That. It is not, however, that in this Vahid aught is to be seen but the Vahid, such that were it to be increased by one, it would become Twenty, rather than Two. The secret thereof is that in this Vahid naught is to be seen but the image of the innumerate Vahid. Thus it is that, in the privacy of one’s heart, one is able to come into the presence of the First Vahid at the beginning of the appearance of the Resurrection.

Consider thou the Bayan: although the order hath been given for it to be bound into separate volumes, yet all, from the Fountain-Head of Revelation, is a “single water;” while in all these letters of the Vahid, it is that same water which is the source of life. It is not that there is any source of creation other than God; or any source of sustenance other than God; or any source of death, or of life, other than He: nay, this First Vahid is His creation, which guideth at the level of the world of being unto such Oneness as it is possible to be made manifest in the realm of being. For otherwise, that Oneness which pertaineth to the Essence hath ever been, and ever shall be, unknowable; neither can it be conjoined with any mention: it hath never entered, nor ever shall it, within the scope of numbers; neither can it be made known by means of geometry.

The fruit of this ordering is that haply, on the Day of Resurrection, all the believers in the Bayan may be guided by the guidance of the Letters of the Vahid. Yet be not beguiled by the love of the Point and the Letters of the Living: for that Day is the day of testing. If someone love that Point and those Letters, and is guided by their guidance, it is an indication that he hath loved this Point and these Letters. Otherwise, observe thou how strenuously the people today profess love for the Point of the Qur’an, and His Letters of the Living, and obedience unto them! – whereas not one in a thousand hath entered within the pale of the Vicegerency of this Point, and of these Letters. Conceive thou the case in that Revelation likewise to be even as in this.

Be thou watchful lest thou allow aught on that Day to shut thee out as by a veil therefrom: inasmuch as the whole of the Bayan, and the spirits thereof, are – in comparison with Him Whom God shall make manifest – as a fruit in the palm of His hand. Should the word “Yea” be sent down from the Point of the Bayan with respect to all, then have they been, and are, within the pale of the mercy of the True One; and should rather the word “Nay” go forth, the sentence implied by this is obvious. Reflect, and consider: is there aught lighter than a fruit, or nay? Such is the reality of the matter in the sight of God. Although beneath the shadow of each letter thousands upon thousands of souls are sheltering – each one of whom is held in esteem and honour in virtue of some law of the Qur’an – yet all depend upon that single thread, which is held in the hand of the Revealer of the Qur’an, not in the hand of other than He.

Conceive thou: Had the Apostle of the Lord revealed a single Verse importing that all the believers in the Evangel were within the pale of God’s mercy, would anyone have been able to allege a sentence of other than mercy in their regard? Yet would it be impossible to count even a part of them, how much less their whole number! So soon, however, as he passed not such a sentence, but decreed rather the reverse, behold how protractedly they have tarried at their own level! This is the essence of all knowledge: that through a single “Yea,” all are quickened to life; while through a single enunciation by Him of “Nay,” all are reduced to naught – in truth, not in virtue of the things they might imagine – whether by force, or by ascendancy, or whatsoever other matters might be conceived of. Nay, this sentence is the true sentence, beyond which naught higher could be conceived of, and which affecteth the quintessential nature of All Things.

Exert your utmost diligence and effort lest on the Day of the appearance of the True One ye cite from His own words arguments against Him, for the whole of the Bayan is the utterance of His own Former Manifestation, and He is better apprised of that which He hath revealed than are all people: inasmuch as the spirit of all is held within His grasp; while that which all possess is but a ghostly shadow, provided that they be steadfast in their recognition of the Truth; for otherwise is it unworthy of mention. Today, for example, if someone be the very Plato of his age in every science, yet accept not the truth of the True One, would his knowledge avail him aught? Glorified be God above any such conception! Nay, he would be entirely destitute of knowledge.

The knowledge that is worthy of the name is the knowledge of God and the Apostle, and of the manifestations of His command and of His judgment. To naught else would those endued with understanding apply the designation “knowledge.” Even as, at the time of Jesus – peace be upon Him – the very moment that anyone who exemplified this name confessed not the Prophethood of His Holiness Jesus – peace be upon our Prophet and upon Him – this appellation availed him naught. Conceive thou such to be the case likewise on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest: were all the people of the Bayan to become, like Him, exponents of the quintessence of knowledge, it would avail them naught, save only through acceptance of His truth. Take heed, therefore, O ye endowed with understanding; then hold Him in befitting awe!

In ordering the Verses, the arrangement thereof should be Surih by Surih, from a single Verse at the lowest level up to the Name of “Mustaghath” at the highest. It is fitting that each person should have in his possession a writing of not less than a thousand verses – exhibiting the various modes of the Bayan – of that wherein he taketh delight. Each thirty letters are reckoned to constitute one verse: which, if the vowel markings be taken into account, should be regarded as composed of forty letters.

The likeness of the whole of the Bayan is that of a gem, which one person entrusteth to another: if, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, He wisheth to retrieve from all the believers that which He had bestowed upon them, they should not tarry to the extent of aught. It is not that one should be shut out as by a veil from Him by a matter relating to its branches; while another should be shut out by its roots; another by its manifestations of judgment; and another by its manifestations of glory: nay, all is from Him, and returneth unto Him.

Do ye recognize Him by His Verses; nor exercise “precaution” in recognizing Him, for as long as ye are thus shut out as by a veil from Him, ye shall be in the Fire. Should ye hesitate betwixt yourselves and God – yet that same Sign whereby, betwixt yourselves and God, ye direct yourselves unto Him, is nevertheless His likeness, which is imprinted in your hearts. Allow not His own image to shut you out as by a veil from Him, but recognize the One for the sake of recognizing Whom ye were called into being; and thereto be vigilant: for if He make not Himself known by His own Name, yet by other matters – even by His Verses – shall He make Himself known unto all, so that no one, to the extent of aught, shall have any pretext for failing to recognize Him.

It may well chance that someone is sitting in his home, and gazing upon the Bayan, when His emissary cometh before him with an Epistle from Him: yet, because he wanteth discernment in his faith, he is not convinced thereby, and on the instant entereth into the Fire; whereas the Bayan by whose precepts he hath been abiding was from Him; while the Epistle which He hath sent down upon him, enshrining His Verses, is greater than the Work in his possession: inasmuch as the former is a gift of the Lord in the after life unto him, which is greater in the sight of the Lord than the previous revelations which He hath sent down upon him from the repository of His bounty and His mystery.

Be it not as today, when each person hath in his possession a Qur’an, in virtue whereof he is devoted to the religion of Islam, even while being shut out as by a veil from both the Revelation and the Bearer of the Revelation. How like it is that the value (Baha’) of the Qur’an in his possession should be a thousand mithqals of gold; yet he alloweth some matter to shut him out as by a veil from both the Revelation and the Bearer of the Revelation; which were he to learn of, gladly would he accept never to have been created, so he might not be without a portion of the fruit of his existence. Do ye exercise the most scrupulous care: inasmuch as the Sirat is finer than aught; yet through the knowledge thereof, it is wider than aught. God beginneth All Things, then returneth them.

Say: Do ye believe with certainty in all that God hath sent down in the Bayan. The knowledge of the Bayan is dependent upon the knowledge of its revelation, from the beginning thereof unto the end thereof: inasmuch as that which hath been sent down in the beginning is according to the laws of the Qur’an; while thereafter the dispositions of the Bayan have become apparent therein. It is not that one should allow the beginning to shut one out as by a veil from the end; or that one should fix one’s gaze upon the end, and have no regard for the beginning. Nay, each letter – in its own particular station of fire and light – hath been, and is, adduced in its proper context. Notwithstanding, the more eloquent it waxeth, the more clearly is the Divine purpose therein made apparent. The whole of the Bayan is the utterance of the Point of Truth; even as the whole of religion is the recognition of Him, and the knowledge of His commandments.

God guideth whomsoever He willeth unto a path of certain truth.

Gate Two of the Sixth Unity

concerning this, that a well should be treated, with respect to purity, in the same manner as a “kurr,” while the restrictions relating to the latter have been lifted, and all have been enjoined to make use of pure water; that water is pureness, pure and purifying, in itself for itself, and for other than itself by itself, should none of its three properties have been altered; and that the state of purity of a part thereof is as that of the whole thereof, and vice versa.

The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world hath, through His bounty and grace, decreed that a glassful of water should be treated in the same manner as a large quantity of water, so that all may enjoy the abundance of His grace and mercy. He hath abrogated the measures previously taken when some object fell into a well; but at all events He hath loved that no land wherein His servants reside should be without a reservoir, so that cleansing and purification may be facilitated. There is no house wherein a pool is not constructed but that the angels shall not pass thereby: and should they be commanded thereunto by God, then only with abhorrence would they do so. Let all the people of the Bayan attend carefully to this bounty, so that no soul may be deprived thereof.

The diffusion of a state of purity throughout this material water hath not occurred save in virtue of the pervasive purity of the water of the Ocean of Unity: in the same way as a single drop thereof guideth unto God, so too the whole body guideth unto God.

Water, by itself, hath been and is pureness, pure and purifying. At the time when some object is to be cleansed, it is better for the water to be poured over it than for the object to be plunged into the water: inasmuch as in this latter procedure a cause of abhorrence may be present, whereas in the former it is absent. Observe ye that the whole of purification resideth in the word of God, in virtue whereof water is rendered pure: and if, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, He decree the purity of some matter, marvel not thereat: for His word is the source of purity, not the thing itself; notwithstanding that such purity appeareth not save through His command.

Methinks I see that all the people of the Bayan, in pursuit of the purity inculcated by His previous decree with respect to water, shall exert the utmost endeavour in this regard; whereas on the Day of His appearance, they shall become veiled from recognizing Him by these same matters, even as is apparent in this day.

O people of the Bayan! Act not as the people of the Qur’an have acted, exerting the utmost diligence and endeavour to purify their physical bodies with material water; yet, in the matter of the purification of the essential body with the Water of Unity, remaining shut out as by a veil from the need to purify themselves withal.

Know thou that any heart wherein is the love of other than God is not pure in the sight of God: and likewise any spirit, soul, or body wherein are the love of other than the Letters of the Vahid, and of those who love them, is not pure in His sight: for the state of purity of the body dependeth upon the purity of the essential body, which is rendered pure through belief, and naught else; otherwise, today no people exceed the Christians in the refinement of their outward persons: whereas their state of purity is obvious.

In like manner, at the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, do ye purify your whole self through belief in Him: for were ye each day a thousand times to enter into the sea, and to come out again, ye would not thereby compass the purity even of your outward person, how much less of your essential body. Suffer not these attempts on your part at sanctification to shut you out as by a veil from the True One. Even as today the people are shut out in this manner. In the matter of bodily purity, there is one to be found who exerciseth an unparalleled degree of caution, composing fifty thousand verses on the subject; yet in a case where mere hesitation will cause the purity of his inner essence to be altered from its pristine state, he hath not a care, but pronounceth judgment in such terms as the Pen is ashamed to set forth.
