Do ye exercise the utmost care lest ye be shut out as by a veil from either the outward or the inward manifestations of purity: nay, acquire them both, and evince them to the very height of perfection: perchance, on the Day of the appearance of the True One, ye may be able to derive illumination from the splendour of the Sun. Should that Sun of Truth, on an instant, pronounce a sentence of purity in any terms that could be conceived of, it is the duty of all to obey Him – whatever the matters affected – and to act accordingly: for that which ye do today is in virtue of His own previous command: and in His eyes the Source of Command is under all circumstances the same.

The state of purity of a part of the water is as that of the whole; and if it be poured twice over some object wherein no intrinsic corruption hath lingered, it shall render the thing in question pure; howbeit, if the object be plunged into the water, a single immersion shall suffice, provided that the water be such as would occasion one no abhorrence on account of its paucity; for otherwise the use of such water for the purpose of purification is not desirable. Nor, in case a quantity of water hath been altered by an impure object, is it desirable to make use thereof: notwithstanding, the water itself is not deprived of its state of purity, unless it can no longer be accounted water; any more than a pure object is deprived of its state of purity if it become similarly altered. Should water become mixed with earth, it is not accounted “commingled;” nor is it permissible to make use of “commingled water” for the purpose of purification, so that the wealthy may not make a show of exaltation above the poor; for otherwise, in the eyes of the Lord, His command can be accomplished swifter than the twinkling of an eye.

Notwithstanding, there is naught more beloved in the eyes of the Lord than that water should be preserved in a state of the utmost purity; so that if it come to anyone’s knowledge that a glassful of water hath passed over such-and-such an earth that is impure, it would not be palatable to the heart of a refined believer. As for the ruling that even after water hath become altered it is still pure, this is to the end that the principle of the purity of water may be universal in its scope: for otherwise, what soul is there who would have the inclination even to approach it, let alone use it for cleansing?

In the eyes of the Lord, it is not beloved that meticulousness in purification should breed some matter that would in the end result in harm being inflicted upon the person concerned: nay, the soul of the believer is too noble for aught to be able to “alter” it; rather, the laws of purity are all to the end that men’s souls should be trained in point of refinement and purity to the degree that no one would be caused abhorrence by aught even in his own self, let alone in others: lest he happen to be present on the Day of the Revelation of God, and some cause of abhorrence be witnessed from him: forasmuch as the displeasure of His Manifestation is none other but the displeasure of God; whilst the good pleasure of His Manifestation is likewise the good pleasure of God Himself.

At all events, it is fitting that the believing servant should protect his sense of smell with perfumes, so that he may not inhale any unlovely odour; and likewise, that in his inner self, he should not inhale the odours of the other than believers, and so be deprived of the good pleasure of his Best-Beloved, without his noticing it.

Say: Water purifieth you not save by the leave of your Lord: wherefore, O ye servants of God, yield thanks unto Me!

Gate Three of the Sixth Unity: On this, that God hath verily ordained His servants to build in each village a House for warm bath

The substance of this gate is this, that inasmuch as in this Revelation happened that which happened, and inasmuch as all have been blessed by the favour of cleansing by virtue of the command of the Apostle of God, blessings of God rest upon Him, yet they desired for the Source of that command, that which is evident, it is, therefore, ordained in the Bayan that no place would be inhabited unless a house of cleansing and refinement would be constructed therein. Thus if one day a faithful is assailed by affliction, he would be able to act, in the religion of the Bayan, in conformity with the utmost height of cleansing and refinement. For, in this religion no other command is as rigorously enjoined as the duty of refinement, and it is forbidden that one bringeth anything into being in a state of imperfection, when he hath the power to manifest it in utter perfection.

For example, should one build an edifice, and fail to elevate it to the utmost state of perfection that is possible for it, there would be no moment in the life of that edifice, when angels would not beseech God to torment him, nay, rather, all the atoms of that edifice do the same. For each thing, within its own station, yearneth to attain unto the utmost height of excellence in its own level. Thus, when a man is in a position of power to realise its yearning, and he faileth to do so, he would be held accountable therefor. This is enjoined that haply should someday in His Resurrected Revelation, the Sun of Truth pass by a place, he would behold the signs of the submission of His faithfuls unto Himself.

It is ordained in this religion, to design the gates of each place in a manner that a tall man can enter through them without bending their head. It behoveth them that they always build every single place in the same manner that they construct the Lofty Seats, namely in utmost exaltation, so that haply in the Day of the Revelation of God, nothing that causeth grief would be witnessed in His kingdom. For all the fruits of the Previous Revelation and the years that hath passed of that Dispensation, should be manifested in the Day of Resurrection.

As to the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, it is God Who knoweth that in how many years after this Revelation, He shall make Him manifest. However, from the inception of the Revelation till nineteen years (number of the unity) take heed and be watchful, inasmuch as each year, the revelation of the faith of the believers would be manifested by a different letter, after which they would not be able to manifest the fruits of the past Revelation, except through the Next revelation. Even as anyone who hath been present from the early days of this Revelation, hath witnessed that they refused to let the Manifestation of the fruits of 1270 years to reveal Himself beyond the station of the gatehood (Bab).

Were anyone to fail in revealing the fruit of his existence, it is he himself who would be shut out as by a veil from Him. However, hasten in His Revelation, in utmost swiftness, inasmuch as the Cause of God is swifter than anything else. Manifest ye all, upon hearing of His Revelation, the fruits of the Bayan by any means in your power, for should there be a delay, to the extent of the twinkling of an eye, all that ye have done would perish. Who knoweth, your present deeds may even fail to be accepted, unless they are manifested as the deeds of the next fruit. God verily doeth what He willeth, and ordaineth that which He pleaseth.

Gate Four of the Sixth Unity

concerning this, that God hath permitted none to reside in the Five Provinces save the Letters of the Bayan, however long this last.

The substance of this gate is that in the same way as the Lord of the world plucketh the jewel of each thing, so too, on the appearance of the Letter “Ha’,” He hath plucked the jewels of the earth, and set them within the bounds of “Ha’:” inasmuch as the effulgence of this Word appeared sooner in these five bounds than elsewhere: nay, from here it penetrated into other parts. Just as the souls in these lands became a pathway of guidance unto other souls, among the lands also the Cause of God, in the eyes of those endowed with understanding, is manifested in this same wise.

The hearts of the people of these lands are ascending unto God through the five degrees of the confession of His Unity: in the Land of “Fa’,” the manifestations of the confession “that there is no God but Him” shine forth in the mirrors of the hearts of those who extol His Glory; in “’Ayn,” the manifestations of the confession “that there is no God but Me” shine forth in the hearts of those who extol His Sanctity; in “Alif,” the manifestations of the confession “that there is no God but God” shine forth in the hearts of those who extol His Unity; in “Kha’,” the manifestations of the hearts of those who pronounce the confession “that there is no God but Thee” shine forth in the hearts of those who extol His Grandeur; while in “Mim,” the manifestations of the hearts of those who extol His Majesty reflect the splendour of the mirrors of “There is no God but the One Who created All Things through His command.”

Although all these degrees are apparent in each land – nay, in each atom – yet the criterion is priority of appearance, and delivery of sustenance from the Source: so that the people thereof may be able to rise up conformably with the gem-like essence of all things. These lands are construed as the “Five Paradises” in the Five Names; and as the “Five Limits” in the human temple: whence if someone were to cast his gaze over the entire earth, he would behold the lines of “Ha’” within these five.

This ruling shall remain in force, however, only up to the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest; at which time the dawning-place of the effulgence shall be taken as the source: for in the Revelation of the Furqan, Mecca became the dayspring of the lands; while in the Revelation of the Bayan it was the Land of “Fa’.” The Lord alone knoweth from which horizon of the earth that Sun of Truth shall dawn.

For this reason hath it been decreed that not so much as an atom of that which God loveth not should remain in these provinces: to the degree, indeed, that were sufficient capacity observed, assuredly the command would have been given that, from the surface of the water unto the limits exalted thereupon, they be raised of diamonds, so that naught unlovely should come to the knowledge of anyone therein; howbeit, this is not at present within the power of these people, unless God will it otherwise. The recompense of a single soul in these Five Provinces is preferable to that of twelve thousand years of worship, should one be steadfast in his belief in the True One; for otherwise, in the shade, do thou gather naught but shade. Had it been possible for the wall surrounding all to be of crimson ruby, the Divine command would assuredly have been issued in this wise: so that, among the lands, the Temple of “Ha’” should be distinguished above the whole earth, and the provinces which were the dayspring of the effulgence of the Divine appearance should be exalted above all regions.

These provinces are not exalted save because they accepted to bow down before the provinces of Him Whom God shall make manifest; otherwise they would not have been created. This is their source of glory among all lands. Likewise, had the souls therein not chosen to accept belief in Him, they too would not have been created.

In every circumstance, beseech Him of His grace to cause to shine forth upon all creation that which befitteth the ocean of His bounty: inasmuch as the sustenance of all is derived from Him alone. Look thou today at the Qur’an, and consider how many prayers are offered up each day by the believers, all of whom are gathered together under the shadow of “Perform ye prayer,” and derive from it their sustenance. Were indeed all that are on earth to undertake the duty thus prescribed, this Word would still contain them all: nay, if the Resurrection constituted by this Revelation had not been set on foot, this Word would have continued to sustain the worshippers to an illimitable extent; nor would there have been any interruption in its supply of sustenance. Such is the exaltation of the command of God, and the sublimity of His ordinance, that all are guided thereby, while that Word is fixed in its own station like the sun in the apex of heaven.

The Lord hath created naught more precious than the gem-like essence of knowledge which is conjoined with action; nor is there any knowledge but the knowledge of the Source of the command, and the comprehension of the various matters subordinate thereto, up to the Day when all return unto Him: inasmuch as the distinction between a believer and other than a believer is in this point of knowledge. Consider thou the believers in the Qur’an: it is through their knowledge that this is the Book of God that they have become “believers;” while it is through the lack of such knowledge that other than they – of all that are on earth – have become other than believers. Regard thou the Manifestation of Truth in this same wise: on the day of ’Ashura one offered up his life for Him as a sacrifice, in truth; while one inflicted upon Him that which he inflicted, in other than truth. This is purely the result of knowledge, naught else: for otherwise both share to outward seeming in the human form.

Conceive thou the likeness of the True One to be that of the sun; and the likeness of the believer to be that of a mirror, which, so only it be set towards it, will bespeak its likeness: and conceive thou the likeness of other than the believer to be that of a stone, which, however much the sun shine upon it, hath not within it the capacity of reflection. Thus it is that the one offereth up his life as a sacrifice; while the other inflicteth upon Him that which he inflicteth. Notwithstanding, were He to wish to make even that stone a mirror, He hath the power to do so; yet the stone itself hath been content to rest a stone: for had it wished to become a crystal, assuredly the Lord would have created it in a crystalline form: inasmuch as on that day, the same matter identically which was a cause of belief for the believers existed for him also; yet, because he was in a veiled condition, he allowed that same matter to shut him out therefrom as by a veil: even as today it is apparent that those who turn unto the True One, do so in virtue of the Bayan; while those who are shut out as by a veil from Him, are shut out by the same.

Conceive thou the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest to be in this same wise: whatsoever in the realm of being is possessed of any substance – in respect whereof it is entitled to the designation “thing” – or shall yet come into being, is realized through Him. Although, ere His appearance, He be unknown in His own home – nay, ere assuming recognizable proportions, He be crying in His cradle for milk – even at such a time the sustenance of all hath been, and is, from Him. All that hath been are but His former revelations; and all that is yet to be are but His latter revelations; while He Himself is that One Thing, Whose likeness is as the sun: the which, should It rise interminably, is but one in Its essence, in the realm of Innovation; and should It set interminably, is but one in Its self, in the exaltation of Its Invention; while all – from the world of the hearts, wherein the essence of the confession of the Unity of God is shining; even unto the utmost limit of the mineral, which is the lowest level of the appearance of His outpouring – derive effulgence from Its splendour.

God causeth to dwell in the chambers of Ridvan whomsoever He willeth among His servants; He, verily, is possessed of grace abounding.

Gate Five of the Sixth Unity

ordaining, with respect to greetings, that men shall use the salutation “Allah-u-Akbar” (“God is Most Great”), to which they shall respond “Allah-u-A’zam” (“God is Most Mighty”); while women shall use the salutation “Allah-u-Abha” (“God is Most Glorious”), to which they shall respond “Allah-u-Ajmal” (“God is Most Beauteous”).

The substance of this gate is that the essence of the whole Qur’an is apparent in the manifestation of the confession of God’s Grandeur, which the Lord of the world hath caused to alight in the court of the Bayan: which manifestation is none other but that first tree who, in the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, greeted God with the salutation “Allah-u-Akbar” (“God is Most Great”): to which the Lord sent down in reply: “Unto whatsoever heights thou hast soared, His Grandeur is Too Mighty for thee to be able either to describe it, or to allude thereto.” It is on account of this enfolded mystery that the order hath been given in the Bayan for greeting to be expressed by way of an affirmation of the Greatness of God; and responded to by way of an affirmation of His Might. In like manner, with respect to the possessors of circles, all should meet each other with the salutation “Allah-u-Abha,” and respond thereto with the salutation “Allah-u-Ajmal.”

The fruit thereof is that haply, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, they may be able to confess that, after the Lord, it is He in the world Who is worthy to assume the mantle of superlative Greatness, Might, Glory and Beauty, for that He is to be neither described, nor qualified, nor praised, nor extolled: perchance those who enunciate these greetings may be enabled, by the act of doing so, to turn unto that Sun of Truth; and so likewise in the case of all Names and Likenesses.

This One Reality revolveth about Itself: whence if thou lookest at the beginning of the Furqan, thou shalt see that the whole of the Revelation of Islam originated therefrom; and likewise, if thou lookest at the return, thou shalt behold the essence of all in the Last Letter: so that naught is to be seen in that return but the beginning. Although he appeared in the guise of the Pillar of Grandeur, yet his heart guided unto Glory: and on that same day whereon he evinced his learning, the sustenance thereof was from that same Point of the Qur’an, inasmuch as the things he spake of reverted unto Him. Although on that day that manifestation was in the presence of God, yet he, and all, were sustained by Him in His Former Manifestation.

Conceive thou likewise in the Dispensation of the Bayan that whatsoever there be, is from Him: and have a care that it be not to His hurt – nay, that it be for Him, not against Him. All these repeated injunctions that no soul should be a cause of sadness to another are for the sake of that Soul: for otherwise, of what consideration are all others that the Point of Truth should reveal for them this law? Yet, because in the Darkest Night the eyes perceive Him not, haply all, through the blessing of this law, may not be occasioned sorrow, and all, by this means, may travel upon the Ocean of Bounty; until the day when He shall make Himself known unto His creatures, announcing,

“I am that same Author of the Bayan, to whose prescriptions ye are all today conforming.”

As for the circumstance that all, on the Day of Resurrection, are unable to enter beneath the shadows of the Fire of God, save him whom God willeth: it is because they behold the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them to have become filled with His previous commandments: and since they look upon Him, in His Temple, with other than His own eyes, they are shut out as by a veil from recognizing Him. Yet, if only they were to look to the beginning of that same Temple they would not be thus deprived. In the case of the Daily Prayer, for example – beneath whose shadow, as thou observest, it would be impossible today to reckon how many are sheltering – consider what things, as attested in the books, the people wrought when first this command was given – things that the pen would be ashamed to recount. In this same wise regard thou the Bayan; and in this same wise behold thou also the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: so that thou mayest not be shut out as by a veil from the Sun of Truth; nor, in the ocean of multiplicity, be deprived of the Secret of Unity.

Consider today, in Islam, that whatever works the Muslims perform, they do in the name of the religion of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; and reflect a little how it fared with that Sun of Truth to Whose word Islam owed its origin. It is not that what happened in the past can afford the people any pretext for their present conduct. Far from it! The followers of Truth in that age, who were confined to those who believed in the Evangel, had all been promised the advent of that Holy Personage, alike by name and by description: yet God alone knoweth how interminably they declared their belief in His religion, in the name of Jesus – peace be upon Him – even while that Sun of Truth was unable – by one account for seven years, and by another for nine years – to make manifest the Qur’an as it truly was.

Consider likewise, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, that when He shall appear, all the believers in the Bayan shall be ensconced on the summit of their belief, and their expectation of the promised advent, and expressing themselves to this effect: yet if, at the very moment of His appearance, not one of them be shut out as by a veil from believing in Him, then shall their truthfulness be apparent; otherwise, swifter than the twinkling of an eye, all shall become as scattered dust: inasmuch as whatsoever they possess of their religion deriveth from His own Former Manifestation. Do thou exercise the utmost care that at the end of each Revelation thou allow not the very exaltation thereof to shut thee out as by a veil from the beginning of the Revelation following, for this is the very essence of knowledge, couldst thou but perceive it.

God blesseth those who believe in God and His Verses, and are firmly persuaded that, on the Day of Resurrection, they shall come into His presence.

Gate Six of the Sixth Unity: Ordaining the annulment of all books, without exception, save that which hath been written, or shall be written, in this Cause

The substance of this gate is that in each Revelation, just as the inner realities of the hearts, spirits, souls and bodies appear in a wondrous new guise, so too the fruits that are made manifest from these trees of love represent the essence of all that had appeared before: insomuch that were these hearts, or spirits, or souls, or essential bodies not to derive their sustenance therefrom, death would on the instant overtake them: and what unbeloved death is there more grievous than a sentence of other than belief?

Reflect thou, and consider: a Muslim becometh a Muslim in virtue of pronouncing the Twin Confessions: whereas these Twin Confessions existed at the time of Jesus – peace be upon Him – even as they exist today: how is it, then, that they cannot be accounted Muslims? Considering that, from the outset, the very matter to which Islam oweth its conception is in each Revelation wondrously renewed in this fashion, how must stand the case with those matters which are subordinate thereto? It is for this reason that the order hath been given for the annulment of all books, save for that which is written in affirmation of the Cause of God and of His religion.

Consider thou the Heavenly Books from the Day of Adam up to the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: although all of them were true, and sent down from God, yet on the appearance of the Furqan they all were lifted up, and in the Furqan a sentence of other than truth was passed upon the believers therein. Regard thou such to be the case likewise on the advent of each Revelation. If, therefore, even those Books which are related unto God are, on the advent of each Revelation, subject to the sentence that they are to be lifted up, what sentence should be pronounced upon the books of the people, which in comparison with those Books are but a ghostly shadow in a mirror in relation to the sun?

Methinks I see that He Whom God shall make manifest shall write unto all the Twin Confessions, incorporating His Name, these being the very essence of all religion: such that if they were to be sent down upon someone, and he were not at once to confess them true, whatsoever he had become possessed of in the Bayan would be annulled. The same is true likewise of the revelation of the Bayan: up to the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the traces of the Point, and whatsoever under their shadow serveth to guide thereunto, are the fruits of this Garden of Oneness.

As for the statement handed down in the Traditions,

“Our partisans shall on the Day of the appearance of the True One bear what they shall bear”

– this is the intention of the True One: even as, at the time of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – this same sentence applied to other than the believers in Him, notwithstanding that they derived their sustenance from that which had been sent down from God upon Jesus – peace be upon Him.

I swear by that Sacred Essence which hath never had – nor ever shall have – any partner, that on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest, to recite a single one of His Verses shall be of greater moment than to recite the whole of the Bayan, and all that hath been lifted up in the Bayan: for on that day a sentence of belief shall be passed upon that reciter, even though it be in virtue of that one single Verse; whereas upon other than he, such a sentence shall not be passed, even should he have arrived at the very highest level of exaltation in the Bayan: that is, unless he return unto God.

O people of the Bayan! Remain not shut out as by a veil from your wondrous new sustenance on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest! Nor persist ye in a veiled condition, even as the people of the Furqan have so persisted: inasmuch as they are feeding upon His former sources of subsistence; while, even on account of His wondrous new sources of subsistence, they are shut out from Him as by a veil. This is the very essence of all knowledge and action, could ye but perceive it.

God guideth whomsoever He willeth unto a path of certain truth.

Gate Seven of the Sixth Unity

concerning matrimony, and the impermissibility that the dowry should be more than ninety-five mithqals of gold for city-dwellers, and ninety-five mithqals of silver for village-dwellers, or less than nineteen mithqals in either case: which amounts should neither ascend nor descend save in steps of a Vahid, meaning the numerate Vahid, not the Vahid itself; while temporary marriage is annulled; and the marital union is established, after the parties give their consent, by means of a formula including the Word “For God.”

The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world hath, out of His bounty and grace, annulled in the Bayan the rules of temporary marriage, so that no soul may be subjected to any humiliation in the good pleasure of God, for Him; while through the consent of man and woman, and their utterance of a formula signifying that they have been, and are, for God, and are content with His decree, according to the procedures elaborated in their own places (briefly, if the bridegroom repeat the Verse “I, verily, am for God, the Lord of the heavens and the Lord of the earth, the Lord of All Things, the Lord of the seen and the unseen, the Lord of all worlds,” observing therewith the rules that have been ordained with respect to the dowry; and the other party do the same; and both affix their seal to a certificate; and there be witnesses thereunto on both sides, from their respective families) – if all of this be for God, then the marital state shall be established.

The Lord hath decreed for the dwellers of cities – by which is intended the dwellers of towns – ninety-five mithqals of gold, whereof the highest limit shall be the number of “Lillah” (“For God”), and the lowest nineteen mithqals, the number Vahid: should the which amounts, in ascending and descending, increase or decrease in steps of a Vahid, they are not to exceed five levels – whereof the first is one Vahid; the second two Vahids; the third three Vahids; the fourth four Vahids; and the fifth five Vahids; while in villages, it hath been decreed in this same wise with respect to silver, on the part of God; should the which payments exceed the topmost level by so much as a single qirat, they shall be rendered vain; and should they fall short of the lowest level by so much as the tenth of the tenth of a qirat, they shall likewise be rendered vain.

The matter hath been commanded in this wise so that all those charged with this obligation may enjoy the grace, and the abundance of the mercy, of the True One. Should they wish to expend their wealth in other ways on these occasions – even to bestow thousands upon thousands upon each other – there is no harm therein; or should they wish to expend it on the occasions of the marriage, there is no objection thereto. The matter hath been ordained in this wise so that all may enjoy the abundance of the grace and mercy of the True One; and thereto have regard for that to which the legitimacy of the marital union oweth its conception, which is the Word “For God:” perchance, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, they shall not stray beyond the Mirror of this Word, Who guideth unto God: for if a person, at the time of His appearance, were not to believe in Him, he would – notwithstanding that he professed himself to be “for God” – be adjudged vain; unless on that day, through His command, whatsoever might befall of the occasions of religion were upheld.

All peoples indeed imagine that whatsoever they do, they do “for God;” yet, if truly they performed it for God, why was it rejected? The same is true in Islam: if all, on the appearance of the Imams – peace be upon them – had been acting for God, how was it that they were rendered vain? Likewise, on the appearance of the Sun of Truth, if a person had been acting for God, he would not have deviated from His Mirror. All those whom thou observest to declare “We act for God;” or to recite the Verse “Verily, my prayer, my devotion, my life, and my death are for God, the Lord of all worlds,” are in the sight of God untruthful; for otherwise, a sentence of “for other than God” would not have been passed upon them. Nay, only in their own conceit do they act for Him; for in truth they perform against Him whatsoever they do. Thus it is that all works, through the recognition of this and this alone, are either accepted or rendered vain.

If in the Bayan, up to the time of the Revelation, all act for God, they shall indeed be acting “for God,” inasmuch as they are reposing beneath the shadow of His Mirror, whence the works they perform are, in the sight of God, acceptable. On the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, however, if they act for Him, then shall they truly have been acting “for God;” for otherwise God hath created betwixt Truth and falsehood no third alternative. Whoever acteth for Him, is raised up under the shadow of “but God;” and whoever acteth for other than Him, is raised up under the shadow of Negation. Yet at all events, all are circling about this Mirror.

For example, whatever works the people of Jesus – peace be upon Him – perform, they do, in their own conceit, for the Lord, through the intermediary of Jesus – peace be upon Him – Who in that age was the Mirror that guided unto God; yet at the time of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – if any among the Christians believed in His Holiness, he it was who had been acting for God; otherwise the untruthfulness of all was revealed in the sight of God, in virtue of that thing which was revealed on the part of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: for the Eternal Essence hath never been, nor ever shall be, amenable to change: whereas to testify of something according to a former state is a testimony to a capacity for change: whence the one who admitteth of such a description is His Manifestation – namely, the Primal Will – Whose testimony is, in each Revelation, that to which the Lord hath borne witness; while that to which the Essence hath borne witness none knoweth but He; and He hath ever been, and ever shall be, a witness of all things ere yet they came into existence: while His testimony with respect to All Things before they came into existence is even as His testimony with respect to all things after they came into existence. None understandeth the manner of it save Him. Glorified is God above all that ye might testify with respect to Him.

Naught can avail to save one unless one be truthful in acting for God; nor, by the same token, can aught avail to shut one out as by a veil from recognizing Him unless, in one’s own self – under the conceit of being “for God” – one becometh shut out in this manner; for otherwise there is no soul who, betwixt himself and God, would wish to disobey Him: nay rather, he imagineth that he is for God, though all the while he hath been for other than God. It is for this reason that his works are rendered vain.

Consider thou the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest: all those in the Bayan who are performing their works for the Lord shall have been doing so in virtue of the proof constituted by the Verses of God: and on that Day, when this same proof also shall be present, how could it come about that they should not perform their works for Him? Even as, at the time of the appearance of the Bayan, words of a like tenor were addressed to all the people of the Furqan: yet, he that was not for God could not accept them; while he that was for God accepted them forthwith.

Thus it is that on the advent of each Revelation, the Lord of the world testeth His servants so as to make known unto them, by their own selves, whether they have been acting for Him, or for another than Him: even as, on the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – He made known unto each believer in the Evangel who claimed to be acting for God in the religion of Jesus – peace be upon Him – how truthfully he spake: and however many of them entered the fold of Islam, just so many had truly been acting for God, and were sincerely devoted to the religion of Jesus – peace be upon Him; while all besides them were not acting for God, and were not judged to have been sincerely devoted to the law of Jesus, the Spirit of God – peace be upon Him: for otherwise, the Lord of the world is too great and glorious for someone who is acting for Him to be suffered to enter into the Fire.

Regard thou in like manner the time of the appearance of the Bayan: whosoever among the people of the Qur’an entered within its fold was truly for God; otherwise was he for other than God, and only conceived in his own fancy that he was acting for God, while all the time, in the sight of God, he was acting for other than Him: and the degrees of “other than,” and the names thereof, are apparent in the eyes of the believers in the Bayan, insomuch that every “other than goodly” description is applicable thereto.

Considering that to act for God is dependent upon acting for the one who manifesteth His Cause, if in the Qur’an anyone acted for the manifestations of the Cause of the True One (who were Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; the House of Muhammad – peace be upon them; and the Gates of Guidance), he acted for God; otherwise he reverteth not unto God. The Mirror of God aforetime was the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – through the effulgence of the sun of Whose bounty in the eighteen Mirrors, these latter became the Mirror of “For God,” even for the Lord: and since all those who acted for the Lord were sheltering beneath the shadow of the manifestations of His Cause, that which they performed for God became accordingly acceptable in His sight.

In the Bayan likewise, if it is acceptable for anyone to pronounce therein the Confession of the Unity of God without conjoining this with the mention of the Manifestation of the Cause, assuredly it would be acceptable for him to perform his works also “for God” without performing them for the Manifestation of the Cause. I take as examples the Evangel and the Furqan in order that the matter may be made the easier for thee with regard to the Bayan and Him Whom God shall make manifest.

For example, the Confession of the Unity of God was not accepted in the Evangel unless conjoined to a testimony to Jesus, the Spirit of God – peace be upon Him; and likewise the testimony to Jesus – peace be upon Him – was not accepted unless conjoined to a testimony to His Letters of the Living, in that age. The specification of “Hayy” (“Living”) is to the end that all may guide unto this Vahid, so that thou mayest not see “Two;” for otherwise all that thou seest in the Evangel is the proliferation of that same First Vahid, though it be a single soul, alike whether he be in the East or in the West. If anyone in the Evangel were acting for God, he was acting for the Letters of the Vahid of that Revelation, inasmuch as whatsoever reverted unto them, reverted unto God.

Now, even had they all performed their works for those Letters of the Vahid, still, all that reverted unto them would revert effectively unto God. Yet when, on the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – they believed not in Him, all that they had done for God, and for the Letters of their age, was rendered vain: unless anyone among them returned unto Him, in which case he it was who had truly been acting for God and the Letters of the Vahid in that Revelation; else had he not been truthful in the sight of God: for otherwise he would have been graciously assisted to believe in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and to believe in His Letters of the Living.

Whereas thou seest that millions upon millions act for God, through the Letters of the Vahid in the Evangel; while in reality they dwell in the Fire, and perform their works for other than God.

Regard thou such to be the case also in the Qur’an: from the beginning of its appearance up to the year one thousand two hundred and seventy, anyone who was truly acting for God was among those servants who were for Muhammad; the House of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; and the Gates of Guidance: whence if someone were in the first instance for Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him; yet not in the second instance for the Commander of the Faithful, he was not truthful in his claim to be for God; and such would be the case likewise in each successive instance, until the sequence terminated in the last of the Gates. However if, from the time of the appearance of the Bayan, anyone were truly for God in respect of Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and the manifestations of His Cause – he it is who was for God in respect of the Point of the Bayan and the manifestations of His Cause.

In like manner, on the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest thou shalt observe all to declare, “We act for God, and believe in the Letters of the Vahid:” yet if, at the time of His Revelation, they act through Him for God, assuredly they speak true; otherwise that which, betwixt themselves and God, they do for God shall all at once be rendered vain – and with how much greater reason that which they do for the Letters of the Vahid, or for the believers in the Bayan, who only in virtue of their relation unto Him are judged to be “for God!” For that sign whereto the servant turneth betwixt himself and God, beholding the Beauty of God in his own heart; and purposing his every action to be “for God,” is a sign that hath shone forth within the hearts of all from Him Whom God shall make manifest, ere yet He hath appeared; which sign is in His eyes like unto the sun in a mirror in relation to the sun in heaven: for the outward form of the Tree of Truth, under the aspect of servitude, shineth upon the hearts of all; whereas the inner essence thereof shineth upon the signs of the hearts wherein naught is seen but God, single and alone: for otherwise, how would it be possible for the servant to act betwixt himself and God for God, and the Manifestation of Truth not to accept from him his works? – forasmuch as that which he doeth betwixt himself and God is the similitude of that sign of Reality, which hath shone forth within him from that Sun of Truth.

For example, if the Apostle of God had not instructed “Perform your works for God,” would anyone forsooth have known that he was to perform his works for God? Shouldst thou represent that the same idea was expressed in different terms, observe that herein lieth the point, for this too is in virtue of that Apostle in whose Revelation those concerned were raised up; and so too in each preceding Revelation, until the matter endeth in the beginning that hath no beginning; and so too from hence forwards, until the matter endeth in the succeeding Revelations, for which there is no end.

For example, at the time when someone, betwixt himself and God, inflicteth sorrow upon the Point of the Bayan, that sign by virtue of which, betwixt himself and God, he performeth such an act, purposing it to be “for God,” is a sign which hath shone forth within him from the sun of His bounty: yet because, in the succeeding Revelation, he is not a believer therein, he becometh shut out as by a veil from perceiving the true complexion of the case. Whereas in the preceding Revelation, wert thou to assert “This sign is through the intermediary of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him,” he would assent thereto, for he hath neither heard nor seen aught else but this; nor was the sign made manifest in this present Revelation.

Consider thou the case in the Qur’an at the time of the conjunction of two souls, both of whom were performing their works “for God.” For example, the Prince of Martyrs – peace be upon him – since he acted for the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – was truly for God; whereas he that wrought against his Holiness, although in his own eyes he was for God, was in fact for other than God; while his Holiness was at that time the physical counterpart, in the fifth sense, of that very sign wherein, betwixt himself and God, he saw none but God: whence if the veil had been removed, he would have seen that whatsoever he did “for God,” he did through him and for him, even though, in his veiled condition, he perpetrated it against him.

All this prolixity is to the end that haply, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, ye may not recline at ease within yourselves, claiming “Whatsoever we do, we do for God:” inasmuch as this sign in virtue whereof ye turn unto God is but a ghostly shadow from the sun of His bounty, within the sign of your own beings, which hath shone forth from His own Former Manifestation; and which if, in His Latter Manifestation, ye direct squarely towards Him, ye shall be for Him, even as aforetime ye were for the Point of the Bayan; otherwise, betwixt yourselves and God, ye shall not have acted for God: for the Lord hath ordained “Whatsoever ye do for Me shall not revert unto Me unless ye do it for Him:” inasmuch as the contingent being is unable to grasp the nature of the Eternal Essence; nay, should ye grasp the nature of His Manifestation, then only so far as lieth within your capacity as a contingent being shall ye have grasped the nature of the One Who is made manifest in this Manifestation.

For example, at the time when the one who gave order for this mountain considered, betwixt himself and God, a particular measure, and commanded its execution, that same “betwixt himself and God” of his, wherein he had mounted up, is a sign which hath appeared within him through the Former Manifestation of this same Being – the physical counterpart of that sign within him – Whom since he hath failed to recognize, he hath accordingly acted in this fashion: for indeed had he known that this is that same Point of the Furqan, in His Latter Manifestation, from Whom hath derived that sign within all Muslims in virtue whereof they turn unto God, assuredly he would not have consented that the very idea of such a measure should enter his heart; how much less that he should give order for its execution: inasmuch as night and day, betwixt himself and God, through His Apostle, he seeketh to draw nigh unto God.

On the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest likewise, all the believers in the Bayan shall be similarly afflicted, conceiving to themselves “We act for God,” even while they work against the One Who, in the world of creation, is the Sun of those signs in virtue whereof they had previously been seeking to draw nigh unto God, and which had shone forth refulgent in their own souls. Nor know ye this to be the case; for otherwise there is no fiercer fire for anyone than to inflict upon his Best-Beloved that which he would allow only in the case of his other-than-best-beloved, even though, from the beginning of his life until the end of his life, he doeth whatsoever he doeth – if he doeth it for God – in virtue of the sign he hath within him from his Best-Beloved.

Observe thou how momentous is this matter! Those who truly perform their works for God, perform them, “in the horizons,” for Muhammad – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and the manifestations of His Cause; and, “in the souls,” in virtue of the signs that have shone forth within them from the Letters of the Vahid of the Furqan: yet since they are shut out as by a veil from apprehending the secret of the matter, all that they do becometh, in this Revelation, for other than God: for had anyone been truly for God, he would not have infringed against the Sun of Truth in this wondrous new Revelation: nay, whatsoever any of them possesseth is from His previous Revelation: whence in the wondrous new Revelation, not one of them can be adjudged to be truly for God, unless he enter within the fold of this Revelation.

Consider thou the period extending from the Day of Adam up to the appearance of the Bayan: and regard thou also the preceding and succeeding ages in this same light. Not so much as the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of a second hath passed over God’s creatures without their having amongst them a Book from Him, in virtue whereof they have believed in His religion; while in each Revelation, those who acted conformably thereto were acting for God, on condition that they performed whatever works had been prescribed therein according as had been sent down therein. Consider, therefore, how unsparingly all that they had done for God in accordance with these Books up to the Revelation of the Furqan became for other than God: for had it truly been for God, they must needs have entered within the fold of belief in the Furqan.

Regard thou likewise the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest in relation to the Revelation of the Bayan: if anyone in the Bayan be truly for God, his being “for God” is not made apparent save in virtue of his being for the Letters of the Vahid; while those who have proliferated in the “ghostly shadow of the ghostly shadow” are, at their own level, judged to be in the same case as the Vahid of the Vahid: insomuch that on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, the whole of the Bayan is but a single Vahid, in the numerate sense: which Vahid reverteth unto the innumerate Vahid, which is none other but the person of Him Whom God shall make manifest: whereafter the Letters of the Living shine forth anew through Him: after which the First Vahid proliferateth again, even unto the day of the Latter Manifestation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: at the time of Whose appearance, all must become once more a single Vahid, wherein naught is to be seen but the innumerate Vahid, Who is He Himself.

Even as today, all the believers in the Qur’an are but the ghostly shadows of that First Vahid, which endeth in the Letters of the Living, whence in turn it endeth in the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him.

Look thou to the Secret of Existence, and regard not the Sun in the Mirror to be in the same case as the Sun of Truth; nor regard thou the mirrors standing after that Mirror to be in the same case as those mirrors which stand directly before it. It is for this reason that, upon the appearance of the True One, not all are able to be guided by the Sun of Truth: for in the same way as the bounty of existence hath come unto them through the mirrors that preceded them, so too is it with respect to guidance.

Consider thou, for example, the case of the lowliest rustic, who, were he himself to encounter the Sun of Truth, would not be able to be guided through His guidance, inasmuch as he is lying at his own lowly level: notwithstanding that, even at this level, were he to look to the Source of Command, he would at once be able to be so guided; yet since such perception doth not exist within him, it would be hard for him to realize this in practice: unless he were to refer to the divine of his village; and this divine to refer to the divine above himself; and so on, little by little, until this process culminated in someone who was able to understand the utterance of the Gates of Guidance; and culminating from thence, little by little, it reached someone who was able to understand the utterance of the Imams; and from thence, little by little, it ascended upwards, until it reached someone who understood the Utterance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: whereupon the matter would arrive before a divine with knowledge of the hearts, who would be able to understand the Utterance of God – which Utterance is of a nature that, when it cometh upon the Apostle, He submitteth Himself thereto at once; whilst the exaltation of His own station of Apostle, in comparison therewith, becometh as naught.

Yet by contrast that rustic, if one day an Epistle were sent down upon him, would not submit himself unto the Sun of Truth, inasmuch as he hath all these intervening veils before his heart, until the which be rent asunder, he would not be able to grasp the true complexion of the case.

The same circumstance is observable in this Mountain of Mah-Ku where, although the Verses of God are being sent down in every mode, no fruit is forthcoming from its inhabitants; howbeit, were the veil to be removed, through the rending asunder of the obstacles to vision – who are the intervening souls – they would at once, each at his own level, believe in God and His Verses: even as the Jewel of All Existence, the moment He hearkened thereto, believed – notwithstanding all the glory and exaltation of His essence, which is such as cannot be compared with all else, how much less with any particular thing. This is the meaning of “That which is hidden to the heart of the Prophet is preferable to the worship of both worlds:” inasmuch as this Soul, for all His gem-like abstraction, becometh at the time of the revelation of the Verses submissive and lowly, confessing the Unity of God; whereas that soul, who by means of a thousand intervening souls hath been guided through His guidance, is not, when he hearkeneth thereto, “cast down in fragments,” but cannot even comprehend what he heareth, how much less believe therein; or be able, after believing, to act in accordance therewith.

O ye witnesses of the Bayan! Be not, at the time of Revelation, shut out as by a veil therefrom, for your likeness is even such as hath been set forth: only through an interminable succession of intermediaries have ye understood the Utterance of the Truth. At the time of His appearance, stand ye abashed before Him, so that ye may not be kept distant therefrom – beyond the highest limit of their proliferation – even should ye not be drawn nigh thereto: inasmuch as the beings and works of the people of the Bayan are all, in His eyes, as a fruit in the palm of His hand, which He revolveth howsoever He willeth, and by whatsoever means He willeth. He that transporteth the mirrors of your very beings from the shadow of for God, rendering them instead for other than God – through that very matter whereby ye are shut out as by a veil from Him – how shall stand the case with your works in His sight? Reflect ye therefore upon the creation of your own hearts: then reason on this basis how must stand the case with Him.

All these explanations were to the end that marital unions should be for God, not for other than God, so that if any fruit be forthcoming in the world of being, it should be for God. Methinks I can discern that at the time of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, all, betwixt themselves and God, shall perform their works for God; whereas He shall adjudge them to be for other than God: unless there be someone who performeth his works for Him, when he it is who, in the sight of God, shall have performed his works for God. The same is true in the case of the Bayan: should anyone perform his works for the Letters of the Vahid, then hath he performed them for God; and this same principle applieth thereafter at each successive level, down to the lowliest atom, if the which be for the exaltation of the Bayan, then is it judged to be for God.

In the Furqan likewise, so long as the line of appointment of the manifestations of the Divine Command had not been severed, whatsoever works were performed in obedience to their commands were performed for God; whereas from the time of the severance of this line, whatsoever works were performed in accordance with their commands were performed for God: as in the case, for example, of the divines of the Furqan, who all performed their works in accordance with the Book of God, and with the traces of the Apostle, the Imams of Guidance, and the Gates of Guidance. In this Revelation too, so long as the line of appointment hath not been severed, whatsoever works are performed in obedience thereto shall be for God; whereas after its severance, whatsoever works are performed in accordance therewith shall be for God.

Stray ye not beyond the Letters of the Vahid: haply, when the Day of Resurrection dawneth, ye may be able to be guided through their guidance. In the same way as naught can definitely be asserted to be for God unless it be “and for the Apostle of God,” so likewise naught can truly be stated to be for God unless (beginning with that Source on the one hand, and ending with the last of whatsoever commands proceed therefrom on the other) it be for the manifestations of His Command. Anyone who acteth in accordance with whatsoever is in the Bayan becometh a ghostly image of the Letters of the Bayan, until the matter endeth in the furthest limit of existence.

Do ye exercise the utmost vigilance lest, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, whatsoever works ye have performed for God become for other than God: for if they be performed for Him, then shall they have been performed both for God and for the Point; otherwise shall they be rendered vain.

This is what God, your Lord, counselleth you, should ye act obediently thereto.

Gate Eight of the Sixth Unity

On this, that he who adduceth any proof other than the Book of God and the verses of the Bayan, as well as the powerlessness of all to produce the like thereof, he is veiled from any proof, and he who reporteth any miracle other than the verses, is veiled from any testimony, and he who claimeth to reveal divine verses, should not be opposed by anyone. All must recite this gate once in every nineteen days, and ponder, day and night, upon that which is revealed therein.

The substance of this gate is this, that should anyone adduce any proof other than the verses of God to vindicate the truth of the Point of the Bayan, he would be veiled from the most mighty proof and the most exalted path. Though in each Revelation, all the attributes of the very Tree of Truth barreth all others from any resemblance, association, likeness, equivalence, or similarity unto Him, yet inasmuch as the eyes of the heart of the multitude fail to behold the supreme exaltation of His own Self, and inasmuch as the divine verses are revealed in a manner that if all desire to understand, they would be able to do so, therefore, He hath ordained the testimony to be but one, namely the verses.

The purpose of this gate is this, that in the Day of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, He would not be told why or wherefore. Likewise, in all that is revealed in the Qur’an, the sole proof that is adduced is the revelation of the verses, and had all comprehended that, today acknowledging the Truth would have been an easier lot for them than this clinging to the authority of strange miracles, the report of which they themselves have devised, when in truth there is no warrant for any of them in the Book of God.

Nay, rather, if He reject any miracle, acting in conformity with that which is ordained in the Book of God, that would eternally be, as it hath always been, the Command of God. Thus it is enjoined upon all to gaze upon this gate once in every nineteen days, that haply in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, they would not be veiled by any condition besides the modes of the verses, which is the most mighty testimony and proof.

But be warned lest ye gaze upon it once every nineteen days, and yet the Desired One revealeth Himself, and ye fail to recognise Him due to your veils. Just as ye read every morning the covenant prayer, and yet by your excessive utterance “may God hasten His coming, may God hasten His coming,” ye conceal from yourselves your real hate of Him, and imagine that ye love Him. Now it is almost more than three years, and the Cause of God hath been manifested, and yet today ye have imprisoned your Desired One in the mountain.

Yet, He hath appeared with the same testimony that the religion of all Muslims is founded upon it, to the degree that after the termination of God’s revelation unto Muhammad till the manifestation of these verses, none hath appeared who produced a single verse. Ye are so deprived of insight that ye fail to comprehend that none besides God can reveal any verse. Therefore, now that ye witness that the same testimony is manifested, ye must know of a certainty that the Point of the Bayan is the same Primal Truth unto Whom the Qur’an was sent by God in the early days of Islam, and thus ye discern that God now desireth to once again reveal unto Him His verses.

Had ye firmly believed in the testimony of your religion, ye would have pondered this truth, inasmuch as there are but two options therefor. God verily hath explicitly revealed in the Qur’an the powerlessness of all in regard to this supreme testimony. But ye cast an indiscriminate glance around you, and inasmuch as ye behold Him as one amongst the multitude of the people, ye imagine that such Revelation is impossible, therefore ye become veiled from Him, even though God is sending down His verses in this Day of Return, in exactly the same manner that He revealed them in the Day of the Beginning. Should ye behold with this gaze, ye would acknowledge the truth in less than the twinkling of an eye. But inasmuch as ye gaze upon the created beings, ye find it impossible. Yea, it is impossible for the creatures, but not for God, inasmuch as He doeth whatsoever He willeth, by virtue of His supreme power.

It is perfectly evident that after the setting of the Sun of Truth none can produce the like of His verses, even as in the 1270 years of the Dispensation of the Qur’an all have become certain of the powerlessness of all. In like manner, it shall also be impossible that after the setting of the Sun of Truth, a single verse would be manifested by anyone but Him, out of primordial nature and supreme power, and without acquisition and the other conditions prevalent amongst the men of knowledge.

Notwithstanding this impossibility, that none besides Him Whom God shall make manifest will be able to claim such a mighty Cause, it is enjoined in the Bayan that should anyone make a claim and verses are manifested from Him, no one should oppose Him, that haply no grief would assail that Sun of Truth. Had this command been observed in the Dispensation of the Qur’an, the deeds of all would not have suddenly come to naught. For in dealing with the Lord, should one fail to become for God, yet he also refuse to become against Him, he would only be judged by his own misdeed and not by those of all the people.

Therefore, if ye now hear of such claim and fail to be certain, refuse to commit that which grieveth Him, even though it would be a false claim by someone other than Him, although this is an impossible supposition. However, the mere mention of His exalted name should suffice His lovers to refuse to inflict sorrow upon the claimant, as a token of respect for Him. For the truth is but one of the two: Either the claimant is truly Him, although naught else is possible inasmuch as none besides Him can reveal verses out of primordial nature, then why should anyone reject God while all his deeds, day and night, are performed in ardent waiting for Him. Or, making an impossible assumption, the claimant is falsely attributing himself unto Him, then leave his judgement unto God, inasmuch as the created beings have no right to judge against him, as a token of their glorification of the name of their Beloved, even though no one can make such a claim. If in the Dispensation of the Qur’an any claim to revelation of the verses hath happened, then it could happen in this Dispensation as well!

His verses are, by themselves, sufficient proof of the radiant lights of the Sun of His Being, just as the powerlessness of all is the mighty evidence of the utter need and dependence of all unto Him. The reason for this command is this, that haply in the Day of the Revelation of that supreme Truth, the feet of the people would not falter upon the bridge, and that they would not pronounce judgement against the Fashioner of their existence, adducing against Him the very shadow of His verse in their heart, and rendering naught, at once, all their inmost realities and deeds, without even perceiving it.

Should all act in conformity with this law, it would befit God to reveal the Truth unto them, and to cast, by virtue of the evidences that shine forth from Him, conclusive testimony and proof in their hearts, that the faithful can proclaim their certitude of His truth, and the non-faithful would be empowered to declare their hesitation, inasmuch as hesitation with regard to truth is naught but untruth.

Should the people of the Bayan observe this command, it would suffice to cause them salvation in the Day of Resurrection. For in that Day, all on earth, acknowledging the verses that have shone forth in their heart from the Sun of Truth, shall declare “We verily act for God.” However, the truthful are only those servants who fix their gaze upon He Who hath fashioned, by the grace of God, glorified and exalted be Him, those verses, Who is none but the very Sun of Truth. And it would be His verses, which are His radiant lights, that shall separate amongst all things. This is the supreme testimony of God that is fulfilled unto you. Be then fearful, O servants of God!

Gate Nine of the Sixth Unity: Ordaining that the use of silken garments is permitted under all conditions, and so likewise the use of gold and silver vessels

The substance of this gate is that the Lord of the world hath permitted unto each soul the wearing of silken garments, under all conditions; and likewise the use of gold and silver vessels: so that all, having attained in this Paradise unto whatsoever is conducive to the tranquillity of the servants’ hearts, may, on the Day of Revelation, express their utmost thanks to God, through believing in Him Whom God shall make manifest: for even were they to expend all that is on earth, they would have had no way to secure such a law: howbeit, the Lord of the world – exalted and glorified be He – hath, by way of His bounty and grace, permitted those capable of benefiting therefrom to do so.

Let no soul, however, experience any sorrow if he be not able to enjoy this bounty: for, out of purest love, the Lord shall double his reward and recompense, and deal graciously with him in the world to come. Howbeit, should anyone, in virtue of any of these outward manifestations, wish to vaunt himself over another, or to evince his exaltation above him, he shall be shut out as by a veil from the good pleasure of his Best-Beloved. Nay, in every matter wherein the Lord showeth favour unto His servant through the manifestations of His material domain, it is befitting that he evince a greater measure of humility and lowliness before the people: which comportment is for him the means whereby, at his own level, he may demonstrate his thankfulness to God.

There is no honour or glory in these outward appearances, save through belief in Him Whom God shall make manifest: for had any honour resided in such trappings, they are found today in greater abundance amongst the Christians than amongst any other people: whereas these cannot even be adjudged believers, how much less endued with honour. Howbeit, if these benefits be conjoined with belief, then is the enjoyment thereof but an evidencing of the bestowals of God in respect of His servant.

Should anyone acquire vessels of gold or silver, and thereby bestow life upon another, it shall be better for him than aught he hath acquired, and wherein he delighteth in the good pleasure of his Best-Beloved: for the hearts of the believers are the dwelling-place of the good pleasure of the True One: and there is no doubt that, in the eyes of the Lord, the good pleasure of the believers taketh precedence over the good pleasure of the one who owneth the thing in question, and taketh delight therein.

This, however, is when regard is not had for the bounds of God’s creation: for wert thou to have regard for the chain of existence, there is no doubt that the good pleasure of the one situated higher up this chain is, in the sight of God, of greater consequence than the good pleasure of those situated in the ranks below him.

For example, if there be aught whereby the soul of Him Whom God shall make manifest becometh joyful, this, in the eyes of God, is of greater moment than that the whole of existence should be rendered joyful; and the same is true of all the Names and Likenesses, the nearest taking precedence over the nearer, down to the final atoms of existence. Howbeit, only on the Day of Resurrection can this ranking be distinguished; whereas at Night it is impossible, inasmuch as all pretend to exaltation, and to nearness unto the True One, whence none is able to discern a person’s true station save the Tree of Truth: while He divulgeth not the ranks of God’s creation. It is fitting, therefore, that everyone should act according to the former ruling, so that no sorrow may befall any soul on the surface of the earth, of those who believe in God and His Verses.

Thus doth God relieve you of that which previously had been burdensome unto you, and permitteth you in the Book that in virtue whereof ye may be thankful.

Gate Ten of the Sixth Unity

ordaining that it is incumbent upon all to engrave upon an agate ring the following Verse:

“Say: God is the Truth; and all else besides God is His creation; and all worship Him.”

The substance of this gate is that no observance in the Bayan is more beloved in the eyes of the Lord than that one should wear upon one’s hand a ring of crimson agate, whereon is engraved this mighty Verse:

“Say: God is the Truth; and all else besides God is His creation; and all worship Him.”

The fruit thereof is that this is a testimony, on the part of the Point of Truth, that the Lord hath ever been, and ever shall be, the Truth; while all else besides Him have ever been, and ever shall be, His creation: haply, on the Day of the appearance of the True One – when He shall be made manifest with that Truth whereby the truth of every truth is established – the wearer of this ring may confess that all else besides the Lord is His creation: not that this ring should be upon his hand, and the True One appear, and he not bring forth the fruit of this Verse before that embodiment of the Truth. Should He be made manifest, and anyone not confess Him to be true, this same ring he weareth shall testify against him, and render vain whatsoever he had wrought in the Bayan.

It is not that to confess His truth is a perplexing matter. Nay, whatsoever confessions have ever been made in the world to the truth of aught were precisely in virtue of His truth: however, since it is the case that the appearance of the True One representeth for the followers of Truth Paradise, and for other than they Fire – it is for this reason that all are tested on that Day; while He for His part is the Mirror of Godhead and the Sun of Lordship, Who hath guideth ever unto God, single and alone.

Should a person wish to cause himself to enter within the protection of the True One, let him give order for a circular agate to be engraved with the figure of the familiar circle, made up of five Vahids, whereof in the first appeareth the “Verse of the Throne;” in the second, the circumferent Names; in the third, the letters of the “Basmalah;” in the fourth, the Six Names; and in the fifth, whatsoever suiteth his own state and aims, the which should not exceed nineteen letters: and if in the first and second circles too he inscribe no more than nineteen letters it would be well-pleasing in the eyes of the True One. All these specifications, however, are subject to one’s apprehending, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, precisely what it is he hath engraved within these circles: for the first thereof is none other but those Letters of the First Vahid who proliferate in the “Hayy” (“Living”) until, in the fifth degree, they are made manifest to the number of “Lillah” (“For God”).

Shouldst thou believe in the Letters of the Living of Him Whom God shall make manifest, having once entered within the First Vahid, through the strength and power of the Lord, thou shalt remain therein even should it proliferate to an illimitable extent. If thou wert in the Revelation of the Point of the Bayan, thou hast beheld this matter with thine outward eye, observing how all were guided through the guidance of those same First Letters. Nor is the one guided other than the image of the one who guided. Thus it is that even should the Vahid propagate itself to an illimitable extent, it is naught but that same First Vahid. This, in the world of creation, is the manner of the generation of all the atoms. Behold thou likewise other matters as conforming to the generation of realities in the world of creation; nor be shut out as by a veil from the Sun of Revelation.

Whatsoever mirror thou observest to bear Its reflection, do thou love it: for that is a Name which guideth unto Him; and whatsoever thing thou observest to guide not unto Him – be it a single atom of clay in the possession of other than a believer – do thou pass upon it a sentence of Negation: for on the Day of Resurrection, that which is for Him Whom God shall make manifest is “For God;” while that which is for other than He is “For other than God.” Regard thou such to be the case likewise with the Point of the Bayan; even as, ere His appearance, such was the case also with the Point of the Furqan; and such too, in the Revelation prior to His, with the Point of the Evangel; and such too with all the preceding Revelations until the matter endeth with the Wondrous First Creation. Likewise, in all succeeding Revelations – ascending upwards from Him Whom God shall make manifest until the end that hath no end – do thou behold, and witness, that which thou hast witnessed in this present Resurrection; and under all conditions say “There is no God but God: we all, verily, are devoted unto Him.”

Gate Eleven of the Sixth Unity

concerning this, that it is not permitted a teacher to administer to a child more than five light slaps: while even to strike a child, ere he attain the age of five, is absolutely forbidden: whereafter it is forbidden to administer more than five slaps, dealt, not upon the skin, but upon the garments: and if he administer more than five such slaps, or deal them upon the flesh, it is forbidden him to draw nigh unto his wife for nineteen days, even should these acts have resulted from mere forgetfulness on his part: or, if he have no consort, let him pay to the one whom he hath struck nineteen mithqals of gold; and God hath permitted children to amuse themselves during feast days with whatsoever playthings they have in their hands; and everyone should repose upon a chair, inasmuch as the time one spendeth reposing upon a chair, or upon a couch or throne, is not accounted a part of one’s mortal life.

The substance of this gate is that under no conditions is it pleasing unto the Lord that any soul should be occasioned sorrow, how much less that injury should befall him: whence all have been forbidden, ere a child attain the age of five, to chastise him verbally; neither should they inflict upon him any sorrow: while after he attaineth the age of five, they should not exceed the limit of five light slaps, which should be dealt, not upon the flesh, but with the interposition of a cushion; nor should these be administered in an otherwise than dignified fashion, as is the custom of this present age.

Should anyone, in administering such chastisement, exceed the limit of five such slaps, for nineteen days it is not lawful for him to enjoy marital union; and should he not have a consort, it behoveth him to render, as a fine for his transgression of the bounds fixed by God, nineteen mithqals of gold unto the one whom he hath struck.

It is well-pleasing unto the Lord that under all conditions the people of the Bayan should seat themselves upon couches, thrones or chairs, inasmuch as the time one spendeth so reposing is not accounted a part of his mortal life.

The fruit of these ordinances is that haply no sorrow may befall that Soul, from the ocean of Whose bounty all are brought into being: for the teacher recognizeth not the One Who is alike his own Preceptor and the Preceptor of all: even as, in the Revelation of the Furqan, ere forty years had elapsed, no one recognized the Sun of Truth; while in the case of the Point of the Bayan, full twenty-five years had passed ere He was recognized; and the Lord alone knoweth what span of life He may have destined Him to pass ere He be recognized – the which are His days of happiness.

Although all expectantly await His advent, yet because they look not to Him, it is inevitable that sorrow should come upon Him: even as it came upon the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: inasmuch as all, ere the revelation of the Furqan, acknowledged the excellence of His perfection and piety: whereas after the revelation of the Furqan, see only what things they did not say about Him! – uttering such expressions as the pen would be ashamed to set forth.

Regard thou in this wise also the Point of the Bayan: His personal dispositions ere He was made manifest are evident unto those who knew Him: whereas after His manifestation – notwithstanding that up to this present day no less than five hundred thousand verses, in diverse modes, have been revealed by Him – some still give utterance to such expressions as the pen would be ashamed to set forth.

Howbeit if all act according as God hath bidden, no sorrow shall befall that Tree: for if it be made a rule that no one should occasion sadness to another, then He too is one amongst the people: and should they not actively undertake to realize the purpose for which they were created – yet so only they draw not nigh unto the reverse, then hath there never been, nor ever shall be, any greater bounty than this.

Notwithstanding, it is even now discernible that His days of happiness are the days prior to His manifestation: for although He shall be made manifest amidst a people who have been, and are, infatuated with His love, yet regard thou the condition at that time to be even as today, when all do whatever they do in His Name, while consenting to befall Him that whereto they consent. O ye servants of God, fear Me!

Gate Twelve of the Sixth Unity

concerning this, that divorce is not permitted unless the man bide patiently with the woman for one (Vahid) year: perchance He may reconcile the twain: and should He not reconcile them, it is permitted them to part; while it is permitted him to return whensoever he wisheth, up to nineteen times; neither is he required to bide in patience after returning, but for a month.

The substance of this gate is that after the Lord hath joined together two souls through the Word “For God,” it is not befitting that the conditions of the tree of other than love should become apparent, inasmuch as separation hath never been, nor ever shall be, among the conditions of the tree of love. Whence, until a person be compelled thereto, it shall not be lawful unto him; and if he be compelled thereto, and inform the other party of the matter, it behoveth him to bide in patience throughout the revolution of one year, composed of nineteen months of the Bayan: at the end of which, if the evidences of affection have become once more apparent, the need for separation shall have been removed; otherwise, it is at this time permissible through a Word indicative of this course.

Thereafter he is permitted to return unto his spouse up to nineteen times; and from the time of separation up to the time of returning it behoveth him to bide in patience for nineteen days, so as to rid himself of the conditions of the Gates of the Fire: then, when the number nineteen is complete, marital union is permitted him: and in this wise, so long as the number Vahid hath not been reached, he is permitted to reunite with his spouse; while after the number nineteen hath been reached, this is no longer permitted: for the process would then enter the domain of duality: whereas in Paradise there hath never been, nor ever shall be, any condition of duality: inasmuch as all have been created from one (Vahid) soul: whence so soon as the degree of One (Vahid) be complete, another One (Vahid) must be initiated – not Two – so that even should Vahids proliferate to an illimitable extent, they are still this same Vahid. If, however, one be added to the number Vahid, it becometh Twenty; and if to the Vahid itself, it becometh Two. This is the secret of the wisdom thereof, should anyone wish to apprehend it.
