Although when true worship is offered, the worshipper is delivered from the fire, and entereth the paradise of God’s good-pleasure, yet such should not be the motive of his act. However, God’s favour and grace ever flow in accordance with the exigencies of His inscrutable wisdom.

The most acceptable prayer is the one offered with the utmost spirituality and radiance; its prolongation hath not been and is not beloved by God. The more detached and the purer the prayer, the more acceptable is it in the presence of God.

All but this one (Vahid) prayer have been abrogated; while that which hath been commanded in this Revelation is the remembrance of God, which if it take place in a spirit of joy and radiance is the best of devotions, and the noblest of degrees. Should a person, for the sake of all that is on earth, be shut out as by a veil from performing a single rak’ah of prayer, he would, in the sight of God, have been defrauded; whereas the virtue thereof is comparatively greater still; while that which it hath within it is comparatively loftier still. All the rak’ahs of the Living (Hayy) circle around the Point of Unity, Who is the beginning of the meridian cycle and the prayer thereof. And know thou that when thou standest to perform thy prayer, thou art before a Person within Whose grasp are held thy beginning and thy return. Naught is hidden from His knowledge; nor can aught frustrate His purpose. He hath power over all things; and is apprised of All Things ere they come into being: even as He is apprised of All Things after they come into being.

Further explanation hath been provided in the repositories of God’s Command. Let all in such wise as they have been worshipping God continue so to do. They shall behold the repositories of God’s Command, and delight in the delightfulness thereof.

Pray ye then by the leave of your Lord; then hold Him in befitting reverence: nor worship ye another than God, and believe ye the while with certainty in His Verses.

The Eighth Unity

Gate One of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that the likeness of the action of Him Whom God shall make manifest in comparison with those of others is as the sun in relation to the stars.

The substance of this gate is this: know thou that the likeness of the action of Him Whom God shall make manifest is that of the sun; while the likeness of the actions of the whole of existence – provided that they be in accordance with the good pleasure of God – is that of the stars and the moon – as in the case of the First One Who, by turning unto the Sun of Truth, partook of His effulgence.

The fruit thereof is that if, on the Day of the appearance of the Sun of Truth, the whole of existence should bear witness to some matter according to His good pleasure, His testimony amongst all these others would be like unto the sun, in comparison with which these others cannot be mentioned. To say this is extremely easy: whereas to act thereupon at the beginning of each new Revelation is to the utmost degree perplexing. For were anyone, when first the Qur’an was sent down, to have viewed matters in this light, then even had all the Letters of the Evangel spoken true, this would not in his eyes have made their word equal to that of the Apostle of God: inasmuch as the word of the Apostle is like unto the sun; while these others are deserving of notice only at Night, not during the Day.

In like manner, were anyone to have looked upon the Point of the Bayan in this light at the time of His appearance, he would have beheld His word to be like unto the sun, and the word of all else besides Him – although true – to be like unto the light of the stars at night. And similarly, in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, should all the people of the Bayan, at the time of His appearance, act upon His word, and perceive their own existence and actions to be like unto the stars in relation to the sun, then shall they have garnered the fruit of their existence: otherwise shall they not deserve to be considered even as stars – save only the believers in Him, who during the Day are completely obliterated, and during the Night only are possessed of light.

Such is the fruit of this law, should any wish to garner it on the Day of Resurrection: and all knowledge and action consist in this, should anyone be graciously enabled to show them forth. For were all in times past to have viewed matters in this light, never, at the beginning of any Revelation, would the One made manifest therein have passed a sentence of other than life eternal upon the people. Thus it is that at Night all behold themselves, conceiving themselves at their own level to be possessed of light: shut out the while as by a veil from perceiving that at the break of Day their former light is fled: nay rather, it fadeth into nothingness before the splendour of the Sun.

Conceive thou the likeness of the light of all to be their knowledge, and their words; and the likeness of the splendour of the action of Him Whom God shall make manifest to be His words, which fold up the whole of existence, and raise it up anew beneath the shadow of a single Relative “Ya’,” proclaiming, in the voice of their Revealer – Who is the Lord, exalted and glorified be He – “Verily, I am God, no God is there but Me; verily, all else besides Me are My creation: say: O My creation, Me alone do ye fear!” His actions too speak in the same wise, shouldst thou have ears to hear.

The essence of knowledge consisteth in recognizing the Source of Command, even up to His return. Consider thou the stars of the Evangel: notwithstanding that, after the ascension of the Sun of Truth, they had, in their own Revelation, acquired a borrowed light, yet, after the dawning of that selfsame Sun their former light was fled. Perceive thou such to be the case likewise on the advent of every Revelation: although their followers persist unto this very day under the apprehension of being possessed of light, and act accordingly, yet in thy view – who becamest a believer in Islam – thou knowest that they have no light, and have remained shut out as by a veil from the splendour of the Sun of Truth, Who is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. Conceive thou the beginning of each new Revelation to be in just this fashion, so that, when the opportunity of meeting with thy Best-Beloved ariseth, thou mayest not remain shut out as by a veil from reaping the fruit of thine existence.

Reflect ye then on that which is made manifest on the part of God: then, even as God hath taught you in the Book, reason ye in the selfsame fashion.

Gate Two of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that it is incumbent upon each soul to bequeath unto his heir nineteen leaves of fine paper, and nineteen rings upon which he should inscribe one of the Names of God; and that none must inherit from the deceased save his father; his mother; his wife; his son; his brother; his sister; and whosoever hath taught him – this after he hath expended upon himself, from his own estate, a sum sufficient to insure that he be dispatched with honour.

The substance of this gate is that whereas the degrees of the confession of the Unity of God are completed in each seven letters, which are the Letters of Affirmation – for this reason hath it been ordained that none shall inherit from the deceased, in the Secret of Reality, save seven souls: even as, at the level of each Attribute, it is possible to call God by that Attribute at seven levels: as for example, Awhad (Unique), Vahhad (Unifying), Vahid (One), Vahid (Peerless), Mutavahhid (Becoming One), Muvahhid (Making One), and Muvahhad (Being made One). It is in virtue of this secret that the matter hath been destined in this fashion on the part of Him Who is the Source of Command.

There is no soul who purposeth some matter, and whatsoever is suitable to his purpose, but that, if he call upon God by the seven Names whereby, in any particular case, it is possible to call Him – each one to the number “Qaf” – the means whereby this matter may be accomplished shall be made manifest for him; and his intention – so only it had been for God and in God – shall be destined to be carried into effect.

The fruit thereof is this, that on the Day of Resurrection, when all the laws are destined on the part of God, should the Tree of Truth decree otherwise than this, let no one ask why or wherefore: even as, in the case of the limits of inheritance which are now apparent in the Qur’an – had He, at the beginning of the Revelation, enjoined other than these limits upon a soul, then such would have been the decree of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him. The difference is this, that in contrast to the day whereon He so decreed, today innumerable people are acting beneath their shadow: whereas on that day, since they are enjoined upon that soul alone, it becometh hard for him, unless he have regard for the Source of the command. Even as was the day whereon the limits of inheritance were sent down in the Qur’an – that Day also shall be identically the same as was the beginning of this law for that soul.

Howbeit on the Day of Resurrection, ere He testeth everyone, the Tree of Truth maketh not Himself known by the name of His First Manifestation. All must be at a level of certitude and perspicacity such that if one hundred thousand souls be gathered in order to perform the circumambulation about the House – having travelled from their native lands especially for that day whereon permission had been granted to perform it – and if, on that selfsame day, the Tree of Truth should appear, and command “Perform ye not the circumambulation” – then, were all, upon the instant, to act thereupon, they would have realized the circumambulation; otherwise, all their actions would be rendered vain: inasmuch as this circumambulation which now, having gathered for the purpose, they are performing, was in virtue of His former command: the warrant for which is His Book aforetime, and His Book hereafter, which none but God is capable of revealing.

If, at the moment of the issuance of the prohibition, there were a perspicacious person who had regard for the Source of the command, and made certain of His truth, then he it is who would have performed the circumambulation for God, devotedly unto Him; while all the rest would be accounted among the abject and foolish. This is that same Sirat which for one person becometh wider than the heaven and the earth; while for him who maketh not certain of the Truth, it becometh sharper than a sword and finer than a hair.

It is for this reason that at the beginning of each Revelation, the people of perspicacity therein are rarer than the philosopher’s stone: for most act upon the basis of following one another, and the appearance of glory in the laws of God. Although all is actually at the bidding of the True One, and for Him, yet, because it is not performed on the basis of discerning insight, they remain, upon the appearance of the Author of the command, shut out as by a veil from abiding by His new command: notwithstanding that the previous ordinances of each Manifestation were to the end that God’s servants should be obedient unto the True One: whence haply, should the Revelation befall, they might, in virtue of that obedience, render obedience unto Him. Howbeit, when the Revelation befalleth, the obedient servant continueth, in his own conceit, to manifest obedience: even though, at such a time, his “obedience” is naught but disobedience.

Even as was the case with the believers in the Evangel: ere the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – all were obedient unto God, in their own religion, and to be praised in their works, provided that they acted according to the law of Jesus, as it truly was: whereas at the time of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – the very root of their religion, which was the formulae of the Twin Confessions, appeared in a novel guise: so that instead of their own confession of the Unity of God, “There is no God but God;” and instead of “Jesus – peace be upon Him – is the Spirit of God,” “Muhammad is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him” were revealed: while as touching the station of His Viceregents, “’Ali and the Imams are the Proofs of God” was revealed; and as touching the Pillars of His House, a reference instead unto the Gates of Guidance.

Considering, therefore, that the very roots of His religion can be made new in such a fashion, how must stand the case with the appearance of the subsidiary aspects of the laws of His religion?

This is the secret of the statement of the late Shaykh – peace be upon him – when someone inquired of him about that Word which His Holiness would utter, and three hundred and thirteen people – who on that Day were accounted the righteous of that Revelation – would be unable to support it – people in whose regard his Holiness Sadiq – peace be upon him – had made mention of “Kaf.” After many protestations to the effect “Thou shalt never be able to support it,” he addressed him: “Should His Holiness appear, and say ‘Renounce thine allegiance unto the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him,’ wouldst thou do so?” The questioner straightway emphatically rejected the course proposed, exclaiming “God forbid!” and “Perish the thought!” Notwithstanding, it is evident in the eyes of the followers of the Truth that those present on this occasion heard that very Word uttered by the tongue of his Holiness, through him: and that he, since he had not supported it, had become a disbeliever, yet adverted not thereto.

This came about because he looked not to the Source of Command, and regarded the Revelation of His Holiness to be other than that of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him: for had he beheld the Revelation of His Holiness to be in the same case as that of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – in relation to the Revelation of Jesus – peace be upon Him – he would then have supported that Word which is wider than the heaven of things accepted and the earth of receptivities; howbeit, since he viewed not the matter in such a light, it became finer for him that a hair, and thereto sharper than a sword.

It is not that the intention of the speaker was that he should actually renounce his allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – for this would be an impossible matter: and the light of his Holiness hath everlastingly shone – as it shall continue everlastingly to shine – in his manifestations. Nay rather, his intention was,

“In that Revelation he went by the name ‘Commander of the Faithful:’ in this Revelation allow not that name to shut thee out from recognizing him as by a veil.”

– even as the Commander of the Faithful – peace be upon him – at the time of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – was the same identical Viceregent of Jesus – peace be upon Him – at his own time, after His ascension. Shouldst thou, on the advent of each new Revelation, look to the Source of Command, then shall the Sirat become broader than every broadest thing that is possible in the world of being; while shouldst thou be shut out as by a veil from recognizing Him, then shall it become finer than every finest hair that thy knowledge could conceivably encompass.

Should the perspicacity of all the believers in the Bayan reach a level such that if all be gathered in some place – as mentioned in connection with the circumambulation –while that Tree of Truth be but a single soul amidst this host; and should he bid someone recite unto them His Verses – then if they at once pronounced them true, they would be judged believers; otherwise their erstwhile state of belief would be lifted from them: how, then, if they went on to perform the circumambulation, would stand the case with this observance, which is but one among numerous subsidiary aspects of their faith?

Know thou that whatsoever all possess is from the bounty of the Tree of Truth, not other than He. For example, had He said “Such-and-such manifestations shall not inherit,” would it have been open to anyone to ask why or wherefore? Thus it is that all deriveth from Him, even while all are shut out as by a veil from Him. He it is Who, from the beginning of their existence until the furthest limit of their remembrance, bestoweth upon them whatsoever they possess: whence haply, on the Day of His Revelation, they may attain the fruit of their existence, which is to believe in Him. Yet still they will not be abashed: and in each successive Revelation the veiled are shut out as by a veil.

Howbeit, in the Qur’an, mention hath been made of the fruit of the creation of All Things, in the noble Verse:

“It is God Who raised the heavens without pillars that ye can see, then mounted the Throne; and subjected the sun and the moon, both running unto an appointed term. He ordereth the Cause, He elaborateth the Verses, that perchance ye may be firmly persuaded of the meeting with your Lord.”

Had anyone, in the present Revelation, made certain that this Manifestation is the selfsame Manifestation of the Point of the Furqan, haply he would have attained the meeting with the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – which is none other but the meeting with God. Yet the cause of certitude in both cases is the same: nay, in this Revelation it is the more compelling: for although, in that Revelation, the Qur’an was revealed over a period of twenty-three years, in the present Revelation it is evident that not even so much as a week passeth ere the equivalent thereof hath been revealed.

Yet thou beholdest the fruit of the creation of All Things: which is that all, though acting in accordance with the laws of the Qur’an, are yet shut out as by a veil from attaining the fruit of their existence. If, on the Day of Revelation, in virtue of a single Verse of the Bayan, all the believers in the Qur’an had known with certainty that this is the same identical Reality upon Whom, at the beginning of Islam, was sent down the Qur’an, haply they would have realized the intention of God in this Verse; whereas it is evident that all recite it insensately, oblivious of the Divine intention: notwithstanding that the Manifestation of Truth is quit of the mere sight of whosever recognizeth Him not, nor knoweth certainly that the meeting with Himself is the very meeting with God.

If all the believers in the Bayan, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, make certain that He is the Point of the Bayan, haply they may attain the honour of having realized the intention of God in the Bayan. Since on that Day all are certain of the truth of the Point of the Bayan – for this reason is He cited by way of an example: for otherwise – exalted be His station above any such comparison! It beseemeth not the Temple of the Revelation of the world to come to make Himself known as the Temple of this nether world: for although He that is manifest in both is One, yet, since the conditions of the world to come are too great and glorious to brook any such comparison, even for this reason He maketh reference to the former.

Howbeit, since all are certain of the truth of His Former Manifestation, nor is their eye keen that they should perceive with certainty His Latter Manifestation, for this reason He mentioneth Himself by the Name of His own Former Manifestation, so that perchance – even should someone be in the most veiled condition – he would be able to recognize Him. Even as, on the Day of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – had all the believers in Jesus – peace be upon Him – made certain that it was He, they would assuredly have arrived at the intention of God in the Evangel. Notwithstanding, His is greater than that Revelation: yet for the sake of the certainty of the followers of the Former Revelation, He mentioneth the name of the Source of His Former Revelation, that perchance the followers of that Revelation may pass thereby over the Sirat, and attain the fruit of their existence.

Reflect ye then upon that which God hath created for you, and make all your actions to be for God, your Lord: perchance, on the Day of His Revelation, ye may believe in His Verses. That is none other but the Day of Him Whom God shall make manifest: should ye believe in Him, ye shall have believed in God, and that which God hath sent down in the Bayan; otherwise shall ye have remained shut out as by a veil from the meeting with God, and from that which God had sent down aforetime in the Bayan. Tarry not in this, for even as ye tarry, your abode shall be in the Fire: nor on that Day shall ye know this to be so, for were ye to know it, ye would not tarry: yet know it ye shall.

It is because ye consecrate not yourselves to God that ye make not certain of the Truth: consecrate, then, yourselves to God, your Lord, whence haply ye may be able to consecrate yourselves to Him Whom He shall, in truth, make manifest unto all worlds. Be ye watchful of the beginning of the Revelation, lest ye tarry to accept the Cause of God, whereupon ye would become in His sight a “new believer,” for such would be an abasement unto yourselves, had ye been aforetime firm believers in God and His Verses. Ye have not been created but for that; nor hath any command been enjoined upon you but for this. Be not, then, shut out as by a veil from attaining the meeting with God, neither aforetime nor hereafter; and believe ye the while with certainty in His Verses.

Gate Three of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that after the appearance, on the Day of Resurrection, of “All things are doomed to perish, except His Countenance,” it behoveth every soul to beseech forgiveness of the Divine Tree, by himself, not through the agency of another – unless there be good reason why it would be impossible for him to present himself in person – and to beseech forgiveness of Him, regardless of whether He should respond to him verbally or in writing; otherwise, let him beseech forgiveness of God by some other means, such as a written missive or the like.

The substance of this gate is that the Day of Resurrection shall inevitably come, and the Tree of Truth be made manifest. Although one cannot with an easy heart make mention, with respect to the believers in the Bayan, of that Word which was pronounced aforetime – namely, “All things are doomed to perish, except His Countenance” – (perchance all may be watchful lest on that Day – for that they are shut out as by a veil from their Best-Beloved – their Affirmation be converted into Negation: nay rather, if there be any possibility of Negation, this be converted into Affirmation) yet (because this distracted people have ever comported themselves in an insensate manner, not on the basis of discerning insight), assuming that He should be made manifest; set the Resurrection on foot; and send down such a Word, which for the people of the Bayan is more grievous than any fire (inasmuch as all had been performing their works to the end of obtaining salvation: yet, after the Lord hath pronounced the decree of Perdition, what salvation can there be?), it behoveth them, with the utmost urgency, to betake themselves, after learning of the revelation of this Verse, and its decree, into His presence; to beseech forgiveness from Him; and to return unto Him: in order that He may convert their perdition into salvation: for this is the fruit of the performance of all works: to the degree that if, after hearing of this decree, one should perform every goodly work, still he would be of those condemned to perish, unless he were to return, and – even by that same word whereby he had been doomed to perdition – to obtain rather his salvation.

Shouldst thou look beneath the shadow of this Word of Perdition, thou wouldst behold that the human realities, and all works, had been consumed by a perishing blow of God’s hand: so that should anyone on that day wish to act upon this Verse, he would not leave a single animate being upon the surface of the earth: for when once a being hath perished, what profit, in the sight of God, can there be in its existence? Yet the straitness of this matter in the sight of God, and of those endowed with understanding, is more grievous than the fruit thereof, which thou mayest beholdest with thine outward eye (albeit, since thou art in the world of limitation, thou canst not understand): that from the beginning of thy life until the end thereof thou shouldst perform thy works for the purpose of securing thy salvation; then of a sudden fall beneath the shadow of Perdition.

Nor can the matter be righted save from the Source of Command: for wert thou, after the revelation of this Verse, to live as long as the world shall endure, beseeching all the while forgiveness of God, it would avail thee not; unless thou shouldst return, and obtain a Word from the Source: which, though it were but the single Word “We have saved thee,” would save thee; whereas all thine entreaties for forgiveness would save thee not.

It is incumbent upon thee, after hearing of this decree, to detach thyself from all works (inasmuch as ye performed them all for the sake of securing thy salvation: whereas after the reverse thereof hath been decreed of God, what profit can they yield?); to return unto Him; and to obtain a Word importing thy salvation, although it be by means merely of a gesture. Wert thou to give all that is on earth for the sake of obtaining such a Word, it would assuredly avail thee better than to expend it in the way of God: for wert thou to expend it in the way of God, it would not save thee; while shouldst thou obtain such a Word, it shall suffice to save thee until the following Day of Resurrection.

Should it lie within thy power, do thou, with the utmost speed of which thou art capable, request, and obtain, such a Word: for wert thou, from the time of hearing of this decree, to tarry for so much as the twinkling of an eye, and at that very instant to be caused to expire, then thou shalt be amongst those condemned to perish; whereas wert thou rather to make haste, and to set on foot the means of obtaining such a Word, then, even shouldst thou be caused to expire, perchance a Word may emanate from the Source whereby, after death, thou mayest dwell in Paradise, and thy fire be converted into light: which of any action on thy part is that, by recourse to which, all thy deeds shall the most readily be accepted, and thy misdeeds converted into righteous acts. Although a whiff of the “new believer” wafteth therefrom, yet still, it would be better for thee to become a “new believer,” than to depart this world among those condemned to perish.

Naught hath been enjoined upon the people of the Bayan to the same degree as this: for their salvation resideth in this, not in the works which they perform. Nor allow thou the limitations of bounds and places to shut thee out as by a veil from the Source. How like it is, for example, that thou shouldst be the most knowledgeable of the people of the Bayan; and be seated in thy home; and the Possessor of Command should be made manifest; yet thou, through prepossession with thine own self, shouldst fail to advert thereto, until His situation should have been changed: as in the case, for example, that He should be lying captive in Mah-Ku, which, to outward appearance, is a place of abasement – none of which conditions make any difference to the Cause of God.

Conceive thou His situation in this land to be as that of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – in the Mountain of Mecca: when, in such a spot, He sent down this Verse in the Qur’an, all the people of that age entered the fold of those condemned to perish; and, in the sight of God; of His Apostle; of those endowed with understanding; and of everyone who recited the Qur’an, were subject to the sentence of Perdition, and judged to be other than believers; notwithstanding that to this very day, in their own conceit, they continue to act according to their religion.

In fine, the intention is this: let the people of the Bayan also, after the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, practice their religion with the utmost piety: yet, after the revelation of this Verse, how can their works avail them? The servant laboureth in the path of God – nay, gladly offereth up his life for His sake – that haply he may attain salvation: yet when once, from the Source of Command, the decree of Perdition is sent forth, what further profit can accrue? At most, should he pursue his works, then in the eyes of himself, and of those endowed with knowledge, he would be in the same case as those servants who, after the revelation of the Bayan, continued to act according to the precepts of its own previous manifestation; while ere this, he shall be like unto those servants who today still abide by the precepts of the Evangel – whereas the Qur’an hath since been sent down, and order hath been given for this latter to be lifted up.

Act ye, at least to some degree, on the basis of discerning insight: haply, on the Day of Resurrection, ye may not perish; or, should ye perish, may obtain again salvation: for, as long as the Tree of Truth be risen, all possible affairs are possible; whereas when once He be set, alteration and change are impossible, until such time as He shall rise again. For example, if, in the Revelation of the Furqan – after the revelation of this Verse – anyone had besought the Apostle of God to save him after he had perished, undoubtedly that Source of bounty would, by the leave of God, have sent down “We have, as a bounty on Our part, saved thee after We had caused thee to perish: We, truly, are the source of grace abounding:” and by this means the recipient of this bounty would until this Day have remained within the fold of salvation – “until this Day,” which, in the eyes of the Lord; His Apostle; the Imams of Guidance; the Gates; and all the believers; nay, in the eyes of the angels of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them – nay, in the eyes of all things – is the beginning of the Revelation of the Bayan. Now, however, that such hath not come to pass, naught hath been taken away from the bounty of the Source: nay, the soul in question hath alone remained deprived.

Conceive thou such to be the case likewise in the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: be thou watchful of the minutes and hours of the Day of Resurrection: and keep thou account, from the time of Revelation until the setting of the Sun, with the utmost scrupulousness wherewith thou keepest account of thy substance in another’s hands: for the fruit thereof is this, that thou shouldst expend it in the path of God, and attain salvation: yet shouldst thou be shut out as by a veil from an account which, if neglected, shall cause all to become as naught, then to what avail thy spiritual accounts with thine own self, and thy worldly accounts with God’s creatures?

I swear by the Sacred Eternal Essence! Assuredly, there is no human spirit in God’s creatures: else on hearing this Word they would have turned to water, and never would the mere thought that they could live thereafter enter into their heart: for it may chance that one hath laboured from the beginning of his life in order to obtain salvation: then finally, from the Source of salvation, such a decree is sent down, whose Divine origin is certain beyond a doubt, inasmuch as it conveyeth the incapacity of all.

Know thou that the number of “His Countenance” (“Vajhu-Hu”) is the number of the Name “Vahid.” Whoso, in the Qur’an, believed in Muhammad, the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – and His Letters of the Living, was of other than those condemned to perish, in the Qur’an, up to the Revelation of the Bayan. Thereafter, whoso hath come under the shadow of the Letters of the Vahid of the Bayan is of other than those condemned to perish, up to the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest. Regard thou such to be the case likewise in each successive Revelation, world without end, even unto the end that hath no end.

There is no doubt that those servants who were truly beneath the shadow of the Letters of the “Countenance” of the Qur’an, were, on the Day of Resurrection, saved through the blessing of their love for them – which is none other but their love for the Letters of the Vahid in the Bayan. In like manner, should anyone, in the Bayan, fall truly beneath the shadow of its Letters of “His Countenance,” he shall be saved on the Day of Resurrection: inasmuch as he shall not, in that Revelation, deviate from the One made manifest therein, and His Letters of the Living: which if he did, it is an indication of his other than steadfastness in the Letters of “His Countenance” of the Bayan. This same secret hath been current from the time of the Wondrous Creation until today: and shall remain current from today, world without end, even unto the end that hath no end.

Be ye watchful of each Revelation: for the Revelation of God is not like unto the revelation of the people: and the proof of God is a proof such as all that are on earth are powerless to produce its like: until such time as the Dispensation shall progress, and men shall be able to behold the Revelation in the essence of Reality: at which time the splendour of that Sun of Truth shall by itself guide unto His revelation. Then shall be realized the import of “Know ye God through God:” inasmuch as in all Revelations up till now, it hath been a question rather of “Know ye God through His proof.” It is not that when “Know ye God through God” cometh into force, there would no longer be a proof, and that thou wouldst never more be shut out as by a veil from the Source: nay rather, the Dispensation shall so progress that those in the Concourse on high who extol the glory of God shall recognize their Best-Beloved in each Revelation through Himself: nay more, they shall recognize the proof through Him, not Him through the proof.

Know thou that the recognition of God in the station “Know ye God through God” is not valid unless conjoined with “Know ye the Letters of the Vahid, at their respective levels, through that which appeareth from the First Vahid:” inasmuch as all hath derived from naught else but the proliferation of that First Vahid: will ye not then fear God? By this “proliferation” is intended the revelation thereof, through the First Vahid, at the level of the proliferation, by the proliferation itself. It is not that the First Letter actually becometh the Letters of the Living; or that the Letters of the Living actually become the proliferating numbers. Nay, it is rather that through the guidance of the First Vahid, all are guided: so that wert thou to look upon the last person in existence, thou wouldst see in him naught but the revelation of the First Person in existence, by himself, at his own level: even as it is evident that the lowliest of people today are adjudged believers in the religion of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – Who is the most exalted of mankind. This is the intention of the proliferation of all the numbers from the First Vahid. Put then your whole trust and confidence in God on the Day of Resurrection, that haply ye may prosper.

By this “putting one’s whole trust and confidence in God” is not intended that thou shouldst recite this Verse, or, whilst kneeling upon thy prayer-mat, tearfully entreat, “O God, I have placed my whole trust and confidence in Thee: do Thou save me on the Day of Resurrection!” Nay rather, the means whereby, on that Day, thou mayest place thy whole trust and confidence in God is this, that when the Tree of Truth appeareth, thou shouldst believe in Him, and make certain of the truth of His Verses: at which time thou shalt truly have placed thy whole trust and confidence in God, and thy tearful entreaties to Him shall have borne fruit. For otherwise, no Prophet hath been sent forth Who hath not enjoined upon His people to place their whole trust and confidence in the Lord.

Nor is there any doubt that the Lord is faithful to His promise: and should anyone place his whole trust and confidence in Him, He would deliver him from aught whereat he might be sorrowed. Yet what hath befallen, that these diverse peoples upon the surface of the earth have all persisted in other than the truth, notwithstanding that in every case they regard themselves as placing their whole trust and confidence in God, in such manner as is current amongst them, each person in his own proper tongue!

Come a little to thy senses, and consider that the matter of putting one’s whole trust and confidence in God is either laid down in the Book of God; or was at the bidding of the Apostle; or at the bidding of the Letters of the Living; or at the bidding of the followers of the Letters of the Vahid: yet observe thou that all reverteth unto the person of the One made manifest in the Revelation: even as today, the source of whatsoever instances of truth there be in Islam is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – notwithstanding that for each several aspect of the Revelation there are innumerable subordinate aspects; and that for the explanation of each instance of putting one’s whole trust and confidence in God there are thousands upon thousands of explanations that could be offered. Do ye therefore put your whole trust and confidence in God: then believe with certainty in God and His Verses.

Gate Four of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that of All Things the highest is for the Point; the medial for the Letters of the Living; and the lowest for the people.

The substance of this gate is that should all be schooled in the Divine nature of the Verses, and the supremacy of the proof which they constitute in the sight of God and of those endued with understanding, perchance, on the Day of Revelation, they shall allow no interval to elapse between hearkening thereto and believing in the Truth. This is the essence of all knowledge: for without this, even should one possess all knowledge, it shall become as naught, and one shall be adjudged other than a believer; whereas if he know naught save this, he hath acquired the essence of all knowledge, and shall attain salvation: for indeed the like circumstance is observable in every Revelation: how the exalted among the people are abased, and the abased among the people are exalted; or else the exalted become yet more exalted, and the abased yet more abased.

Were anyone, on the Day of Resurrection, able to estimate the ranks of the believers in terms of their precedence of belief, assuredly, so long as that Revelation continued, it would be possible for him to determine, with respect to any believer, in which sequence of the Vahid he fell. For example, should a soul, following three hundred and sixty others, believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest, he would be the last of the Vahid from the number Vahid. In such wise, this chain of precedence is the rule, from whence thou mayest discern the limit of all the numbers. Whatsoever is peerless in its kind is for the First Vahid: and so likewise in descending order, step by step, until the succession embraceth all the numbers.

Such is the entitlement of each being, at the moment of its coming into being: whence if, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, He had in His possession three hundred and sixty-one diamonds – each of them being ninety-five mithqals of gold greater in value (Baha’) than the last; and if, on a single day, three hundred and sixty-one people believed in Him – the interval between each of them being but the space of a single utterance of “Yea” – then, should He wish to bestow these numbers upon those numbers, He would, agreeably with this principle, bestow them according to the ranks of these latter numbers.

Behold thou likewise the Mystery of God as current, and the Decree of God as manifest, in every matter: haply, on the Day of Resurrection thou shalt obtain precedence in owning the confession of the truth of the True One: in the Primordial Gathering of “Am I not your Lord” through answering “Yea;” and in each and every Primordial Gathering through manifesting the appropriate response. Mark thou that each thing hath its own such Gathering: whence for example, should He pick up an atom of clay, and say “This clay is the substance of the Wondrous First Creation” – or designate it by any term whatsoever: even should He denote it by its own constituent clay, nor mention aught beyond this; and shouldst thou not respond to Him in the Primordial Gathering of the clay, which is at the level of the mineral, and the furthest limit of existence, then shalt thou not have responded unto God. Even shouldst thou, at the level of thine own inner essence, upon hearkening unto the call “Am I not your Lord,” have answered “Yea,” yet in this arena shalt thou have been found wanting, at the level of thine own existence.

What difference doth it make whether the command be given to bow down before Adam, or to bow down before an atom of clay? The purpose is simply to obey His command, not to do reverence to this or that. Wherefore, in such a case, if thou art shut out as by a veil from responding to His bidding in the Primordial Gathering of the clay, thou hast remained shut out as by a veil from recognizing the very Secret of Existence: and even shouldst thou perform all good, thou shalt still have arrived beneath the shadow of the saying of the first who “bowed not down” before Adam; and even shouldst thou say, “I shall render all obedience;” and have done so, and be doing so, or shalt yet do so – the doom of God shall still be sent down in thy respect: even as there was sent down aforetime in this regard a statement to the effect: “As I wish, not as thou wishest.”

Although it is inconceivable that the Tree of Truth would issue a command such that men’s minds would be unable to apprehend it; or promulgate an ordinance whose plausibility all were unable to grasp with certainty: yet the above example was to the end that the servant should recognize the repositories of God’s Command, and realize that in virtue of the same Command whereby hath been enjoined “Believe ye in God and His Verses” – by this selfsame authority “Cause ye not sorrow unto any soul” hath likewise been enjoined. Even though the one concerned be lying at the furthest limit of existence, why, if thou hast regard for the authority to command, art thou shut out as by a veil from observing one command, and steadfast in thine obedience to another?

Thus it is that the observance of all the Divine ordinances hath ever been, and ever shall be, among the prerequisites of piety: but only on condition that thou be not shut out as by a veil from recognizing the Source of Command, in each successive Revelation; else is there no doubt that in whichsoever Revelation thou abidest, thou shalt observe its precepts, if thou art sincerely devoted to thy religion. Otherwise, thou thyself art witness unto thine own impiety: and “sufficient art thou today as a recorder against thyself.”

The fruit thereof is this, that haply on the Day of Resurrection no one may remain shut out as by a veil from obeying the ordinances of Him Whom God shall make manifest: for were He to lay His commandment upon the whole of existence, His command hath ever been, and ever shall be, the command of God: whence whosoever shall ask why or wherefore shall have done so with respect to the command of God, irrespective of whether His command be such as to affect All Things, or whether such as to affect only the ninth of the ninth of the tenth of the tenth of a dinar, the value (Baha’) of a thousand whereof shall be that of one mithqal of silver in that Revelation.

Do ye therefore recognize the limits of your own selves; then, on the Day of Resurrection, destine ye in such wise as God Himself hath destined.

Gate Five of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that it hath been enjoined upon whoso hath sufficient means, to acquire three diamonds, the number of the “Bism”(“In the Name of”); four topazes, the number of “Allah” (“God”); six emeralds, the number of “Al-Amna’” (“the Most Exalted”); and six rubies, the number of “Al-Aqdas” (“the Most Holy”) – to acquire them and deliver them unto Him Whom God shall make manifest, and the Letters of the Living, on the Day of their appearance.

The substance of this gate is that (as hath been mentioned in other places) the whole of existence is in the Bayan; the whole of the Bayan is in the First Vahid; and the First Vahid is in the First Point: and whereas all, on the Day of Resurrection, shall be gathered together according to the degrees of the Vahid – the whole of which Vahid becometh a “Vahid” only in virtue of the decree of the First Vahid; while in all a single life-bestowing water is observable, which is none other but the Cause of God: and whereas each several thing, in its own arena – until it resembleth this Vahid – becometh not perfect at its own level, neither guideth unto God – for this reason hath it been commanded that on the Day of Revelation, up to the following Revelation, each person who hath sufficient means to acquire three diamonds, four topazes, six emeralds, and six rubies, should in this manner create about him a resemblance unto the First Vahid.

He should, if he be able, bring them beneath the shadow of the property of the First Vahid; otherwise, on the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, these offerings may, subject to His command, be bestowed upon His Letters of the Living – this as a bestowal on the part of God unto the First Vahid in that Revelation. The value (Baha’) of all must be equivalent to the value (Baha’) of the First Vahid, whence those who consider matters in the light of reason may not be shut out as by a veil from apprehending the Secret of Unity. Should all, in that Revelation, be honoured to render Him this obedience, the Lord of the whole of existence shall bestow their offerings upon the proliferation of the Vahid. Should anyone possess such gems, yet, when the Tree of Truth shineth forth, tarry to the least degree that can be mentioned in rendering unto Him this due, then to that same degree his tardiness shall become unto him a fire.

It is befitting that those who arrive by reasoning at a knowledge of the Unity of God in respect of Essence, Attributes, Actions and Worship; of Creation, Sustenance, Death and Life; of Glory, Thanks, Unity and Grandeur; of Fire, Air, Water and Earth; of Heart, Spirit, Soul and Body; and of White Light, Yellow Light, Green Light and Red Light, should behold them all beneath the shadow of the letters of “Bismi’llahi’l-Amna’i’l-Aqdas” (“In the Name of God, the Most Exalted, the Most Holy”).

Four prayers have been mentioned for the Four Lights, which are the greatest of all prayers: whosoever is graciously favoured to read them shall attain the good of this world and of the next. God bestoweth His grace upon whomsoever He willeth among His servants, and shall bestow upon whomsoever He willeth whatsoever of His property He hath destined on His part: He, verily, is the All-Bountiful, the All-Encompassing.

Gate Six of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that permission hath been granted for refinement: that is, to cleanse oneself once every four days, through recourse to a bath-house; for the removal of hair from the whole body with nurih every eight or fourteen days; for the paring of the nails; for the use of henna over the whole body; for men to write upon their breasts “Al-Rahman” (“All-Merciful”), and women upon theirs “Allahumma” (“O my God!”); and for one to look into a mirror each day and night.

The substance of this gate is that permission hath been granted in the Bayan for refinement and cleanliness to the highest degree attainable in the world of being. If, once every four days, the nails, hair and adornments of a man be trimmed, this hath been, and is, beloved in the sight of God. The more promptly garments be purified and cleansed, the closer hath this been, and is it, to refinement.

Permission hath been granted for the use of henna, whether over the whole body, or over only part of it. If, upon the breast, which is the place of the love of God, the word “Allahumma” in the case of the possessors of circles, and the word “Ar-Rahman” in the case of the possessors of temples, be by some means imprinted in the finest script – this is beloved, and permission hath been granted for this to be done: as it hath likewise for the representation in this manner of more than these two words.

Should one be accustomed to the use of nurih, this hath been prescribed at an interval denoted by the letter “Ha’;” and if it hath not been one’s practice to apply it to the arms and legs, it is not desirable for one to do so: notwithstanding, permission hath been granted for its use over the entire body, for no single hair is removed but that the body is relieved of seventy different kinds of ailments, through the leave of God.

It is befitting that the servant should look into a mirror; behold his physical creation; and render thanks unto his Best-Beloved for the excellency of his comeliness; or else beseech forgiveness of his Best-Beloved: inasmuch as all beings, in their pristine state, were created in the utmost excellence of beauty: and should one interpose not a barrier to its appearance, he will conform to the pristine image of the creation of his own being. As for the prevailing notion that at night it hath been forbidden to look into a mirror, this hath not derived its origin from any mention in the Book of God.

At all events, the servant must evince ever such conditions that if at that very moment the Tree of Truth were to appear, and he were to happen into the presence of God, he would behold in his own person no cause of abhorrence in aught, in respect of aught: inasmuch as this matter of refinement hath not been enjoined but for the sake of the Day of the Revelation of God: to the end that, should one happen into the presence of God, there would be about him naught but the conditions refinement, lest the Lord should witness upon him aught unbeloved. In the Bayan aught that might interpose a barrier to refinement hath been forbidden: to the degree even that, should one happen to observe upon his body, or upon his garb, an atom of defilement – no more than would suffice to cause him, within himself, a feeling of abhorrence – it is not beloved that he should land in the presence of God in such a state: perchance, all in the Bayan having become trained in this demeanour, haply, on the Day of the appearance of the Manifestation of Truth, He may behold no object of abhorrence in those who believe in Him.

Stage by stage, and little by little, the Dispensation shall progress, until, if someone be wearing a robe, and perspire, he would exchange it for another: how indeed could he bear to continue wearing it? Since, however, the followers of this Revelation are as yet unable to proceed at such a level, if the cleaning of the garments take place at the same interval as the cleansing of the body, they shall become trained in refinement; notwithstanding, the briefer the interval, the more beloved is it in the sight of God. Should this procedure be impossible for anyone, let him not be sorrowed, for in virtue merely of his love of such refinement, he shall be granted the recompense thereof.

Howbeit, it hath ever been, and is, incumbent upon each soul to be watchful that he evince in himself whatsoever refinement lieth potentially within his power: inasmuch as the Tree of Truth, during His concealment, is witness of His creatures, and knoweth and seeth them all: yet none knoweth Him, nor seeth Him with His own eye, inasmuch as that eye is created in All Things only after His Revelation. How like it is that even in His own home, neither His father should know Him, nor His mother: neither His consort, nor any among God’s creatures. Regard thou the likeness of this state of affairs to be as that of the revelation of the Apostle of God ere He received His Prophetic Call; or as that of the revelation of the Point of the Bayan ere He declared His Mission.

His knowledge, however, encompasseth alike His own Self and the creatures of the Lord, who are travelling beneath His shadow. from the moment of the appearance of the Spirit within Him, He hath knowledge of His own Self, even up to the final phase of His Revelation, when the Spirit attacheth unto another throne: and He seeth all, observing how all, in His Name, do whatever they do, from the beginning of existence unto the end thereof; and how all subsist – and are in consequence entitled to the designation “thing” – only in virtue of His substance, in respect whereof He is supremely entitled to this designation. Yet no one cometh to know Him, unless, through His Verses, He maketh Himself known unto him: neither shall He make Himself known but at the time of His Revelation, when all shall be judged by their ability to recognize Him, and the Verses of glory shall shine forth from the dawning-place of His sanctity.

Blessed is he who attaineth the meeting with God on the Day of His appearance, and who cometh into His presence in a state such that He shall not witness upon his outward person aught but what he loveth; He, verily, is the Exemplar of refinement and the Essence of refinement. Say: God is refined above every possessor of refinement. None shall be able to resist the revelation of His refinement, neither in the heavens, nor in the earth, nor in whatsoever is between them. He, verily, is the Exemplar of refinement; the Embodiment of refinement; and the Essence of refinement.

Gate Seven of the Eighth Unity: Concerning printing, and the enjoining of recourse thereto

The substance of this gate is that permission hath been granted for the printing of the Bayan, and of whatsoever is composed beneath its shadow, in accordance therewith: up to the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, at which time, if all have acquired sufficient capacity to be able to preserve the Words of God in the finest script, then doubtless He will give order in this wise; otherwise He shall grant permission for whatsoever is the requirement of His bounty and grace.

After this permission hath been granted, no further excuse can remain for anyone, in the sight of God, not to possess a copy of the Bayan, wherewith to be reminded of Him Whom God shall make manifest – in the finest script: not as is the custom of this present age, when any available manuscript is set in print. (Nay, it hath reached the pass that the value [Baha’] of a gift copy of the Qur’an is but twenty-eight nakhuds of silver. ) Were it not out of consideration for the incapacity of all the believers, assuredly permission would not have been granted for recourse to print: yet since all are now abiding in the grace and bounty of the True One, this measure is permitted. Notwithstanding, whoso is able to write the Bayan in the finest script, it shall be better for him than to acquire a fine printed copy thereof. This is a token of the grace of God: He favoureth therewith whomsoever He willeth among His servants; and the grace of God is infinite.

Know thou that the veneration accorded the Qur’an is due not but to the veneration accorded the relation which, in its own right, it beareth unto God: and is for the sake also of the spirits that are in those words. All the spirits in the Qur’an revert unto the spirits of its Letters of the Living, even as their beginning likewise was from these Letters. (For today, if a believer is active in his faith, he is guided in his actions by the word of the members of the Holy Family, and of the Four Gates during the period of the Lesser Occultation – which period having come to an end, whatsoever had come down from them no one was able rightfully to alter or change.) All the Letters of the Living revert in turn unto the Point of the Furqan, Who is the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – while He reverteth unto God, by His own Self: which return is in virtue of His return unto His own Self, inasmuch as the contingent world is not able to surpass the limits of its own contingent state.

So likewise in the Bayan, all the exalted spirits thereof shall revert unto the First Gate, Who is He Whom God shall make manifest; while all the other-than-exalted spirits thereof shall revert unto the first manifestation of other than truth, who boweth not down before Him. Behold thou in this same wise all the Heavenly Books, perceiving that the veneration in which all are held is due to their relation unto God; and that they have ever been – as they are now – living, in virtue of their being lifted up from the preceding Revelations, and becoming connected with the succeeding Revelations.

There is no doubt that the Evangel was the Book of the Lord: howbeit, after the revelation of the Furqan it lifted up the true spirits thereof unto the Qur’an; those, however, whom it lifted not up were of other than the exalted spirits of the Evangel, inasmuch as they tarried in the former faith. Likewise in the Bayan, the spirits of all those believers in the Qur’an who enter within the fold of the Bayan are among the Exalted Letters; otherwise are they accounted the reverse. Likewise in the Bayan, all who believe in Him Whom God shall make manifest are the exalted spirits thereof. Yet if there be a soul who boweth not down, he is all the other-than-exalted letters.

Do ye then employ your craftsmanship in that whereby ye may be rightly guided, in the finest script whereof ye are capable.

Gate Eight of the Eighth Unity

concerning the permissibility of cutting the hair of the head for boys; and removing the facial hair so as to strengthen it; and praying in an ’aba, not in another garment such as a jubbih, for God loveth this not.

The substance of this gate is that permission hath been granted for the cutting of the hair of the head, and its removal from the face, for the purpose of strengthening it, so that it may present a handsome appearance. The trimming of the moustache hath under all conditions been commanded. They among God’s servants who are truly shut out as by a veil are those who are shut out as by a veil from the Divine command.

Permission hath been granted one to perform his daily prayers wearing an ’aba, in such wise that naught appear of his hands but the fingertips, which attire hath been, and is, more consonant with dignity. To perform the daily prayers in a jubbih, however, hath not been, and is not, beloved, except on an occasion of necessity, when permission to do so hath been granted. All these various matters are to the end that haply, on the Day of Resurrection, no one, whether outwardly or inwardly, may have about him aught but what God loveth: so that those who view matters in the light of reason may reason that if, for the accidental body, the Lord would not wish aught but what He loveth, how then must the stand the case with the essential bodies, the souls, the spirits, and the hearts, which are the dawning-places of the revelation of the First Vahid? Fear God, then, O ye the God-fearing, on the Day of Resurrection, whence haply ye may prosper.

Gate Nine of the Eighth Unity

Let everyone write down his name, and whatsoever he hath wrought of good and the reverse, from the beginning of the revelation of the Cause even unto the day of its setting; and let the viceregents preserve this up to the Day whereon the Tree shall be made manifest.

The substance of this gate is that from the beginning of one Revelation until the next, permission hath been granted for each person to write in his book, in his own hand, or in that of another, whatsoever he hath wrought in the Bayan; and likewise any instance of other than good he may have wrought ere entering within its fold: so that in the following Resurrection, those who, in the previous Revelation, were active in their faith may be rewarded for their works, if they be not shut out as by a veil from the Sun of Truth: for otherwise, it may chance that He be made manifest, and one be still performing his works as before: for example, it is now one thousand two hundred and seventy years since the Qur’an was sent down, and still the members of the earlier faith perform their works according to the Evangel.

Regard thou the Cause of God to be in this wise on the advent of each and every Revelation: nor remain shut out therefrom as by a veil: for the Day of Resurrection is a day on which the sun riseth and setteth like unto any other day. How oft hath the Day of Resurrection dawned, and the people of the land where it occurred did not learn of the event. Had they heard, they would not have believed, and thus they were not told!

When the Apostle of God [Muhammad] appeared, He did not announce unto the unbelievers that the Resurrection had come, for they could not bear the news. That Day is indeed an infinitely mighty Day, for in it the Divine Tree proclaimeth from eternity unto eternity, ‘Verily, I am God. No God is there but Me’. Yet those who are veiled believe that He is one like unto them, and they refuse even to call Him a believer, although such a title in the realm of His heavenly Kingdom is conferred everlastingly upon the most insignificant follower of His previous Dispensation. Thus, had the people in the days of the Apostle of God regarded Him at least as a believer of their time how would they have debarred Him, for seven years while He was in the mountain, from access to His Holy House [Ka’bah]?

Likewise in this Dispensation of the Point of the Bayan, if the people had not refused to concede the name believer unto Him, how could they have incarcerated Him on this mountain, without realizing that the quintessence of belief oweth its existence to a word from Him? Their hearts are deprived of the power of true insight, and thus they cannot see, while those endowed with the eyes of the spirit circle like moths round the Light of Truth until they are consumed. It is for this reason that the Day of Resurrection is said to be the greatest of all days, yet it is like unto any other day—save only that the Manifestation of God is on that day apparent.

The fruit of the law prescribed in this Chapter is that haply on that Day one’s eye may be open, so that he may behold his Best-Beloved; and be able on that Day to write down whatsoever he may accomplish: for until the following Resurrection he shall be judged on this. That which the Point of the Bayan must write is this:

“That which was before it, it lifted up unto itself, and the Lord sent it down unto me.”

This is that which He hath accomplished in the Resurrection. Let all too write down whatsoever they may accomplish, and deliver it unto Him Who is the very essence of existence: perchance their exploits may be remembered on the Day of Resurrection before God, should they be able, on that Day, to enter within the fire of the confession of His Unity: for otherwise, night and day they shall continue their tearful supplications; their Best-Beloved shall appear; and they shall fail to recognize Him: as in the case of those who await still the advent of the promised Ahmad – which the Christians all await, offering up pitiful entreaties that His advent may be hastened: whereas already one thousand two hundred and seventy years have elapsed since the time of His appearance.

Be thou perspicacious on that Day, with the eye of thine heart, lest thou be shut out as by a veil, and the Resurrection be set on foot, and thou be uninformed thereof: for it behoveth the Lord to give thee tidings thereof, if thou wilt but hear: which tidings shall be given unto thee by Him Whom God shall make manifest, if thou wilt but accept.

Do ye therefore put your whole trust and confidence in God, your All-Merciful Lord: then write down whatsoever ye may accomplish, whether of good or the reverse, even from one Resurrection unto the next.

Gate Ten of the Eighth Unity

concerning this, that it is permitted unto all who are reared in a particular clan to look upon and converse with one another, whether male or female; and permission is granted unto whosoever wisheth to converse with women, or in their case with men, to the degree that shall bear fruit between them: and should neither exceed the limit of twenty-eight words it shall be better for them.

The substance of this gate is that permission hath been granted unto all who are being reared in a particular clan to look upon and converse with one another, alike whether the physical temples of those concerned be in the image of a temple, or in that of a circle. In case of need, permission hath been granted for a man to speak with a woman to the degree sufficient to allow their conversation to bear fruit. If the limit of twenty-eight words be not exceeded, this would be nearer unto godliness; yet, if this much avail not, permission hath been granted for a greater number. By “clan” is intended the actual denotation of this term, not the acceptation of the word now apparent, as for example when the hundred thousand households constituting a whole tribe are spoken of as a single “clan.”

Perchance on the Day of Resurrection, through the latitude afforded by this law, no one shall be shut out as by a veil from obtaining his or her share of grace from the Source: and should the Tree of Love increase or decrease the number of words permitted, after He hath been made manifest, let no one ask why or wherefore. Fear ye then God as it is meet that He be feared, whence haply ye may prosper.

Gate Eleven of the Eighth Unity

concerning the washing of the body of the deceased three times, which is undertaken in this order: first do thou wash the head, whilst saying “Ya Fard!” (“O Thou the Peerless!”); then the torso, whilst saying “Ya Hayy!” (“O Thou the Living!”); then the right arm, whilst saying “Ya Qayyum!” (“O Thou the Self-Subsisting!”); then the left arm, whilst saying “Ya Hakam!” (“O Thou the Arbiter!”); then the right foot, whilst saying “Ya ’Adl!” (“O Thou the Just!”); and then the left foot, whilst saying “Ya Quddus!” (“O Thou the Holy!”): with water, or with whatsoever he pleaseth of camphor and lotus; and let him be shrouded in five sheets; and let the ring be placed upon his right hand, bearing the inscription, in the case of men “Unto God belongeth all that is in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever is between them, and God, verily, hath knowledge of All Things;” and in the case of women “Unto God belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and God, verily, is potent over All Things.”

The substance of this gate is that all the laws of the Bayan have flowed forth conformably with the mysteries of Divine Unity and understanding, so that if one were to look from the beginning to the end thereof, he would behold the Water of Unity flowing uniformly throughout the whole: wherefore, with respect to washing the body of a deceased person, permission hath been granted for this to be performed at least once, as a matter of obligation; and thereto for it to be performed up to three, or five times: inasmuch as the degrees of the confession of the Unity of God are assigned five levels; namely: “There is no God but Him;” “There is no God but Me;” “There is no God but God,” “There is no God but Thee;” and “There is no God but Him in Whom …:” and had such a person lived at the time of revelation, and become in the first year convinced of the revelation of the Unity of God, assuredly by the Year Five he would have arrived at the final degree of the confession of God’s Unity.

It is for this reason that the washing of the body of the deceased at least once hath been made obligatory: while all will doubtless be able to support it with respect to the four degrees, should there be no attendant hardship.

Permission hath been granted for the washing of the head; the torso; and the arms and legs of the deceased; and let those concerned, whilst performing this task, hold him in remembrance, offering praise and thanksgiving unto God. Whatsoever, during the life of the deceased, would, with respect to the coldness or the hotness of the water, have been the exigency of each particular season – it is now fitting that he be washed in the selfsame manner, by the hands of the righteous; while, after the completion of this task, let them, if such be available, anoint him with rose water, or some other perfume.

Leave hath been granted for the deceased to be shrouded in five sheets, ranging from silk at the highest level down to the coarsest of cotton at the other. It is not permissible for more than nineteen Names to be written thereupon; and as for the Names suitable to this purpose – each person may choose whichsoever he desireth.

Should a little dust from the tomb of the First and the Last be interred with him, this shall become a cause of his not beholding any sadness after death; and of his enjoying, in the Divine Paradise, whatsoever hath been, and is, to him beloved.

Leave hath been granted for a ring to be placed upon his right hand, bearing the inscription, in the case of men “Unto God belongeth all that is in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever is between them, and God, verily, hath knowledge of All Things;” and in the case of women “Unto God belongeth the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatsoever is between them, and God, verily, is potent over All Things.”

The deceased should under all conditions be treated in such a manner that naught but dignity and tranquillity be evinced towards him; inasmuch as the respect paid to the body of a believer is respect paid to the believer himself. Let one, from the beginning unto the end of his transportation to the place of burial, be engaged in reciting, either in his heart or by his tongue, the Six Names, or simply the Name of God.

Know thou that death is even as life. Should the deceased be caused to expire in a state of belief in the Revelation of the age in which he liveth, he shall enjoy the felicity of the Divine Paradise; otherwise He abideth in the Fire. Be thou watchful that the Day of Resurrection befall not, and one be caused to expire, and he go into the Fire, yet advert not to his fate: even as, from the day of the appearance of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – until today, anyone who hath been caused to expire in a state of other than belief in Him hath not entered into Paradise; and likewise, from the beginning of the appearance of the Bayan, if anyone be caused to expire therein, it is the Lord Who layeth hold upon him, through the agency of the angels into whose charge he is committed: and He shall enter Paradise, should he have given proof of his obedience by acting in accordance with whatsoever the Lord hath enjoined in the Bayan; whereas if he be laid hold upon in a state of other than belief in the Bayan, then should he perform the works of both worlds it shall not avail him: and even if, after his death, every charitable endeavour be undertaken on his behalf, still it shall not benefit him: save only if he believe in the Lord and His Verses, and obey his Best-Beloved, in respect of that which He hath sent down in the Bayan: perchance then the mercy of God may reach him, and he may be caused to abide for ever in the Eternal Paradise.

Be thou watchful of the Revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest: for if thou hear thereof, and hesitate for so long as it taketh thee to utter “Yea,” thou art in the Fire, alike whether thou be caused to die, or continue in existence. This is the degree of vigilance which God, on the advent of each Revelation, desireth of every soul. Be thou watchful lest, in the stupefying convulsions of the Day of Resurrection, thou go astray: inasmuch as the stupefying convulsions of that Day are none other but the manifestations of sorrow that befall; and the peerless Verses that are revealed in behalf of the One made manifest in the Revelation; or else they are the beatific breezes blowing from the Morn of Eternity upon the temples of the hearts of all created things: even as, wert thou to look upon this present Revelation, thou wouldst behold them all.

Do thou pay one (Vahid) visit to the dead in the course of each number Vahid. Other matters have been sent down under this head, the which thou shalt erelong behold in the Tablet wherein they are revealed. Say: God causeth you to die through His command; and commandeth the angels to lay hold upon His believing servants.

Just as the angels lay hold upon the spirit of a believer, by the command of the Lord, so too the demons lay hold upon the spirit of other than a believer: so that, should anyone ascend beneath the shadow of the Bayan, it is the exalted angels who lay hold upon his spirit; whereas should anyone be overtaken by death – or any other condition – in other than the Bayan, the angels shall not draw near him: for if a believer will not touch him, how much greater reason hath an angel for refusing to do so? Nay, were the veil to be lifted from the eyes even of the demons, they too would refuse to do so, such is the intensity of the heat of the fire within him: yet, since they are wrapped in a veil, they do lay hold upon his spirit, and entrust it unto the keepers of the Fire.

The spirit of the believer cometh into the presence of God; and conversely the spirit of other than the believer, in his own station – the Lord deigneth not to look upon, but commandeth the Fire “Take him.” Put thy whole trust in the Lord lest death overtake thee, and – for that thou wast not on the right path – thou be not recompensed for the “Lord” whom thou hast worshipped. God counselleth you with regard to your own selves; then to all His servants: that haply ye may show Him befitting reverence.

Gate Twelve of the Eighth Unity: Concerning the decrees of the place of scourging

The substance of this gate is that it behoveth whoever liveth in that land, or up to a distance of sixty-six farsakhs around it – no matter who he be – having completed twenty-nine years of his existence, to visit that place once each year; and to remain upon that land for nineteen days, consecrating himself the while to God. Five rak’ahs of prayer have been prescribed upon that spot. Whoso hath not the means to undertake this observance may act in a similar fashion in his own home. Dwellers of other than these bounds have been exempted therefrom: yet had such exemption not been granted, who would have been able to deviate from the command of God? Behold thou the grace of the True One, and observe by contrast the limit of the people.

God alone knoweth what sums shall be expended in the way of this observance: yet on that day there was not a single soul who would take a single step for the sake of God. In like manner, ye yourselves shall, in the coming Revelation, be similarly afflicted: all of ye shall perform your works, remaining the while shut out as by a veil from recognizing the Source of Command; and all of ye shall bow down for His sake, remaining the while shut out as by a veil from reverencing His person.

Were ye indeed content merely to be shut out as by a veil, these binding precepts would not then become applicable to all: yet now if one person be shut out as by a veil, the whole of creation become, through him, bound by the Divine precepts.

If, on the Day of the appearance of Him Whom God shall make manifest, ye make it your endeavour to believe in God, which is to believe in Him; to obey Him, which is to obey God; to love God, which is to love Him; and to win His good pleasure, which is to win the good pleasure of God, then no command shall be sent down such that ye all – even unto the Day of Resurrection – shall be subject to its doom. Such is the power of God to do what He willeth; such His invincible Will to ordain what He pleaseth. Perchance, on the Day of Resurrection, ye may be watchful of yourselves lest, whilst rebuffing those who, in the present Revelation, are shut out as by a veil, ye yourselves become yet more veiled than they: even as today ye rebuff those who are shut out as by a veil from the Apostle of God, yet have become yourselves more veiled than they.

Fear ye then God as it is meet that he be feared, lest ye accept for anyone other than what ye would accept for your own selves: haply, then, on the Day of Resurrection, ye may not pronounce judgment against God Himself.

Gate Thirteen of the Eighth Unity: Concerning this, that permission is granted to pronounce ninety-five salutations upon the Point in His Former and His Latter Manifestations

The substance of this gate is that since the Tree of Truth hath ever been, and is, the Mirror of God, wherein naught is to be seen but God – for this reason hath it been commanded that at the time of His ascension to the throne of His temple, and His transition from His own former temple, ninety-five times should the salutation “Allah-u-A’zam” (“God is Most Mighty”) be uttered; while on other than these occasions, permission hath not been granted for more than five such salutations: inasmuch as the Letters of the Living are revealed from that innumerate Vahid: while all the degrees of the proliferating numbers – Vahid after Vahid – are revealed from the First Vahid: whence haply, on the Day of Resurrection, at the time of the appearance of the Tree of Truth, hadst thou truly been performing thy works “for God,” thou shalt behold in that Mirror all the Letters of the Living – not in the same manner as thou wouldst behold in the Letters themselves: nay rather, behold therein His sheer unmitigated power to reveal Himself to them with such splendour as to make them into manifestations guiding unto His own Essence – and so likewise all the degrees of the proliferating numbers.

With thy tongue thou sayest “I perform my works for God:” yet on that Day it shall be revealed whether thou wast truthful in thy profession. If, at the time of the revelation of Him Whom God shall make manifest, thou performest thy works for Him, then hadst thou truly been performing them for God; otherwise, hadst thou not been truthful in thy works. Every believer who, on that Day, is deserving of that title, and had truly been performing his works for God, shall perform them for Him: otherwise, his works had been performed for other than God, inasmuch as they fell out not to be for Him. Even as, in the Revelation of the Apostle of God – may the blessings of God and His salutations be upon Him – had any of the Letters of the Evangel truly been acting for God, he would have declared his belief in the Apostle of God; and so soon as this came not to pass, it is a sign that he was not sincere.

Likewise, in the Revelation of the Tree of the Bayan, if there be one who is truly performing his works for God, it is he who now performeth his works for God through following Him; else was he not sincere, for had he been truly sincere, he would not have turned out to be for other than God.

Fear ye then God on the Day of His Revelation, that haply ye may prosper.

Gate Fourteen of the Eighth Unity
